VitiBot's public site describes full autonomy and worker safety benefits but does not disclose the perception stack, so no computer vision or machine learning claim is verified here; treat it as autonomous machinery until the navigation technology is documented. It matters to the wine data landscape as one of the main European sources of in row robotic operating data.

name: Kegshoe
ai_use_case: keg fleet tracking / sales CRM
short_description: Keg tracking and management software plus a sales CRM for breweries: scan-based fills, deliveries, returns and lookups across the keg fleet, with inventory levels and pickup timing. Founded 2015 by Torin Regier and Adrian Pawliszko. Kegshoe makes no public AI or machine-learning claims; it is tracked here as the system of record for keg fleet and account data, not as an AI vendor.

name: Kaspar Schulz
ai_use_case: brewhouse process control / cloud maintenance
short_description: The world's oldest brewing plant manufacturer, ten generations family-owned, building brewhouses, malting systems and distillery plants. Its Pioneer Pro control system is marketed as intelligent process control with innovative automation and cloud-based maintenance management, alongside the web-based SCHULZ app for remote plant control. Kaspar Schulz makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the plant and control layer that brewing process data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Anton Paar
ai_use_case: inline and lab beverage measurement
short_description: Measurement instruments for beverage quality control: the Alcolyzer alcohol meter, CarboQC dissolved-CO2 meter, density meters and modular packaged-beer measurement systems used inline, at-line and in the lab across beer, wine, spirits and RTDs. Over 40 years in beverage analysis. Anton Paar makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the measurement layer that brewery and winery quality data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Meura
ai_use_case: mash filtration and brewhouse technology
short_description: Brewing and distilling process technology, best known for the Meura 2001 thin-bed membrane mash filter, used in production of more than 25 percent of global beer volume; the 500th unit sold in 2023. Founded 1845 by Jean-Baptiste Meura; a Boccard subsidiary since the Boccard family entered the shareholding in 1987. Meura makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as brewhouse process technology, not as an AI vendor.

name: Worter
ai_use_case: brewery ERP / mass-balance recipe engine
short_description: Grain-to-glass brewery management ERP for craft breweries and fermentation businesses: equipment register with auto QR tagging, batch lifecycle records, inventory with PAR and expiry alerts, QC approvals, and a mass-balance based recipe engine that calculates expected COGS as a recipe is built and flags process deviations against recipe intent in real time. Worter Technologies Private Limited, CIN U62013PN2024PTC234801, incorporated 7 October 2024 in Pune; directors Shaju Balakrishnan and Kranti Satyanarayan Mamidpalliwar. Worter makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as an Indian brewery system of record, not as an AI vendor.

name: Praj Industries
ai_use_case: AI-enabled precision fermentation / brewery plant engineering
short_description: Process solutions company for bio-energy, high-purity water and brewery plants, with a brewery division running since 1994, over 70 percent market share in India and installations across Africa and Southeast Asia. In 2025 Praj opened an Advanced Precision Fermentation Lab at its Praj Matrix R&D centre in Pune with a research partnership with BRIC-NCCS, designed to support high-capacity AI-enabled fermentation processes across food, pharma, biofuels and beverages, aimed at reducing scale-up risk and improving process reliability. The AI claim attaches to the fermentation R&D facility, not to the brewery plant product line. Praj's own resources index also lists Remote Bridge, an application for remote monitoring and management of plants, described publicly in terms of higher site availability and reduced downtime; its product page currently returns 404. On public evidence Remote Bridge is plant monitoring and reporting, and carries no AI or machine learning claim of its own.

name: ProLeiT
ai_use_case: brewery process control and MES
short_description: Software manufacturer of the PLC-based process control systems Plant iT and brewmaxx, with MES built in: integrated process visualisation, pre-configured automation objects, ISA-88 compliant batch systems and continuous recipe and materials management, running on Schneider Electric, Siemens and Rockwell controllers. brewmaxx is one of the most widely installed brewery process control systems. Part of Schneider Electric. ProLeiT makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as the process control and MES layer that brewery batch data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Konvoy Kegs
ai_use_case: iot keg fleet tracking
short_description: Konvoy rents, services and tracks kegs for brewers across Australia, New Zealand and the UK, and describes itself as operating the largest IoT tracked keg fleet globally with automated location tracking on every keg and no scanning required. The trackers were built by UnaBiz on the Sigfox 0G network operated by Thinxtra, and report keg location, temperature and usage. Konvoy makes no machine learning claim: the platform is asset telemetry and fleet visibility rather than modelling.

name: BinaryBeer
ai_use_case: smart keg supply chain insights
short_description: BinaryBeer builds KegLink, a low power IoT device that turns a keg into a tracked container reporting location, temperature and beer freshness, plus the Binary Cloud platform that brewers use for fleet maps, alerts and reporting. The company states the platform is "powered by machine learning and AI-driven algorithms" that "continuously refine its insights" for fleet activity and supply chain optimisation, though it does not name the models or specific predictions. Asahi Europe and International selected BinaryBeer for an international smart keg deployment, and the product is also sold in North America through a partnership with Kegshoe.

name: MicroStar Logistics
ai_use_case: shared keg pool logistics
key_people: Michael Hranicka (President and CEO), Bryan Place (President, Kegstar), Harley Green (VP Technology and Customer Experience)
short_description: MicroStar runs the largest shared keg pool in the beer industry on a pay per fill model, so brewers use pooled kegs instead of owning a fleet, and it claims to remove 4.1 million truck miles of empty keg returns a year. Its international arm is Kegstar, which serves brewers in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand and offers a customer platform called TAP. MicroStar makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site: it is a physical keg logistics network with a customer portal, and it is included here because it is the incumbent that owns most of the keg movement data in the sector.

name: KegChek
ai_use_case: keg and draught asset tracking
short_description: KegChek is a keg tracking and fleet management system for breweries, operated by UBC COOL CANADA INC, part of the UBC Group. It tracks kegs by barcode, QR, RFID and Bluetooth scans at each stage of keg rotation and shows location and status on a map, and it extends the same tracking to trade marketing and dispensing assets such as tap handles, jockey boxes, kegerators and patio umbrellas. The product makes no AI or machine learning claim: reporting is standard inventory and status reporting exported to PDF or Excel.

name: Kegtron
ai_use_case: keg level and pour monitoring
short_description: Kegtron makes inline smart keg monitors that sit between the keg and the tap, using a flowmeter and a wireless processor to report how much beer has been dispensed and how much remains, for both home kegerators and multi tap venues. Products are the Kegtron Pro and Gen 1 lines plus SAFECID line cleaners, and the platform adds reporting and an Untappd integration. Kegtron makes no AI or machine learning claim: the value is direct volume measurement and real time reporting.

name: KegSpeed
ai_use_case: cellular smart keg trackers
short_description: KegSpeed sells patented smart trackers that attach to any keg brand and report location and status over cellular and GPS, with embedded sensors for motion, temperature and pressure, aimed at brewers and distributors trying to cut keg loss. It positions itself as an open system with an API that works across keg makers and brewery inventory software rather than a closed fleet. KegSpeed makes no AI or machine learning claim: it refers only to analytics and data insights on top of the tracker feed.

name: KegID
ai_use_case: keg scan tracking and traceability
short_description: KegID is a low cost keg tracking subscription, run by the Hillebrand keg team inside DHL, that lets brewery staff scan kegs with a smartphone camera and see fleet location, keg age and days in circulation. It covers batch traceability and quality control reporting and integrates with the Kegspediter keg management service. Pricing runs from USD 25 a month for 150 kegs to USD 100 a month for 500 or more. KegID makes no AI or machine learning claim: it is barcode scanning plus reporting.

name: TrackAbout
ai_use_case: returnable asset and keg tracking
short_description: TrackAbout, now a Datacor product, is a returnable asset tracking platform whose named verticals include beer kegs alongside industrial gas cylinders and pallets. It covers keg lifecycle visibility, mobile scanning and photo capture at delivery, maintenance and inspection workflow, rental billing calculation and a customer portal showing asset and delivery history. The keg product makes no AI or predictive analytics claim; Datacor markets a separate Datacor AI offering that is not described as part of TrackAbout.

name: eProvenance
ai_use_case: wine cold chain scoring
short_description: eProvenance is a Franco American company that monitors the temperature and shipping conditions of fine wine at container, pallet or case level, using sensors placed in shipments and analysis of the resulting condition data. Its proprietary scientific algorithm converts a shipment temperature history into the eProvenance Score, a 0 to 100 rating of whether the wine stayed fresh or was heat damaged. In 2020 it launched VinAssure, a wine supply chain platform built on IBM Blockchain Transparent Supply. The scoring algorithm is described as scientific and rule based rather than machine learning, and the company makes no explicit ML claim.

name: Hillebrand Gori
ai_use_case: beverage freight and cold chain logistics
short_description: Hillebrand Gori, part of DHL, is the dominant specialist logistics provider for wine, beer and spirits, moving cased and bulk beverage by sea, rail, road and air, including temperature controlled transport, flexitanks, ISO tanks, warehousing and a control tower service. Its digital layer is the myHillebrandGori platform for shipment booking and tracking plus a carbon calculator that compares emissions across shipping scenarios, and it also runs the KegID keg tracking product. It makes no AI or machine learning claim, and is included because it sits on more beverage supply chain movement data than any pure software vendor in this surface.

name: Cellr
ai_use_case: serialised bottle track and trace
short_description: Cellr gives wine and spirits producers serialised QR codes and NFC or RFID enabled lids and labels applied on the bottling line, creating a per bottle digital identity used for anti counterfeit verification, track and trace, digital product passport compliance and direct to consumer engagement. Brand dashboards report scan, claim and conversion analytics, with published customer results such as Red Hill Estate averaging 250 bottles claimed per month. Cellr makes no AI or machine learning claim: the platform is serialisation, authentication and engagement reporting.

name: Waterplan
ai_use_case: water risk and replenishment modelling
key_people: Jose Ignacio Galindo (Co-founder and CEO), Nicolas Wertheimer (Co-founder)
short_description: Waterplan is a water risk platform that combines a site's operational data with hydrological models and satellite remote sensing to quantify water risk in financial terms and validate volumetric water benefits from replenishment projects. Its own case study covers Ambev, the AB InBev brewing subsidiary in South America, which uses the platform to measure and validate watershed and restoration projects in three high water risk basins and to auto-generate the evidence log for sustainability reporting. The company describes itself as an AI native platform and cites AI agents for data collection and anomaly detection in resource use; the substantive modelling described is hydrological plus remote sensing rather than a named ML model. Y Combinator Summer 2021.

name: Zevero
ai_use_case: automated scope 3 emission factor matching
short_description: Zevero is a carbon accounting and ESG reporting platform that measures scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions and produces CSRD, SECR and CDP disclosures. It has an unusually deep drinks customer base and names Northern Monk, DEYA Brewing, Stroud Brewery, Brixton Brewery, JUBEL Beer, Yakima Chief Hops, Asahi and the sake producers Suigei and Manotsuru on its own site. The AI claim is specific and modest: AI driven emission factor matching and document extraction that reads uploaded invoices and utility documents in multiple languages, applied to fermentation related scope 3 lines. It integrates with BrewMan brewery management software so purchase and delivery data flows in automatically.

name: ClimateHound
ai_use_case: carbon footprint accounting for drinks producers
short_description: ClimateHound is a carbon footprint and decarbonisation reporting platform aimed squarely at small and mid sized drinks producers. Its winery page names customers including pleb urban winery, Wanderlust Wine Co, Cellarest, Old Elk Distillery, Montanya Distillers, 3BR Distillery and Bauman's Cider, and it pulls data through more than 200 integrations with business tools and utility providers. It makes no machine learning claim anywhere on the site: this is integration driven emissions accounting and reporting, not modelling. Included because it is one of the few carbon platforms with a genuinely wine and spirits native customer list.

name: Cambrian Innovation
ai_use_case: remote monitoring of brewery wastewater treatment
short_description: Cambrian Innovation is an MIT spinout that treats brewery and winery effluent on site with bioelectrically enhanced anaerobic systems, EcoVolt and BlueCycle MBR, recovering biogas and reuse water, and sells it as a Water Energy Purchase Agreement so the producer puts up no capital. Its own site names Anheuser Busch Houston, Russian River Brewing, Bear Republic Brewing, Northern United Brewing and Rombauer Vineyards as customers, and Lagunitas in Petaluma has run an EcoVolt system since 2014 under a ten year operations agreement. The digital layer is cloud based real time monitoring and analytics of reactor operation; the company makes no machine learning claim. Relevant to the water stewardship and effluent side of beverage ESG.

name: Aquacycl
ai_use_case: remote real time control of modular wastewater reactors
short_description: Aquacycl treats ultra high strength food and beverage wastewater at source with BETT, a modular bioelectrochemical reactor using electrochemically active bacteria, avoiding dilution and cutting sludge. Every reactor is remotely monitored and controlled in real time from Aquacycl, which removes the need for a full time onsite operator, and probe data is used to read microbial colony health. Its own brewery case study documents 99 percent BOD and 85 percent TSS removal at Joshua Tree Brewery, and PepsiCo is named on the site; the company has also worked through AB InBev's 100+ Accelerator. No machine learning claim is made: this is instrumented process control, not modelling.

name: Zero Carbon Forum
ai_use_case: sector carbon benchmarking and reduction roadmaps
key_people: Mark Chapman (Founder and CEO), Bob Gordon (Director)
short_description: Zero Carbon Forum is a not for profit collaborative representing over a third of the UK brewing and hospitality sector across roughly 35,000 sites, providing carbon footprinting, benchmarking, sector roadmaps and carbon coaching rather than software. Named brewer members include Adnams, St Austell Brewery, Gipsy Hill Brewing, Thornbridge Brewery, Stewart Brewing and Wells and Co, with BrewDog, Fuller's, Greene King, Marston's, Shepherd Neame and Young's cited in trade coverage of the membership. It launched a brewing sector specific decarbonisation roadmap in 2022 and partners with Mondra for product level carbon data. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; it matters here because it is where a large slice of UK brewing emissions data is actually pooled and benchmarked.

name: Provenate
ai_use_case: chat assistant over distillery production and duty data
short_description: Provenate is an all in one production, stock, duty and compliance system built specifically for whisky distilleries and bottlers, replacing spreadsheets and manual HMRC duty returns and holding a full audit trail from wash to spirit yield and cask. It names Ardnamurchan Distillery and Adelphi Distillery as customers; Ardnamurchan uses it to digitise its operational flow and to back consumer facing provenance claims, including sourcing and climate impact of the liquid, via a bottle QR code. The only AI in the product is an assistant that lets staff query their own cask stock and duty data in natural language; there is no carbon accounting or LCA engine, so treat this as a system of record with a provenance and reporting layer.

name: NIRAS
ai_use_case: brewery discrete event simulation and digital twin, plus industry benchmarking
short_description: Danish independent engineering consultancy with a named brewing and distilling practice covering process design, mashing and fermentation engineering, water treatment, automation and full project delivery. It runs the NIRAS Brewing Benchmark Club (NBBC), a global beer and beverage benchmarking dataset members can explore across regions and plant sizes, and sells Opti-Brew, a modelling tool that analyses production efficiency and finds process bottlenecks for expansion planning. Its Virtual Brewery offering is 3D discrete event simulation that becomes a digital twin when wired into plant MES, SCADA, PLC and IoT data. NIRAS makes no machine learning claim: the modelling described is deterministic simulation, not statistical learning.

name: Briggs of Burton
ai_use_case: no ai claim; process engineering design and build for breweries and distilleries
short_description: Process engineering contractor tracing its history to 1732, now part of the CLPT Group, designing brewhouses, cold block equipment, stills, ageing and blending processes for brewers and distillers. Named work includes Scotch whisky producers and a Mexican tequila plant running 140,000 litres per day, and it markets a combined BrewStillery technology. Services run from feasibility study through project management and commissioning. Its own site makes no artificial intelligence, machine learning or data analytics claim; it is included as an engineering layer that shapes what beverage plant data exists at all.

name: Seeq
ai_use_case: self service time series analytics and golden batch profiling on brewery process historian data
short_description: Industrial advanced analytics vendor that sits on top of process historians such as OSIsoft PI and lets process engineers cleanse, contextualise and model time series data without a data science team. Its own resource library carries a brewery use case in which engineers built a reference profile from five historically good batches, then used average plus and minus three standard deviation boundaries to flag temperature deviations during the diacetyl rest, giving early warning on batch quality when offline diacetyl results lag. The brewery case is statistical boundary monitoring rather than machine learning, though the wider platform also offers ML tooling on the same data. Seeq is a cross industry vendor, not a beverage specialist.

name: TrendMiner
ai_use_case: self service industrial time series analytics and anomaly monitoring for process plants
short_description: Belgian self service industrial analytics platform for continuous and batch process industries, offering search over historian time series, data contextualisation into events, 24/7 monitoring with alerts and, more recently, agentic AI and an Analytics Agent. Its food and beverage page covers compliance and CIP optimisation, OEE and resource efficiency, and taste and texture consistency. Named reference customers on that page are Nestle, Avebe and CP Kelco; beers and spirits are listed as coming soon, so there is no verified brewery or distillery customer yet. Included as part of the historian analytics layer that beverage plants buy, not as a proven drinks deployment.

name: Dennis Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim; food and beverage plant design build with automation and controls data integration
short_description: Design build firm working exclusively for the food and beverage industry, ranked the largest food and beverage design firm by Engineering News Record since 2015, covering process design, controls and automation and system integration. Its beverage market page lists beer and distilled spirits among its categories, with Boston Beer named as a client on an 880,000 square foot facility. One case study describes a data driven beverage facility where building management systems were integrated with process controls to generate more actionable operating data. No simulation, digital twin or machine learning product is claimed on its own site.

name: Alfa Laval
ai_use_case: iot condition monitoring and root cause analytics on brewery and beverage process equipment
short_description: Swedish process equipment maker supplying heat exchangers, separators, decanters, pumps and valves into breweries and beverage plants, with a hygienic processing product line covered by the brewing trade press. Its digital layer is CM Connect, a subscription condition monitor and 4G cloud gateway linking up to ten wireless vibration monitors, and Clariot, a sensor plus gateway plus analytics package that reports vibration, temperature and run time and returns root cause recommendations for process, installation and mechanical faults before breakdown. The published beverage reference is a Britvic bottling plant, and the site does not disclose the algorithms, so the analytics should not be read as a machine learning claim. In November 2025 Alfa Laval announced work on AI assisted heat exchanger service diagnostics.

name: Pellenc (Pera-Pellenc)
ai_use_case: connected winery press and cellar telemetry
short_description: Pellenc, through its Pera-Oenoprocess winery division, builds pneumatic presses, destemmers and cellar process equipment for wineries. Its named digital product P-Connect transmits real-time pressing data to a smartphone or PC (press state, time remaining, programme number, phase number, and juice volume in hectolitres with EasyPress 2), sends SMS alerts on cycle end and press faults, and supports remote diagnostics for after-sales assistance. The wider Pellenc Connect platform visualises machine, agronomic and oenological data from vineyard to winery. No AI or predictive maintenance claim is made.

name: BrauKon
ai_use_case: brewhouse process automation and recipe control
short_description: BrauKon is a Bavarian brewhouse and brewery plant OEM serving craft and mid-size breweries. It ships two named control products: BrauControl, a full brewery process automation system covering malt intake through to bright beer tank and CIP, with 60 recipe positions of 30 steps each, weekly brew scheduling, a brewing log and remote maintenance over a network connection, built almost entirely on Siemens components; and BrauKon TControl for brewhouse steps such as mashing, lautering and wort boiling, also available with remote maintenance. BrauControl includes self-optimising fuzzy logic lautering control that adjusts rake height, pump speed and sparging, which is classical control engineering and not machine learning. BrauKon makes no AI claim.

name: Orise
ai_use_case: anomaly detection and asset health monitoring on brewery production lines
short_description: Orise is a German industrial automation, digitalisation and optimisation firm that absorbed the brewery engineering expertise of Rolec Prozess- und Brautechnik as Rolec winds down through liquidation in 2026, and now sells a Brewery Optimization Services line. Its named digital products include Performance Monitor, Lean Shopfloor Manager, Asset Health Monitoring, and a Manufacturing AI line covering Anomaly Detection, Micro-Stop Detection and custom AI solutions. Orise states plainly that this was a transfer of people and know-how, not an acquisition of the Rolec business. The AI claim sits in the Manufacturing AI product line rather than in the brewery process control itself.

name: Parsec
ai_use_case: algorithmic fermentation kinetics control and nutrient dosing
short_description: Parsec builds automation and control systems for wineries, covering micro-oxygenation, fermentation control, selective extraction and real-time monitoring, with patented technology installed in more than 30 countries. Its named products are the SAEn5000 monitoring and vinification automation platform, ADCF (dynamic analysis of fermentation kinetics), which measures CO2 output continuously to track sugar consumption and flag slowdowns or stuck fermentations, EVO2FERM, which adapts yeast nutrient additions in real time, and Aphromate for sparkling wine prise de mousse. Parsec describes these as intelligent algorithms developed experimentally; there is no machine learning claim. Parsec is being acquired by Enartis.

name: Wine Technology Incorporated (VinWizard)
ai_use_case: winery tank and cellar process control
short_description: Wine Technology Incorporated sells VinWizard, a winery automation, monitoring and control system used by over 200 wineries, with a second base in Marlborough, New Zealand. It controls tank temperature, automated pumpovers, air injection, headspace gassing and agitators, reads in-tank sensors for temperature stratification, brix and redox, and extends to chillers, barrel and case goods rooms, CO2, water and power. Its IOWIZ-4 and IOWIZ-16 IO controllers have been built in-house since 2016, and CellarView is a browser-based digital tank board. Alerts go out by email or SMS when tanks drift out of range. No AI or machine learning claim is made.

name: CARL GmbH
ai_use_case: distilling process control and automatic fractionation
short_description: CARL GmbH, the Christian Carl still works founded in 1869, builds pot stills and distillation plants for craft and commercial distilleries worldwide. Its named control products are DPC 510 (Distilling Process Control), a 20 inch touchscreen system regulating heating and cooling, temperature monitoring, safety interlocks and automatic fractionation with recipe management; the compact DPC 200/210 TOUCH with optional remote access for retrofitting older CARL stills; CADi (Computer Aided Distilling) with integrated flow and alcohol measurement for fully automatic runs; and DPC 50, a calculator that works out dilution water and duty. CARL makes no AI or machine learning claim; this is recipe-driven process control and the origin point of distillery process data.

name: ABE Beverage Equipment (American Beer Equipment)
ai_use_case: brewhouse assisted brewing automation
short_description: ABE Beverage Equipment, formerly American Beer Equipment and a division of Norland International, builds brewhouses, fermentation, grain handling and canning lines for craft breweries. Its named control offering is the Brewhouse Automation Plus assisted brewing package, standard on new brewhouses, which automates liquor blending, vorlauf and wort grant, sparge control, lauter to kettle and whirlpool transfers, knockout to fermenter at a regulated pitch temperature, and liquor tank management with volumetric auto-stop and remote viewing and control. BrewPilot is its entry-level system for nano and brewpub scale. ABE deliberately uses off-the-shelf automation components and makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: ZoomAgri
ai_use_case: computer vision barley varietal purity and grain quality grading
total_raised: USD 9.3 million (USD 3.3 million Series A plus a USD 6 million round backed by GrainCorp)
short_description: ZoomAgri sells scanner devices plus software that identify barley varieties and grade physical grain quality from images, described on its own site as computer vision and machine learning delivered as vision as a service. Malting barley is a core commodity: the site cites MEBAK approval for barley varietal purity and Syndicat de Paris and Bipea testing for malting barley. Grain Trade Australia endorsed ZoomAgri One for varietal purity assessment in the Barley Trading Standards from the 2026-27 crop year, and GrainCorp has bought more than 40 devices for its east coast sites and ports. This is the clearest verified machine learning claim on the malt and barley raw material layer.

name: Fermentis
ai_use_case: machine learning prediction of yeast contribution to beer aroma
short_description: Fermentis is the beverage fermentation arm of Lesaffre, selling active dry yeasts, bacteria and fermentation aids to brewers, winemakers, distillers, cider makers and mead makers under the SafBrew, SafOeno and SafSpirit lines. Its own corporate news reports a Sensory Machine Learning project run by Fermentis Academy with Lesaffre Group R&D that trained models on analytical and sensory datasets to explore and predict how yeast strains shape the aromatic profiles of beer, and which won an award at Lesaffre's first Digital, Data and Tech awards. The work is presented as an internal R&D project rather than a product brewers can buy today.

name: Berkeley Yeast
ai_use_case: synthetic biology strain engineering for flavour, no machine learning claim
key_people: Charles Denby (Co-founder), Nick Harris (Co-founder), Rachel Li (Co-founder)
short_description: Berkeley Yeast is a UC Berkeley spinout that uses synthetic biology to engineer brewing and wine yeast strains, selling FRESH low diacetyl strains, TROPICS and SUPERBLOOM thiol releasing strains for hop-like aroma, SUMMERSTONE, the GALACTIC souring strain and non-alcoholic beer strains in dry and liquid formats. It was co-founded by Charles Denby, Nick Harris and Rachel Li with UC Berkeley professor Jay Keasling as key inventor, and is funded by NSF, NIH and USDA grants plus venture capital. Its own website makes no machine learning claim: the AI angle in press coverage belongs to a separate Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory project using the ART Bayesian recommendation tool to tune hop-flavour metabolite production, which does not name the company. Included as the flagship engineered-strain supplier on the ingredient layer, with the AI claim explicitly not attributed to it.

name: Renaissance BioScience
ai_use_case: ai assisted wild yeast strain discovery from genomic and phenotypic data
total_raised: CAD 550,000 GeneSolve grant from Genome BC for this project
key_people: John Husnik (Co-CEO and Chief Scientific Officer)
short_description: Renaissance BioScience is a Vancouver yeast bioengineering company whose Food and Beverages solutions cover wine, cider, beer and distilled spirits. In February 2026 it announced a 24 month, 550,000 dollar Genome BC GeneSolve project with Dr Vivien Measday at the University of British Columbia to build a proprietary wild yeast discovery platform, characterising more than 700 natural strains and combining metagenomics with AI to identify commercially valuable traits faster than conventional screening. The announced commercial focus of the platform is waste valorisation and industrial compounds, not brewing or wine, so the AI work is adjacent to beverage rather than aimed at it today.

name: Hopsteiner
ai_use_case: genomics assisted hop breeding, no machine learning claim
key_people: Martin Biendl (Head of Research and Development and Analytics)
short_description: Hopsteiner, trading as Simon H. Steiner Hopfen GmbH, is a sixth generation global hop supplier of varieties, pellets and extracts, founded in 1845 and headquartered in Mainburg, Germany with US operations. Its research and development function under Dr Martin Biendl runs a breeding program for drought, heat and pest tolerant cultivars and novel flavour profiles, with partners including the Fraunhofer Institute and the Technical University of Munich, and the company has published chromosome-scale haplotype-resolved hop genome assemblies to support genomics-assisted breeding. Its own R and D pages make no machine learning or AI claim: the work described is genomics and conventional breeding science. Included because the hop breeding layer is otherwise absent from the database.

name: BrewMan by Premier Systems
short_description: Premier Systems sells BrewMan, a cloud brewery and distillery management system used by over 300 producers globally, covering production and fluid movements, raw material traceability, cask and container tracking, dray planning and distribution, CRM, inventory and automatic UK alcohol duty calculation with audit reports. Variants are marketed for distilleries and wineries as well as breweries. The product is a system of record: nothing on the vendor site claims machine learning, and the only forward-looking feature is a rules-based forecast of stock required for upcoming production.

name: Bevica
short_description: Bevica is a UK drinks-industry ERP built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and delivered by TVision, serving breweries, distilleries, wineries, fine wine merchants and drinks distributors. It covers finance and KPI reporting, duty management, HMRC bonded warehousing, inventory, supply chain, production and CRM, plus fine wine specifics such as En Primeur, broking, allocations and cellarage. Its own website makes no machine learning claim; the company describes the platform on LinkedIn as having 'built-in AI as standard', which appears to mean inherited Microsoft Business Central and Power Platform capability rather than any drinks-specific model of its own.

name: Wherefour
ai_use_case: llm assistant that drafts quality-control test definitions
short_description: Wherefour is a manufacturing ERP and lot-traceability platform with a dedicated breweries and distilleries vertical, covering inventory, production runs and formulas, MRP, purchasing, warehouse management, costing and recall readiness. It has US and Canadian offices in Petaluma, California and Toronto, and is SOC 2 audited. The only AI in the product is a built-in assistant in the compliance module that drafts QA test definitions and control points from scratch; the forecasting and MRP features are described as lead-time and reorder-point logic, not machine learning.

name: Process2Wine (Ertus Group)
ai_use_case: machine learning for production cost reduction and environmental footprint in viticulture
short_description: Process2Wine is a SaaS vineyard and cellar management platform from Ertus Group, a Bordeaux company formed in 2016 by the merger of the Ertus Consulting wine consultancy and the D2E software house, with offices in Bordeaux, Montpellier, Reims and Santa Barbara. It handles vineyard work orders, plot mapping, tank and cellar operations, packaging and traceability reporting for wineries, cooperatives, Champagne houses and negociants. Ertus states it is a pioneer in applying machine learning to viticulture and that its Exapta decision-support module, developed with INRIA and supported by BPI Aquitaine and the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, targets production cost reduction and environmental footprint calculation. The core Process2Wine product itself is a traceability and production system of record; the ML sits in the adjacent Exapta module and no model detail or performance figure is published.

name: vinSUITE
ai_use_case: wine club member churn prediction
short_description: vinSUITE is a direct-to-consumer winery platform covering wine club management, tasting room POS, ecommerce, CRM and payments, claiming over 200,000 wine club members supported and more than 2 billion dollars in annual DTC sales processed. Its vinSIGHT analytics module is the AI component: a churn model that scores which club members are about to cancel using signals such as skipped shipments, fewer visits and declining engagement, then surfaces a weekly at-risk list with recommended actions. The company advertises 94 percent prediction confidence and positions the churn model as the one thing competing DTC platforms do not offer; the confidence figure is a vendor claim with no published methodology.

name: Orion Wine Software
short_description: Orion Wine Software sells two winery systems: Orion Cloud for wholesale sales, case goods inventory, depletion tracking and compliance reporting, and WiPS for winemaking production covering grape intake, trial blends, work orders and cost tracking. It targets larger enterprise wineries, importers and multi-brand producers that need TTB compliance and combined wholesale plus production visibility. The company markets 'data-driven decisions' and real-time insight but makes no machine learning claim anywhere on its site; the analytics are reporting and dashboards, including a recently launched Orion Scorecard.

name: VinNOW
short_description: VinNOW is winery management software originally built by a winery for its own use, covering tasting room and web point of sale, wine club processing with automated credit card billing, multi-location inventory, CRM, accounting, compliance and shipping label generation for UPS, FedEx and GLS. It integrates with QuickBooks, VinoShipper and ShipCompliant and runs either on local machines or in the cloud. It is a plain system of record with reporting; there is no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on the site.

name: Brewers Dashboard
short_description: Brewers Dashboard is a brewery data acquisition, automation and visualisation product built on a full SCADA software suite, sold to breweries from nano scale to large distributed facilities. It provides fermentation and brite tank temperature control, brewhouse monitoring and step mash programming, tank level, glycol, chiller and boiler monitoring, alarming to phones, and batch reports combining live temperature traces with laboratory results against the recipe. It is supplied by Infinite Automation Systems, which also does custom PLC and integration work. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; this is deterministic process control and reporting.

name: Breww
ai_use_case: brewery management software
short_description: Cloud brewery management software covering production, sales and CRM, distribution, container tracking, a private online trade store and reporting, used by over 800 breweries. Built in the UK with explicit support for the Indian Rupee and local-language invoicing. BREWW LTD, incorporated 2018, Harpenden. Breww makes no public AI or machine-learning claim; it is tracked here as a brewery system of record, not as an AI vendor.

name: Peritos Solutions
ai_use_case: wine label recognition and provenance enrichment on aws
short_description: Peritos Solutions is a cloud, data and AI consultancy operating across India, New Zealand, Australia and the United States, and an AWS partner. For Wine-Searcher it built an AI label assist pipeline: a custom CNN trained on more than 500,000 labelled wine label images hosted on an Amazon SageMaker real-time endpoint, Amazon Textract OCR to structure label text into JSON, and RAG-grounded provenance summaries generated with Amazon Bedrock against a wine knowledge base indexed in OpenSearch. Its own case page claims 94 percent label identification accuracy, enrichment of over 8 million wine listings, and a drop from 15 to 20 minutes of manual research per SKU to under 2 seconds. AWS separately published a Wine-Searcher and Peritos success story in August 2025 covering the wider AWS platform work.

name: AgroSense
ai_use_case: irrigation decision support for vineyards
short_description: AgroSense is a Mendoza-based agtech platform that combines soil IoT sensors, weather data and satellite imagery to tell irrigated growers how much water to apply and when. Vineyards are a core customer segment, with published deployments at a 70 hectare operation in Rivadavia, Mendoza and a 700 hectare estate including vineyards in Valle de Pedernal, San Juan. The product includes an AI assistant delivered over WhatsApp, currently marked beta, that answers irrigation questions by text or voice against the grower's own field data. The company does not describe the underlying models, so the AI claim is a conversational assistant layered on sensor and satellite analytics rather than a documented machine learning system.

name: Last Call Analytics
ai_use_case: retail sales analytics for beverage alcohol
short_description: Last Call Analytics turns store-level retail and distributor sales data into dashboards for beverage alcohol producers, agencies, distributors and industry associations in Canada and the United States. It covers performance benchmarking, competitor comparison, distribution gap detection and inventory visibility, with published case studies including Social Lite Vodka and Bruce Ashley Group. Its site describes an Assisted Insight Engine that flags declining SKUs, underperforming stores and distribution gaps, but it makes no explicit machine learning claim, so this reads as rules-driven exception reporting rather than a predictive model. It was acquired by cannabis software company Ample Organics in January 2019 and continues to operate under its own brand.

name: Bump Williams Consulting
ai_use_case: beverage alcohol category analytics and shopper insights consulting
key_people: Bump Williams (Founder and CEO), Dave Williams (President), Dan Wandel (VP, Chief Strategy Officer)
short_description: Bump Williams Consulting is a beverage alcohol consultancy working across suppliers, distributors and retailers on executive strategy, organisational design, national accounts and class of trade planning. Its analytics practice is built on syndicated scan data and its team came out of AC Nielsen and Information Resources, and it publishes a widely cited monthly beer and flavoured alcohol category read through Brewbound. It sells no AI or machine learning product and makes no such claim, so it belongs in the beverage data landscape as a human analytics practice sitting on top of syndicated retail measurement. Leadership is Bump Williams as founder and CEO, Dave Williams as president and Dan Wandel as chief strategy officer.

name: Bodega Anaia
hq_location: Agrelo, Lujan de Cuyo, Mendoza, Argentina
ai_use_case: connected vineyard sensing and precision viticulture
short_description: Bodega Anaia is a 72 hectare winery and wine tourism estate in Agrelo, Lujan de Cuyo, Mendoza. Argentine business press describes it as one of the most advanced connected vineyard implementations in the region: IoT sensors reading soil moisture, temperature and mineral presence, transmitted over LoRa to the cloud and controlled from a mobile app, combined with satellite monitoring to detect small variations in soil composition and target water and fertiliser per block. The winery's own website covers the estate, wines and lodge only and makes no technology, sensor or AI claim, so the sensing programme is established from press reporting rather than from the operator itself. There is no machine learning claim anywhere in the evidence; this is instrumentation and precision agriculture.

name: Grist Analytics
ai_use_case: brewery production and quality analytics using statistical process control
short_description: Production and quality analytics software for breweries, deliberately positioned as not an ERP. It covers brew deck data capture, automated brewhouse calculations, real time fermentation analytics, yeast tracking, quality data management and cellar scheduling, and it integrates with the Brew Ninja brewery management system. The published method is classical statistical process control, control charts, standard deviations and process capability, not machine learning. Grist makes no machine learning claim on its own site and this is a plain statistics and analytics product.

name: AnyRoad
ai_use_case: taproom and tasting room experience analytics with AI feedback analysis
key_people: Jonathan Yaffe (Co-founder and CEO), Daniel Yaffe (Co-founder and COO)
short_description: Experience relationship management platform that runs booking, ticketing, payments and first party data capture for brand experiences, with tours and tastings and bottle clubs as named use cases. Alcohol customers listed on the site include Diageo, Pernod Ricard, Campari, Johnnie Walker and Budweiser, so it sits squarely in brewery, distillery and winery DTC. The AI is described as AI powered analysis that turns guest feedback and journey signals into themes and connects them to NPS and brand affinity. No model detail is published. Raised 47 million US dollars in a Series B led by BlackRock with a16z and Runa Capital participating, roughly 66 million US dollars total.

name: Brew Ninja
ai_use_case: brewery production, sales and keg management system of record
short_description: Canadian brewery management software covering production scheduling, inventory, sales and distribution, keg tracking, compliance and payments, with QuickBooks Online and Square integrations. Named brewery customers include Rebellion Brewing, Pile O Bones Brewing and Split Rail Brewing. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site and is a straight system of record. It is included because it is the integration partner that feeds production data into Grist Analytics, so it matters to the beer data landscape.

name: Graine
ai_use_case: taproom and tasting room point of sale and member analytics
short_description: Point of sale and commerce platform built specifically for breweries and wineries, covering taproom and tasting room POS, mobile order and pay, online ordering, reservations, wine and beer club subscription automation, loyalty and inventory costing. It is powered by the payments company Shift4. Graine makes no AI or machine learning claim on its brewery and winery page. It is included as a taproom system of record that owns the transaction and membership data other analytics tools depend on.

name: BeveragePro AI
ai_use_case: AIoT monitoring of brewhouse, fermentation and keg assets
short_description: AIoT platform for beverage production plants covering brewhouse processing, fermentation management, blending, filtration, filling, canning, packaging and distribution. Breweries are the lead named segment, alongside soft drinks, water, juice, dairy and RTD, but not wine or spirits. The bulk of what is described is sensing rather than modelling: RFID and BLE for workforce and asset location, industrial sensors for fermentation temperature, tank level and humidity, GPS for tankers, over LoRaWAN and cellular. AI is claimed only in general terms as predictive analytics and AI forecasting models for consumption rates and equipment failure patterns, with no model detail given. Developed inside Aperture Venture Studio with support from GAO.

name: Gray
ai_use_case: no ai claim; distillery engineering, automation and controls with historian delivery
short_description: Gray is a design build engineering and construction firm with an explicitly named distillery practice covering process systems, refrigeration, architecture, equipment fabrication and automation and controls. Named distillery projects include the Buffalo Trace mash house, Castle and Key and the Diageo Lebanon distillery. Its automation arm Gray AES, based in Lexington, delivered the Ignition SCADA and tag historian system that replaced FactoryTalk at Castle and Key, building it with DevOps practice on GitHub and Docker. Gray makes no machine learning claim for this work; it is the engineering and controls layer that determines what distillery process data exists in the first place.

name: Haskell
ai_use_case: no ml claim; digital twin simulation and production data modelling for drinks plants
short_description: Haskell is a design build engineering firm whose published drinks projects span all three verticals: Anheuser-Busch, the SweetWater brewery expansion, Bently Heritage distillery and Constellation boxed wine manufacturing. Its manufacturing systems group sells system analytics and modelling, meaning digital twins of a facility, system capacity and material flow analysis run off a plant's own production output data, and virtual commissioning of PLC and HMI control systems against 3D models before installation. The analytics described are deterministic simulation and capacity modelling, not learned models, and Haskell claims no machine learning on that service page.

name: Inductive Automation (Ignition)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; scada and tag historian as the distillery process data layer
short_description: Inductive Automation makes Ignition, an unlimited licence SCADA and industrial application platform whose Tag Historian module is the plant data layer in many food and drink sites. Its published distillery case study covers Castle and Key in Frankfort, Kentucky, which replaced an ageing FactoryTalk system with Ignition Perspective across 27,505 tags, 62 of them historised, and 736 alarms, delivered by the integrator Gray AES on iPads for mobile operation. The distillery states it uses the historical record to tie product quality back to process data. The case study makes no AI or machine learning claim; the stated value is mobile HMI, alarming and access to history.

name: Grantek Systems Integration
ai_use_case: no ai claim; brewery mes, process historian and oee integration
short_description: Grantek is a food and beverage focused systems integrator of over 150 engineers across nine North American offices plus India, working on process design, packaging automation, MES and ERP integration, process historians, statistical process control, OEE and downtime measurement, vision and label verification, and IIoT and cloud data enablement. MillerCoors is named on its food and beverage page alongside Agropur and Tassimo. Note for the record: a previous sweep on 2026-08-01 rejected Grantek as having no named brewery; the MillerCoors reference on its own industry page is the new evidence. No AI or machine learning capability is claimed anywhere on those pages.

name: COPA-DATA (zenon)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; brewery scada, isa 88 batch recipe and energy data platform
short_description: COPA-DATA makes zenon, an independent SCADA and industrial software platform with a dedicated brewery automation practice covering ISA 88 batch control, recipe management for new brewing procedures, energy data collection and analysis, and central monitoring of filling and packaging lines. Its food and beverage pages describe deployments from small breweries to global players, including a large German brewery kept running on older applications through zenon's backward compatibility, and a herbal liqueur producer, but name no brewery customer directly. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim for the brewing solution.

name: Factry
ai_use_case: no ai claim; open process historian and mes for fermentation plants
short_description: Factry sells Factry Historian, a time series historian that collects and structures real time process data, and FactryOS, a web based MES for production execution, downtime tracking and order management. It markets itself directly against legacy historians including the PI System. Its named food and beverage customers are fermentation adjacent rather than brewers, notably the brewing and baking yeast producers Lesaffre and Algist Bruggeman, plus Agristo, Puratos and Jacques Ijs. Factry also ran Factry Historian against a real 40 hL beer lot brewed on its behalf and published the fermentation temperature, density, pH and CO2 saturation trends. A previous sweep on 2026-08-01 rejected Factry for having no brewing tie; that brewing lot and its published dashboards are the new evidence. There is no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on the site.

name: Bucher Vaslin
ai_use_case: connected press monitoring and remote fault finding
short_description: Bucher Vaslin is a French winery plant OEM best known for its Bucher XPlus and XPert pneumatic grape presses, and part of the Swiss Bucher Industries group. Its presses ship with Winect, a smartphone application that shows the pressing programme in progress, time remaining, pressure and flow rate, plus configurable email and SMS alerts for events such as end of pressing, juice selection and press stop, and a remote assistance path so a technician can fault find without a site visit. Operating data is uploaded to a Bucher cloud through the company Connect portal for follow up and anomaly notification. Bucher Vaslin makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is connected telemetry and remote service, and it matters because it is where a large share of primary winemaking process data originates.

name: Arnold Holstein
ai_use_case: automated still control and fraction data acquisition
short_description: Arnold Holstein GmbH is a German still maker in Markdorf whose pot and fruit stills are used by distillers worldwide. Its automation option is an in-house control system operated from a stainless housed touch screen on the unit, regulating heating and distilling speed, dephlegmator target temperature, the separation of heads, hearts and tails, product pre-selection by fruit type and the rinsing cycle, with parameters saved and recalled for repeat batches. It also performs digital data acquisition of the concentrations and quantities of each fraction and offers connection to existing data acquisition systems. There is no named software brand, no remote access and no AI or machine learning claim anywhere in the offering: this is the plant layer that distillery process data comes from.

name: Diemme Enologia
ai_use_case: remote machine monitoring and alarm diagnostics
short_description: Diemme Enologia is an Italian winery equipment maker in Lugo, Ravenna, active since the 1920s and known for membrane presses and grape processing plant. It ships the Dme1923 app, a cloud connected mobile client that lets a winery watch its Diemme machines in real time, receive push notifications on work sequences, alerts and alarms, read the diagnostic section and alarm report, and act on process parameters of the running sequence within safety limits. Different users at the same winery can register the same machines and receive differentiated notifications, and a VPN remote connection is an optional paid extra currently limited to membrane presses with the E-Panel. Diemme makes no AI or machine learning claim; this is connected monitoring and remote service.

name: CFT Group
ai_use_case: line performance monitoring and remote predictive maintenance
short_description: CFT Group is an Italian food and beverage plant OEM in Parma that supplies complete bottling, canning and kegging lines for beer, spirits, ready to drink, juice and water, and which owns the brewing engineering house Rolec and the kegging specialist Comac. It offers three named HMI and monitoring platforms, Memento, Illuminate and FACTS, for tracking machine and line performance, and sells remote support and predictive maintenance as part of its service package. CFT publishes no AI or machine learning claim behind these platforms, so they should be read as line data capture and condition based service rather than modelling. It is relevant to the radar as the packaging and brewhouse plant layer that beverage line data originates from.

name: Vapour
short_description: Vapour is a cloud SaaS platform for spirit producers, warehouse operators, cask managers and bottlers, covering distillation, maturation and bottling end to end. Modules include production, maturation and a bottling add-on, with a 3D warehouse view, cask-by-cask loss analysis, auto-generated provenance records, an API integration portal and compliance reporting, plus separate logins for cask investors. It was built in Speyside in partnership with Scotch industry practitioners; named case studies include Lochlea Distillery and Copal Tree Distillery. It makes no machine learning claim: the analytics are operational reporting, production efficiency and loss accounting, not predictive models.

name: MasterDistiller
short_description: MasterDistiller is an end to end distillery management system for whisky, rum, gin and kombucha producers, bottlers and warehouse keepers. It is built as a custom application layer on the open source Odoo ERP platform, so distillery-specific apps for production and distillation, maturation and warehousing, vatting and bottling and a grain to glass provenance journey sit alongside Odoo inventory, manufacturing, purchase, sales and accounting. It sells on integration, traceability and regulatory reporting rather than analytics, and makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site.

name: CASE SA (Bodegas Bejerman)
short_description: CASE SA is a Mendoza software house in the Parque Tecnologico whose Bodegas product is a management system built specifically for the Argentine wine industry and fully integrated into Bejerman ERP, the Thomson Reuters business management suite. It covers vineyard work with cost allocation to the resulting wine, grape maturation tracking that produces a ripening curve to inform the harvest date for each variety and parcel with year on year comparison, harvest intake logged truckload by truckload against the originating parcel, and the traceability and quality records demanded by export markets and Argentine regulation. CASE also sells a separate data analytics practice. Nothing on the site claims machine learning: the maturation curves and vineyard yield reports are conventional record keeping and reporting.

name: Agaram InfoTech (AgES Brewery ERP)
short_description: Agaram InfoTech is a Chennai ERP and IT solutions company whose AgES Brewery ERP is a purpose-built brewery management system for the Indian market, one of very few Indian-domiciled brewery ERP vendors. Modules cover material management, brewing, fermentation, bright beer tracking, production planning, quality control, sales and distribution and plant maintenance, with automated excise duty calculation, batch traceability and keg tracking as the local differentiators. It is sold to craft breweries, contract brewers and regional operations, and the company claims over 100 clients across its product range. It makes no AI claim: the product offers real-time dashboards and production reporting only.

name: VinesOS
short_description: VinesOS is an all-in-one direct-to-consumer platform for wineries, covering point of sale, wine club and subscription management, ecommerce, tasting room events and reservations, CRM and email, loyalty, inventory management and website hosting on a single system with Stripe payments. It is sold on flat-rate pricing from 299 US dollars per month with no percentage taken on transactions, and the entry tier is also marketed to smaller breweries, distilleries and drinks shops. Its analytics are conventional sales reporting sliced by location, channel, product and customer. There is no AI or machine learning claim on the site; this is a system of record for winery DTC revenue.

name: BeerRun (SWK Technologies)
short_description: BeerRun is brewery management software for craft brewers, owned and sold by SWK Technologies, a US accounting and ERP reseller. It handles production logging with batch numbers, crew, date and tank capacity, a fermentation Gantt chart that reflows as batches move, and scheduling of future batches that are not committed until they hit the mash tun. It integrates with the brewery's accounting system so the reorder point is driven by projected brews against ingredients on hand rather than a static threshold, and it targets microbreweries in roughly the 1,000 to 50,000 barrel range. It has been on the market since at least 2013. The forecasting is deterministic projection arithmetic against planned batches, not machine learning, and no AI claim is made. Note that beerrun.com is a JavaScript single page app serving no crawlable text, so the product detail was verified on the owning vendor's own site.

name: BatchMaster Software
short_description: BatchMaster is a process manufacturing ERP with a dedicated brewery and distillery vertical, sold heavily into India alongside its US base and marketed there as brewery ERP software for beer and wine producers. The brewery configuration covers recipe management with version control and R&D support, brew assembly control, per-bottle and per-barrel margin visibility, stage-by-stage actual cost tracking, lot tracing from vendor procurement through customer shipment, and TTB audit preparation. It runs standalone or on top of QuickBooks, SAP Business One, Dynamics 365 Business Central, Dynamics GP or Sage 100 and 300. The company lists an Artificial Intelligence module among its process manufacturing modules, but the brewery and distillery material describes no machine learning of any kind, so treat this as a system of record for drinks production until the AI module is verified.

name: Earthly Labs (Chart Industries)
ai_use_case: co2 capture monitoring and performance tracking
key_people: Alex Calkins (Technical Solutions Manager, Earthly Labs)
short_description: Earthly Labs sells CiCi, a small footprint carbon capture and purification system that recovers fermentation CO2 at breweries and wineries and repurifies it to ISBT beverage grade for reuse in carbonation and production. It was acquired by Chart Industries and its installations are monitored through the Howden Uptime remote monitoring dashboard, which tracks capture volume and key performance indicators and interfaces with the Earthly Labs team. Named beverage installations include Real Ale Brewing Company and Maine Beer Company in beer and Opus One in Napa Valley in wine. The monitoring layer is telemetry and KPI dashboarding; no machine learning claim is made in the product material.

name: ecoSPIRITS
ai_use_case: closed loop packaging and carbon reduction reporting
short_description: ecoSPIRITS runs a closed loop distribution system for premium spirits and wine, replacing single use glass with the reusable ecoTOTE and SmartPour dispensing hardware, and reports the resulting packaging waste and carbon reductions to brand owners. It says it works with nearly 200 spirit and wine brand partners across 27 countries and about 3,000 venues, naming Bacardi, Remy Cointreau, Smirnoff, Beefeater, Goslings and Accolade Wines. Offices are in Singapore, London and Miami. This is circular packaging plus tote tracking and impact accounting; the company makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Napa Green
ai_use_case: vineyard and winery sustainability certification data
short_description: Napa Green is a nonprofit certification body for Napa Valley vineyards and wineries, running two standards built on more than 250 best practices covering soil health, water conservation, emissions reduction, biodiversity and social equity. It reports 51 certified vineyards, 96 certified wineries and 5,500 certified acres, with named certified members including Silver Oak Cellars, Truchard Vineyards and Chimney Rock Winery, and it supports members in building Carbon Farm Plans. It is a structured audit and data collection scheme for wine sustainability reporting and makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Deep Sky Vineyard
ai_use_case: sensor driven precision irrigation and vineyard analytics
short_description: Family owned Arizona winery with vineyards in Arizona and Argentina that co-developed a smart vineyard platform with Google Cloud Technology Partner niolabs. Sensors across the blocks feed water flow and soil moisture readings through Cloud IoT Core and Pub/Sub into BigQuery, with Looker Studio for analysis, letting the growers irrigate by gallons per vine rather than by timer. Published results include roughly 1.6 million gallons of water saved in 2018 and the elimination of shrivel and bunch rot in their Grenache. The company makes no machine learning claim: the Google Cloud case study says only that it is exploring ML for future yield insight, and its own technology page describes zone profiling and record keeping rather than models.

name: Enartis
hq_location: San Martino di Trecate, Novara, Italy
ai_use_case: distribution of ai fermentation monitoring to wineries
short_description: Italian winemaking inputs company making stabilising agents, fining agents, oak alternatives and mannoproteins, part of the Esseco group. It is the worldwide exclusive distributor of WINEGRID, the Portuguese SaaS fermentation monitoring system from Watgrid whose algorithms read production parameters in real time and support predictive analysis of a vinification, which Enartis markets under a Smart Enology positioning. Enartis has also announced the acquisition of Parsec, the Italian winery automation and intelligent control company. The AI is not Enartis's own: it is built by WINEGRID and Parsec, and Enartis is the commercial, integration and distribution layer around it.

name: Spirits Consulting Group
hq_location: New York, New York, United States
ai_use_case: beverage operator reporting dashboard
short_description: New York beverage industry consultancy working with spirits, wine, coffee and non alcoholic brands on go to market planning, ecommerce and digital strategy, brand and product innovation, and strategic advisory. Its proprietary tool is the Bevantek Dashboard, which pulls distributor sales and depletion feeds, ecommerce platforms including Shopify and ReserveBar, social accounts, Klaviyo email, on premise POS partners and QuickBooks into a single operator view. Bevantek is unified reporting rather than modelling and the company makes no machine learning claim for it, although Funnel 3D and an Assistant module are flagged as new.

name: NextGen Wine Marketing
ai_use_case: generative engine optimization for winery discovery
short_description: Napa Valley digital marketing agency working with wine brands on websites, ecommerce, SEO, paid media, email and marketing automation, with clients including Grgich Hills Estate, Hill Family Estate, LIOCO and DaVero Farms. It now sells Generative Engine Optimization and AI Search Optimization as named services, aimed at getting winery inventory, tasting notes and brand content surfaced by assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. This is advisory and content work around third party models: the agency builds no model of its own and makes no machine learning claim.

name: IBM
ai_use_case: enterprise ai, asset maintenance and supply chain for beverage producers
short_description: IBM sells AI, automation and supply chain software into brewing, distilling and wine, and is the technology partner behind several beverage deployments already tracked here. Published beverage engagements include a company-wide AI and automation transformation at HEINEKEN through IBM Consulting and Red Hat, IBM Maximo asset management across three Spendrups Bryggeri brewery sites in Sweden delivered with IBM Platinum Business Partner Epical, an AI solution built for Bodegas Cepa 21 in Ribera del Duero on Watson Studio, Cognos Analytics and Weather Company data, and IBM Blockchain Transparent Supply, which is the platform underneath eProvenance's VinAssure wine supply chain product. IBM Japan also co-developed Sapporo Holdings' recipe generation AI. The AI is IBM's own across watsonx, Watson Studio and Maximo Monitor and Predict; the beverage work is delivered as consulting plus product rather than as a beverage specific offering.

name: Integra Estrategia y Tecnologia
ai_use_case: viticultural zoning and grape ripening prediction
short_description: Spanish technology and strategy consultancy with a Food and Beverages practice. It was the technology partner on the Cepa 21 winery AI project in Ribera del Duero alongside IBM and Universidad Europea de Madrid, designing a solution fed with Ribera del Duero Designation of Origin data and Weather Company meteorological data. The published case study states the solution applied more than ten AI techniques over more than 50 million records to characterise and zone the region, relate climate events to grape parameters, and predict grape ripening indices, with results surfaced on dashboards. Evidence for its beverage work is a single client project, not a productised wine offering.

name: Bodegas Cepa 21
ai_use_case: harvest and vintage decision support
short_description: Ribera del Duero winery of the Emilio Moro family that commissioned a bespoke AI system to inform winemaking decisions each harvest. The system, built with IBM and consultancy Integra using Watson Studio, Watson Machine Learning and Cognos Analytics, cross-references historical winemaking data held by the Ribera del Duero Designation of Origin regulatory board with historical weather data from The Weather Company. Reported outputs are viticultural zoning of the region, links between climatic events and grape parameters, and prediction of grape ripening indices. The AI is not built in house; the winery is the operator of a system built for it, and the most recent public evidence of the project dates from August 2020.

name: HEUFT SYSTEMTECHNIK
ai_use_case: deep learning machine vision inspection of empty and full bottles on brewery filling lines
short_description: German maker of inspection, fill management and X-ray systems for beverage filling lines. Its own site describes HEUFT reflexx A.I., an image processing stack using multi-layer neural networks pre-trained on thousands of defect-free bottle images that classify containers as good or bad on overall pattern rather than single features, plus anomaly detection for previously unseen defect types, shipped inside the InLine II IX empty bottle inspector. A December 2025 HEUFT reference names the Austrian private brewery Zwettl (Karl Schwarz GmbH, Lower Austria), where an InLine II IR, two Spectrum II VX units and three reflexx A.I. cameras built into the labeller check labelling quality and best-before dates at up to 36,000 bottles per hour. The AI is packaging line quality inspection, not process or fermentation modelling.

name: Whiskey House of Kentucky
ai_use_case: fully instrumented contract distillery building ai-ready production data for ml and model predictive control
key_people: Roger Henley (VP of Engineering and Technology)
short_description: Contract whiskey producer on a 176 acre campus in Elizabethtown, Kentucky, offering custom distilling, warehousing, bottling and financing to brands that do not own a distillery. An Inductive Automation customer project published on the build describes a plant automated end to end on Ignition, with SCADA, MES, ERP and cloud analytics unified on one platform and production data exposed to contract customers through a portal. The distillery team states its roadmap is predictive analytics on Microsoft Fabric plus machine learning and model predictive control, and describes the data as AI ready for LLM and retrieval augmented workflows. The AI is stated as in development, not in production, and the company's own website makes no AI claim. Build ran July 2023 to July 2024 with deployment through April 2025; partners were Quantum Solutions Inc for PLC and SCADA and Flexware Innovation for scheduling.

name: optek-Danulat
ai_use_case: no ai claim; inline optical sensors feeding brewery process control
short_description: German maker of inline optical process sensors measuring turbidity, colour, UV-VIS-NIR absorbance and concentration in process liquids, with a dedicated brewing product line. Its own brewery pages cover beer filtration control, separator control, yeast management and harvesting with the AS16-VB-N beer and yeast interface sensor, brewhouse turbidity and ASBC and EBC beer colour measurement. The company states more than 30,000 installations worldwide and offices in Germany, the United States, Singapore and China, but names no individual brewery on these pages. optek makes no machine learning claim; it matters to the beverage data landscape because these sensors are where much of the continuous measurement data in a brewery originates.

name: Corso Systems
ai_use_case: no ai claim; scada, plc and process historian integration for distilleries and breweries
short_description: US industrial automation system integrator and Premier Integrator for Inductive Automation's Ignition platform, working on automation, systems integration, visualisation, OT cybersecurity and legacy modernisation. Its own case study names 10 Torr Distilling and Brewing in Reno, Nevada, where Corso delivered Allen Bradley CompactLogix PLC programming and an Ignition Perspective SCADA covering automated grain dispensing, two mash systems, fourteen fermenters, a glycol chiller, a stripping still, a 28 foot vacuum still and a canning line, plus process historian, recipe management, scheduling and TTB reporting. Founder Randy Soule of 10 Torr is quoted on running multiple batches with one operator. Corso makes no machine learning claim; it is the consulting and integration layer that puts brewery and distillery process data into a historian in the first place.

name: Flexware Innovation
ai_use_case: no ai claim; mes, scada and industrial data integration for distilleries
short_description: US OT and IT systems integrator of more than 25 years, selling MES integration, SCADA and HMI, industrial data management, business intelligence, automation controls and ERP integration, including its own SparkMES product. Its own site names The Bardstown Bourbon Company, where Flexware advised on and built a new Ignition based SCADA system sized for future distillery demand rather than a like for like legacy conversion, and it was the second phase partner on scheduling and internal help desk at Whiskey House of Kentucky. Ball Corporation, a beverage can maker, is also a named customer. Flexware makes no machine learning claim for the distillery work; it is a consulting and integration player in the distilling data stack.

name: Soufflet Malt
ai_use_case: ai recommended malting recipes and a group malt data platform
short_description: Soufflet Malt, part of the InVivo group, is one of the largest maltsters in the world with 2,200 employees, 35 malthouses in 20 countries and about 3.6 million tonnes of capacity, supplying brewers, distillers and food manufacturers. Its MAITE project (Malt Artificial Intelligence Technologies), developed with a startup partner from 2018 and first deployed at the Canteleu malthouse near Rouen, collects data recorded through the malting process and recommends the production parameters a plant manager should apply to reach a target malt spec; it has since been extended to other sites in France and abroad. In 2026 the company launched MALTimize, a group data platform built with InVivo's IT and Digital Factory that consolidates production and commercial data for predictive analytics and decision support, with an AI chatbot layer announced for the second half of 2026. The AI is malting process optimisation and quality prediction, not barley genomics.

name: Lesaffre
ai_use_case: machine learning on yeast sensory data plus protein language models for strain and enzyme engineering
short_description: Lesaffre is a global yeast and fermentation group and the parent of the brewing yeast brand Fermentis, which is tracked separately. Its own newsroom, in a piece dated 30 June 2025, describes AI-guided protein language models used for protein engineering at the Lesaffre International Science and Technology campus, an AI production analysis tool already deployed in several plants with reported yield and energy gains, and a target of AI implementation across 30 manufacturing sites covering 80 percent of production volumes by 2028, run by a Digital, Data and Tech department of over 120 professionals. The beverage-specific piece is the Sensory Machine Learning project run by Fermentis Academy with group R&D, which trained models on analytical and sensory panel data to predict how a brewing yeast strain shapes beer aroma and won an award at the group's first Digital, Data and Tech awards in November 2025. Tracked at group level because the AI programme, the biofoundry and the protein models sit with Lesaffre rather than with Fermentis.

name: Yakima Chief Hops
ai_use_case: predictive inventory modelling and brewing supply analytics
key_people: Cesar Silva-Monroy (Chief Information and Strategy Officer)
short_description: Yakima Chief Hops is a grower owned hop supplier selling pellets, Cryo products and extracts to brewers worldwide, and runs an extensive GC-QTOF and GC-SCD analytical and sensory programme to characterise beer soluble hop aroma compounds. A previous sweep rejected it for having no AI claim; the new evidence is a vendor case study describing its Business Technology team, an enterprise data warehouse with a dedicated data science sandbox, near real time BI across six business units and a model that predicts the probability of over and under inventory so overstock hops can be released for sale, targeted at a 5 to 10 percent revenue improvement. The verified modelling is commercial and supply analytics, not aroma or breeding prediction: the hop chemistry work is analytical chemistry with no machine learning claim attached. The corporate site returned HTTP 429 on repeated fetches during this sweep, so its own pages could not be quoted directly; the tools subdomain resolved.

name: Boortmalt
ai_use_case: none claimed
short_description: Boortmalt is a global maltster with about 3 million tonnes of capacity across 25 malting plants on five continents, supplying brewers, distillers and food manufacturers. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its own website; the malt expertise pages describe conventional analytical quality control. The closest data work is a VLAIO funded Flanders innovation project announced in October 2019 investigating which wort and malt analyses can be used to select new barley varieties against beer quality traits such as taste, foam and colloidal stability, and it is described in purely analytical terms with no modelling claim. Included as a reference point on the ingredient layer alongside Soufflet Malt and Malteurop, not as an AI vendor.

name: SimpliRoute
ai_use_case: ai route optimisation for delivery fleets
key_people: Alvaro Echeverria (Co-founder and CEO), Eyal Shats (Co-founder)
short_description: Latin American route optimisation and last mile delivery platform that plans, sequences and dynamically recalculates delivery routes against vehicle capacity, traffic, terrain and delivery windows, with dispatchers approving every suggested change.
