It grew out of Alvaro Echeverria's University of Chile research on emergency response routing and now reports over 1,000 customers across 26 countries. Beverage evidence is direct: Vina Concha y Toro appears as a named customer and the Chilean craft beer retailer Beervana as a case study. That makes it one of very few beverage relevant logistics AI vendors headquartered in South America.

name: Wineshipping
ai_use_case: temperature controlled wine fulfilment, no ai claim
short_description: Third party logistics provider dedicated to the wine industry, running direct to consumer, direct to trade and wholesale fulfilment out of temperature controlled bonded and tax paid warehouses, including weather triggered ice pack and hold protocols. Its software layer is a client portal for order, inventory and shipment visibility across the warehouse and carrier network. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site. It belongs in this database because it holds one of the largest pools of wine cold chain and DTC shipment data in the United States.

name: Keg Logistics
ai_use_case: keg rental and return logistics, no ai claim
short_description: Keg rental and rent to own provider serving over 2,800 craft brewery customers across the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, with lease terms up to eight years and buyout options rather than a pooled fleet. It also ships full kegs outbound, retrieves empties from distributors and delivers dry goods, so it sits on keg movement data across a large fleet. The company advertises technology and support but names no tracking platform and makes no AI or machine learning claim. Included as a major keg fleet incumbent alongside MicroStar and Konvoy.

name: CaskPilot
ai_use_case: cask inventory and still telemetry, no ai claim
short_description: Distillery management software for craft distillers covering production, cask maturation and warehouse inventory, sales and Australian Taxation Office excise compliance. It includes live still telemetry that streams temperature, ABV and flow into the production record, plus barrel and cask management with scan based stocktakes. Built in Australia with native excise rules rather than adapted from United States software. It makes no AI or machine learning claim: it is a system of record and a telemetry capture point for maturing cask stock.

name: LogiLab AI
ai_use_case: route sequencing for beverage distributors
funding_stage: pre seed, recruiting a founding customer cohort
short_description: Route optimisation software built only for beverage distributors running roughly ten to one hundred trucks, positioned explicitly against generic routing tools. It generates next day schedules that respect standing accounts, delivery windows and vehicle constraints, rebuilds routes when a driver calls out or an emergency order lands, and keeps the dispatcher as approver of every change. The company frames beverage routing as a stop sequencing and three tier compliance constraint problem rather than a distance problem. Early stage: it is openly recruiting a founders cohort of five distributors, so the deployment base is unproven and HQ is not disclosed.

name: NielsenIQ (NIQ)
ai_use_case: genai assistant over retail and on-trade drinks measurement data
short_description: NielsenIQ is the retail measurement and consumer panel business that measures beer, wine and spirits sales for suppliers, distributors and retailers. Its own beverage alcohol pages describe omnichannel measurement across off-premise retail, on-premise venues, e-commerce and DTC, plus the NIQ On-Premise service that absorbed the CGA on-trade drinks panel. The named AI is NIQ Ask Arthur, a generative AI persona that answers questions over NIQ Discover data, and NIQ also runs Byzzer, a self-serve POS and shopper reporting product for small and emerging brands that lists Beverage Alcohol as a covered industry. The underlying product is panel and point of sale measurement with a GenAI query layer on top rather than a bespoke drinks model.

name: Circana
ai_use_case: ai analytics layer over alcohol point of sale and depletion data
key_people: Boris Oglesby (Executive Vice President, Practice Leader, Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco)

people.name: Boris Oglesby
people.role: Executive Vice President, Practice Leader, Alcoholic Beverages and Tobacco

short_description: Circana is the market measurement firm formed by combining IRI (founded 1979) and NPD (founded 1966), and it runs a dedicated alcoholic beverages practice led by EVP Boris Oglesby. For drinks it combines retailer point of sale data with a wet and dry enhanced projection methodology and harmonises it with NABCA control state depletions inside its Unify+ platform. Its named AI product is Liquid AI, which sits on the Liquid Data technology platform and powers the published alcohol category rankings, with the alcohol data spotlight sourced to Circana Liquid AI, May 2026. Circana states it was one of the first in the industry to integrate AI within its technology platform.

name: Mintel
ai_use_case: generative ai research assistant over proprietary drinks market intelligence
short_description: Mintel is a market intelligence agency with about 1,100 staff across 14 offices, and its store carries an Alcoholic Drinks category alongside its wider Food and Drink coverage. Mintel Leap, announced in February 2024, is a closed loop generative AI platform built only on Mintel's own research and analyst output, which the company says removes hallucinations while answering category, consumer and product questions. Mintel also names Mintel Spark, a concept generator that produces new product ideas and mock ups, and Ingredientscape AI for tracking fastest growing ingredients. The AI is a GenAI retrieval and generation layer over a proprietary research corpus rather than drinks-specific modelling.

name: Numerator
ai_use_case: consumer panel and receipt data for bevalc, no ai product named
short_description: Numerator is a consumer insights company built on a receipt and purchase panel, and it lists Beverage and BevAlc as an industry segment it serves within consumer packaged goods. Its products are Insights, Promotions, Verified Voices, TruView omnichannel share, Data Feeds, Media Solutions and consulting. On the pages checked Numerator makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim and names no AI product, so it belongs in this landscape as a panel data source rather than an AI vendor. It matters because brand and distributor teams in beer, wine and spirits use its shopper data to decide assortment and promotion.

name: bw166
ai_use_case: beverage alcohol market data and data science consulting, no ai claim
short_description: bw166 is a beverage alcohol market intelligence and consulting firm led by managing partner Jon Moramarco, publishing the Total Beverage Alcohol Overview plus beer, wine and spirits import and export reports and product approval tracking. It absorbed Gomberg Fredrikson Associates, the long-running US wine shipment research organisation it had partnered with since 2015, and publishes the Gomberg Fredrikson reports. Its data science services page describes business intelligence, M and A analysis, financial optimisation and macroeconomic work, and explicitly does not claim machine learning, AI or algorithmic forecasting. Latest published update seen is the bw166 2026 mid year update.

name: NABCA (National Alcohol Beverage Control Association)
ai_use_case: control state spirits sales data warehouse, no ai claim
short_description: NABCA is the association of US alcohol control jurisdictions and the source of control state spirits sales and depletion data, covering roughly 25 percent of the distilled spirits market. Its Statistics for Alcohol Management (SAM) data warehouse holds account level inventory and sales activity with online analytical processing, real time access and five or more years of SKU level history, alongside the PQRS price quotation system and the Spectre platform. This data is what Circana harmonises into its alcohol measurement, so NABCA is an upstream source for much US whiskey and spirits analytics. NABCA makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: WineBusiness Analytics
ai_use_case: wine industry databases and market reporting, no ai claim
short_description: WineBusiness Analytics sells wine industry data and analysis, including the Wine Analytics Report, the Wine Analytics Database, winery, grower and distributor databases, a Distributor Market Service and the WineBusiness Directory and Buyer's Guide covering more than 2,000 vendor profiles across 190 winery categories. It sits alongside WineBusiness Monthly and carries the Gomberg Fredrikson wine shipment reporting brand. Customers such as Far Niente use the Analytics Report to evaluate performance and segment markets. The site makes no artificial intelligence claim, so this is a database and reporting business rather than an AI vendor.

name: Western Computer
ai_use_case: copilot order entry and financial reporting inside wine and spirits erp
short_description: Western Computer is a Microsoft Dynamics partner that publishes 365WineTrade, an ERP for wine and spirits suppliers and distributors built on Dynamics 365 Business Central and listed on Microsoft AppSource. The product covers multi-state compliance, excise and tax calculation, container management, DTC sales and pre-built Power BI reporting. The AI content is Microsoft Copilot embedded in Business Central rather than proprietary models: the vendor claims Copilot extracts order details from inbound emails to cut manual entry and assists with financial reporting. The company states the solution is used by more than 30 wine and spirits businesses.

name: Velosio
ai_use_case: vineyard and winery erp with production and yield reporting
short_description: Velosio is a Microsoft partner that sells and supports SilverLeaf, an agribusiness ERP built on Dynamics 365 Business Central and listed on Microsoft AppSource, with a dedicated vineyard and winery configuration. It covers vine health and production metrics, inventory, traceability from grape to bottle, and compliance, alongside Power Platform and Azure services. Velosio makes no machine-learning claim for the wine offering: the analytics described are dashboards, custom reports and yield reporting, which is standard business intelligence rather than AI.

name: inecta
ai_use_case: wine and spirits distribution erp with demand forecasting
short_description: inecta builds food and beverage industry ERP on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and runs a wine and spirits distribution vertical covering multi-location inventory, lot traceability, multi-state tax calculation, regulatory compliance and transportation management. The company lists an inecta AI product and offers demand forecasting inside inventory management, but publishes no detail on what the models are, so the verified core is a system of record rather than a demonstrated machine-learning product. It states more than 25 years in the food and beverage industry.

name: Anchor Group
ai_use_case: llm assistant embedded in netsuite
short_description: Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner that implements NetSuite for craft breweries and distilleries, covering batch production tracking, tank and lot traceability, TTB compliance reporting and taproom POS integration. It ships Sonar, a free AI assistant built inside NetSuite with a library of over 260 NetSuite-specific prompts, which is an LLM prompt layer over the ERP rather than a trained forecasting model. Also sells 35 or more pre-built SuiteCommerce apps used by beverage clients for direct-to-consumer sales.

name: Beyond Cloud Consulting
ai_use_case: ai production scheduling on netsuite
short_description: Oracle NetSuite implementation partner with a dedicated distillation and brewing practice, positioning NetSuite for catch-weight costing, lot tracking, regulatory compliance and supply chain management at drinks producers. It has built its own AI-branded NetSuite extensions including an AI Production Scheduler and Execution module, an AI Voice Agent, AI Field Service Management and AI Fleet Management. The technical basis of the AI in these modules is not disclosed on the site. Named Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner Spotlight Award winner in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, with over 400 implementations claimed.

name: FoodQloud
ai_use_case: none claimed; craft drinks erp reseller
short_description: Dutch Oracle NetSuite partner that implements Crafted ERP for craft breweries, wineries and distilleries in Europe, covering fermentation management, tank monitoring, barrel management, excise tax reporting and label registration alongside NetSuite CRM and SuiteCommerce. It makes no AI or machine learning claim of its own: the offering is role-based dashboards and KPI reporting on top of the NetSuite data model. Named beverage customers include Toorank Distilleries, Texelse Brouwerij and ODB Beverages.

name: Repsly
ai_use_case: shelf image recognition and ai territory planning for beverage field teams
short_description: Repsly is a retail execution platform for consumer goods field teams, with a stated push into the beverage category and Asahi named as a customer on its own site. Its AI is real and named: image recognition that returns shelf insights from photos in under 60 seconds at a claimed 98 percent SKU accuracy, delivered through a September 2025 partnership with ParallelDots, plus an AI-powered Territory Advisor launched in July 2025 that reworks rep territory assignments. A November 2025 release added Calypso Lemonade, Mela Watermelon Water, Health-Ade and So Good So You to its beverage portfolio, so the alcohol exposure is beer-side while the wider book is non-alcoholic drinks.

name: ParallelDots (ShelfWatch)
ai_use_case: computer vision shelf auditing for drinks brands
short_description: ParallelDots builds ShelfWatch, an image recognition product that reads shelf and cooler photos taken by field reps to score availability, planogram compliance and share of shelf. Its own site names Heineken, Asahi and Bacardi Limited among its clients, which puts it directly on beer and spirits execution, and it lists alcohol as an industry solution. The company reports coverage of 2.5 million retail outlets across 50 plus countries and 15 million photos processed monthly, and raised a 4.5 million dollar Series A led by Btomorrow Ventures, the venture arm of BAT. It supplies the image recognition layer behind Repsly's retail execution product under a partnership announced 30 September 2025.

name: Customertimes (CT Mobile)
ai_use_case: ai assisted field sales and visit execution on salesforce
short_description: Customertimes builds CT Mobile, a native Salesforce field sales app with full offline working, guided visit workflows, in-visit ordering and automated data capture, listed in the Salesforce Consumer Goods app guide. Pernod Ricard is named as a customer on the product page and quoted describing a relationship of more than five years, which puts the product inside a major spirits and wine group's route-to-market stack. The AI claim is deliberately general: the site says AI-powered insights and intelligent automation but names no specific model or AI feature, so treat the AI depth as unverified while the Salesforce-native field execution is well evidenced.

name: Salesforce
ai_use_case: platform layer under beverage crm, retail execution and route to market
short_description: Salesforce is the platform the beverage alcohol software layer is largely built on, and until now the radar tracked only the products built on it, not the platform itself. Consumer Goods Cloud carries retail execution, visit management, trade promotion and order capture, and is now branded and taught as Agentforce Consumer Goods, its agentic AI line. Its AppExchange consumer goods collection lists beverage alcohol apps directly, including GreatVines for three-tier supplier, distributor and agency execution, alongside CPGvision, CT Mobile and Ivy Retail Execution. Salesforce also owns Tableau, Data Cloud and MuleSoft, which are the analytics and brewery ERP integration paths used across the drinks companies already tracked here.

name: Mirketa
ai_use_case: salesforce crm and einstein consulting for wineries and spirits brands
short_description: Mirketa is a Salesforce consulting firm with a published winery and spirits CRM practice, covering three-tier sales tracking, distributor and tasting room data, and its own AppExchange utilities for sales cycle analytics, lead distribution and duplicate record management. It sells Salesforce Einstein consulting rather than any proprietary model, so the AI here is implementation of someone else's, not its own. Delivery is US strategy teams plus centres in Noida and Bangalore. Included because consulting is one of the thinnest slices in the database and this is a named wine and spirits practice, not a generic one.

name: 6Street Digital
ai_use_case: salesforce b2b commerce accelerator for alcohol distribution
short_description: 6Street Digital is a Salesforce commerce partner that ships an AlcBev Storefront Accelerator, a preconfigured Salesforce B2B Commerce storefront for alcohol distributors with industry components such as mix and match promotions and inventory checks to cut ordering errors. It reports 70 plus B2B commerce implementations and works across Austin, San Antonio and Carrboro. The accelerator page makes no AI claim at all and none should be read into it; the homepage lists AI and automation only as a general service line. It matters to the beverage data landscape as the ordering front end feeding distributor Salesforce data, not as a machine learning vendor.

name: Omnivo Digital
ai_use_case: salesforce and agentforce implementation for beverage distributors
short_description: Omnivo Digital is a Salesforce consultancy with a published beverage distributor practice covering route management and direct store delivery, multi SKU pricing and discount tiers, order and inventory integration, and field rep mobile rollout, sold on a pay for results rather than hourly model. Its own site lists Agentforce and AI deployment as a service line, so the AI is Salesforce's, implemented by them, with no proprietary model of their own. No beverage client is named publicly; the disclosed case studies are outside drinks. Included to fill the thin consulting slice, with the caveat that beverage evidence is a practice page rather than a named account.

name: GQS AG
ai_use_case: no ai claim, sap erp add-ons for beverage excise duty and batch traceability
short_description: GQS AG is an SAP Gold Partner in Grasbrunn near Munich that builds industry add-ons on SAP S/4HANA for food and drinks manufacturers across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Its beverage modules cover excise duty (beer tax) reporting, contract management, returnable packaging and empties, and batch traceability for brewers and other drinks producers. The company makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim anywhere on its beverage pages; it is a system of record and compliance layer, not an analytics vendor.

name: SAPTOOLS (a valantic company)
ai_use_case: machine learning demand forecasting in sap ibp for a brewing group
short_description: SAPTOOLS is a Spanish SAP supply chain consultancy, now part of the valantic group, specialising in SAP IBP, APO, PP/DS and Digital Manufacturing. It delivered SAP IBP demand planning and DRP plus tactical S&OP at Hijos de Rivera, the Galician brewing group behind Estrella Galicia beer, 1906, Maeloc cider and Ponta da Boga wine, using its own easyDP accelerator over a 5.5 month project. The forecasting capability is SAP IBP's built-in statistical and machine learning models rather than SAPTOOLS' own algorithms; the firm also lists machine learning in supply chain as a separate service line.

name: Savantis Solutions
ai_use_case: sap systems integration for drinks companies, marketed with predictive and augmented analytics
short_description: Savantis Solutions is a full service SAP global systems integrator in Scottsdale, Arizona that runs Beers, Wines and Spirits as a named industry vertical alongside consumer goods and life sciences. Its published beverage work is SAP S/4HANA, commerce, CRM and marketing for alcoholic beverage distributors covering web ordering, field sales, procurement, fulfilment and finance. The firm markets predictive and augmented analytics and process automation at company level, but publishes no named machine learning deployment at a brewer, distiller or winery, so treat the AI framing as positioning rather than a verified beverage model.

name: Clockwork Business Solutions
ai_use_case: no ai claim, sap business one distillery erp with batch and excise traceability
short_description: Clockwork Business Solutions is a Bengaluru based SAP Business One partner with a dedicated distillery blueprint covering process mapping, regulatory alignment and industry add-ons for spirit producers. The solution tracks raw material and spirit movement end to end, runs recipe driven production with controlled loss monitoring, automates excise duty and statutory reporting, and integrates weighbridges, flow meters and barcode or RFID hardware across bonded and non-bonded warehouses. It offers SAP Business One Analytics and refers to advanced analytics in later rollout phases but makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim, and names no distillery customers publicly.

name: VisualK Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim, sap business one for winery production and vineyard to bottle traceability
short_description: VisualK Group is a Chilean SAP Business One distributor and implementation partner founded in 2004, the first SAP Business One partner in Chile, operating across Chile, Argentina and Peru with a certified development arm, VisualD. It publishes wine industry material covering SAP Business One for vineyard cultivation, cellar production, inventory, traceability from vine to bottle and distribution, aimed at South American bodegas. It makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim; the wine work is ERP, traceability and reporting, and no winery customer is named publicly.

name: Coopers Brewery
ai_use_case: tableau production and supply chain dashboards, no ai claim
key_people: Dr Jon Meneses (Brewing and Supply Chain Manager)
short_description: Australia's largest family-owned brewery, founded 1862 and now in its sixth generation. It is the named beer company in Tableau's own customer-story library: the case study describes Tableau dashboards across more than 350 SKUs used to cut beer wastage, unify inventory, sales and demand visibility, and surface a correlation between mash temperature and foam stability, with a stated 70 percent reduction in potential revenue loss from wastage. The case study names Dr Jon Meneses, Brewing and Supply Chain Manager. This is visual analytics on brewery process and supply chain data, not machine learning: neither Tableau's write-up nor Coopers' own site makes any AI or predictive-model claim.

name: Fintech (Financial Information Technologies)
ai_use_case: alcohol invoice and scan data analytics, no ai claim
short_description: Fintech runs PaymentSource, the dominant US network for automated beverage-alcohol invoice payments and invoice data capture between distributors and licensed retailers, reported at over 250,000 retail locations and roughly 1 million distributor-to-client connections. Beyond payments it sells scan-based trading with SKU and store-level insight, alcohol scan data for suppliers to track competitor activity, and spend analytics that flag cost variance against expected cost. It serves breweries, wineries, distilleries, distributors and retailers. It matters to the beverage data landscape as a data spine, but makes no AI or machine-learning claim anywhere on its site.

name: Analyticsmart
ai_use_case: retail bi dashboards and category management for drinks brands, no ai claim
short_description: A retail analytics firm with a dedicated beverage-alcohol practice, selling BI dashboards, a beverage-alcohol CRM, category management, planograms and data modernisation to drinks producers, distributors and brand teams. It works retail and market data into brand and category reporting for the drinks trade, with offices in Toronto, Montreal and New York and roughly 15 years in retail analytics. It is a member of the Drinks Ontario trade body. The site names no underlying BI engine and makes no AI or machine-learning claim.

name: TEKreset
ai_use_case: winery power bi data unification, no ai claim
short_description: A Napa-based winery data consultancy that unifies tasting room, wine club, wholesale, distribution, inventory and compliance data into a single model and delivers role-specific dashboards. It builds on the Microsoft Power Platform, using Power BI, Power Apps and Power Automate over the winery's existing ERP rather than replacing it, and publishes public demo dashboards including a Napa Valley winery explorer and an inventory location view over legacy ERP data. It is a services and dashboard consultancy with no AI or machine-learning claim.

name: BeyondVino
ai_use_case: winery depletion and cross-channel kpi dashboards, no ai claim
short_description: An operations platform for wine brands covering logistics and 3PL fulfilment, DTC and wine club, e-commerce and national compliance, with a BeyondVino Intelligence layer on top. That layer supplies real-time depletion and retail account data, consumer and market trend reporting and cross-channel KPI dashboards spanning sales, operations and finance. In June 2026 it announced a partnership with LibDib to join wholesale and direct-to-consumer selling for wineries. The analytics are reporting and dashboards, with no AI or machine-learning claim made.

name: iFactory AI
ai_use_case: predictive maintenance and fermentation anomaly detection
short_description: iFactory AI sells a manufacturing analytics platform with dedicated brewery, distillery and winery configurations, connecting to existing plant automation to monitor fermenters, stills, CIP systems, barrel room environment and bottling lines. It describes itself as an AI native manufacturing intelligence platform using domain specific algorithms trained on real brewery and distillery data, and claims equipment failure prediction two to four weeks ahead, stuck fermentation early warning from Brix curve deviation, AI exception alerts and AI generated work orders. Its headline yield and OEE improvement figures are attributed to unnamed early adopters and are not independently verified. No founding year, founders or funding are disclosed on the site.

name: DBFEX (Spirits Capital Corporation)
ai_use_case: whiskey barrel valuation and pricing
short_description: DBFEX, the Distilled Barrels Financial Exchange, is a digital marketplace from Spirits Capital Corporation where distilleries, brokers, bottlers, brands and institutional investors trade new fill and aged whiskey barrels, alongside a subscription inventory and compliance tool. The company announced in March 2024 that it had completed a three year machine learning programme behind the exchange, centred on a Barrel Value Optimizer pricing tool that it says analyses the supply chain behind each barrel in real time. Trading commenced in January 2025 with over 200,000 barrels listed. The live site says only that the platform offers AI powered tools and insights, with no model detail, so the machine learning claim rests on company press releases rather than published method.

name: Caskd
ai_use_case: genai assistant for scotch collecting and valuation
short_description: Caskd is a UK peer to peer marketplace and digital cellar for whisky collectors, operated by MissionObjective Ltd, where members catalogue bottles, record provenance and trade directly at a three percent flat fee instead of auction commissions. On 25 July 2026 it launched CaskdAI, its own assistant for Scotch collectors and investors, which it says combines whisky domain knowledge with market intelligence and answers valuation questions using current UK retail prices and recent auction results. The AI is a generative assistant layered on market data rather than a published pricing model, and no accuracy claims are made. Founded by Jonathan Yates, a collector with a background in commercial strategy for quantum computing and AI hardware.

name: Atol CD (VineMapper)
ai_use_case: tractor mounted computer vision for vine disease mapping
short_description: Atol CD is a French digital services firm with offices in Paris, Dijon, Lyon, Besancon and Gevrey-Chambertin that has worked with the agricultural sector for over 25 years. On 30 October 2025 it acquired VineMapper from the failed startup Greenshield. VineMapper is a high definition camera with embedded AI mounted on a tractor or straddle machine that identifies vine anomalies, principally early downy mildew symptoms, and maps them at centimetre level positioning with photographic evidence. Atol CD says it will add a new data processing platform and API integration into existing farm management systems.

name: Solumatic (Vitisoft / VINCA)
ai_use_case: conversational assistant over winery management data
short_description: Solumatic publishes Vitisoft, a management suite used by more than 1,600 wine and spirits businesses in France covering CRM, marketing, stock and bottling, invoicing, point of sale and DRM/DAES excise compliance. Its own site lists an integrated AI called VINCA under decision statistics. French trade press reports VINCA shipped in the second half of 2025 and is built on Mistral models, answering plain language questions about the estate's own Vitisoft data and drafting commercial prospecting messages. The rest of the suite is a system of record rather than machine learning.

name: Unhyped AI (Vintelligence)
ai_use_case: terroir and vineyard parcel intelligence API
short_description: Unhyped AI runs a spatial intelligence engine over roughly 7.3 million land parcels, scoring more than 800,000 vineyard plots on bedrock geology, slope, elevation, aspect and classification across 19 to 23 regions in France, Spain, Italy, Germany and Australia. It sells the data two ways: Vintelligence, a REST and MCP native API for wine businesses and AI assistants, and Unhyped, a consumer app that surfaces bottles sharing terroir with Grand Cru sites at lower prices. The engine is geological and geospatial scoring plus producer lineage mapping rather than a learned taste model, and the company says so on its own site.

name: Yamaha Agriculture (The Yield)
ai_use_case: vineyard yield and harvest forecasting
short_description: Yamaha Agriculture sells AI Crop Prediction, an analytics platform that forecasts vineyard yields and grape volumes from operational and sensing data, alongside the Prospr autonomous hybrid vehicle for vineyard work and the FAZER R unmanned helicopter. The analytics line descends from the Australian agtech The Yield, whose Sensing+ irrigation and harvest prediction models were sold to Treasury Wine Estates before Yamaha took the business over; theyield.com now redirects to this domain. Dealers are listed in the United States, Australia and New Zealand, and the company runs a 100 acre test orchard in Washington State.

name: FermentIQ
ai_use_case: brewery management with fermentation forecasting and voice assistant
short_description: All in one production and business management platform for craft breweries, microbreweries, distilleries, cideries, meaderies, kombucha and coffee producers. Covers batch tracking, inventory, CRM, compliance and QC. The AI layer is a voice assistant called BrewBuddy for hands free logging, AI assisted recipe generation, AI trend analysis in quality control, and demand forecasting. The site names no models or technical detail behind the forecasting claims, so the depth of the machine learning is unverified. Publicly priced from 30 US dollars per month for homebrewers up to 1,200 US dollars per month enterprise, which indicates a live product rather than a concept.

name: iStill
ai_use_case: automated cut control plus a genai distilling assistant
short_description: iStill B.V. builds modular automated mashing, fermentation and distillation equipment for craft distilleries and says it serves more than 1,500 distilleries worldwide. Its stills run what the company calls level three automation and robotization: sensors drive the cuts between heads, hearts and tails, reflux and air pressure compensation are handled by the controller, and validated recipes replay with no operator intervention. That control layer is deterministic process logic, not machine learning, and iStill does not claim otherwise. Separately the company has added DistillingAI to its website, a generative assistant it describes as the easiest way to learn about everything related to distilling and iStill, which is a customer facing language model rather than anything running on the still.

name: International Wineries for Climate Action
ai_use_case: winery greenhouse gas inventory and carbon accounting
short_description: IWCA is a working group of wineries founded in 2019 by Familia Torres of Penedes, Spain and Jackson Family Wines of California, which has developed carbon accounting methodologies specific to the wine sector and requires members to produce verified greenhouse gas inventories. It is a partner of the United Nations Race to Zero campaign, and named members include Yealands Estate Wines in Australia, VSPT Wine Group in Chile, Neleman in Spain, Voyager Estate in Australia and Sogrape in Portugal. Its value to the beverage data landscape is the protocol and the verified emissions data set it forces members to build; it makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: The Smart Container Company (KegTracker)
ai_use_case: iot keg telemetry and fleet visibility
short_description: Builds KegTracker, a patented battery powered sensor that turns returnable kegs and casks into connected containers, reporting location, volume, temperature and motion over cellular with a stated five year plus battery life. It sells to brewers, keg lessors, distributors and pub operators trying to cut keg loss, spoilage and wasted collection trips. The company describes reports, real time visibility and data driven decisions, and makes no machine learning claim on its own site. Founded in Cardiff and grant supported by the Welsh Government Smart Cymru programme with engineering support from Swansea University.

name: Node4 (formerly TNP)
ai_use_case: beverage erp implementation for breweries and distilleries
short_description: Node4, which absorbed the Microsoft Dynamics practice TNP, is the main UK provider of Aptean Beverage (Drink-IT), the beverage vertical built on Dynamics 365 Business Central and published on AppSource. Its beverage practice serves breweries, distilleries, cider and soft drink producers and covers production, MES, quality management, plant maintenance, alcohol duty reporting, EMCS movement tracking and pub or outlet contract management. Node4 makes no AI claim for the beverage product itself; it markets general AI business solutions separately. It states it has worked in the beverages sector since 2003.

name: Catalyst ERP
ai_use_case: none claimed; drinks erp system of record
short_description: UK Oracle NetSuite partner selling Bottle ERP, a NetSuite SuiteApp built for small and mid-sized drinks producers. It covers a visual production planning calendar, in-process quality control, label-based traceability, mobile work orders, warehouse management, automated duty and alcohol content reporting and recently added cask management for whisky maturation. Catalyst makes no AI or machine learning claim: Bottle ERP is a system of record and compliance engine, not a predictive tool. Named drinks customers include The Borders Distillery and Ethimex.

name: BioScout
ai_use_case: airborne spore detection for vineyard disease risk
short_description: BioScout makes an autonomous solar powered air sampler that captures airborne fungal spores and images them by light microscopy at 5K resolution, down to 2 microns. Machine vision models classify the spores and return grower facing disease pressure data within about 24 hours, which vineyards use to decide when to spray for downy mildew, powdery mildew and botrytis. Wine industry partners named on its own site include Treasury Wine Estates and Mollydooker. The sensor is also sold in France, priced in French trade press at about 7,000 euros a year.

name: Oculyze
ai_use_case: computer vision yeast cell analysis for brewing, wine and bioethanol fermentation
short_description: Oculyze Automation GmbH sells automated microscope image analysis for fermentation. Better Brewing (BB) analyses a yeast sample for cell concentration, viability and budding count in under a minute from a phone-mounted microscope, with parallel products for wine (Fermentation Wine) and bioethanol, plus a custom image analysis platform and its own annotation tool. The company positions itself as 'Tailored AI Image Solutions' and the brewing product is stated to have been validated by VLB Berlin. The AI claim is genuine and specific: this is image recognition applied to cell counting, replacing manual haemocytometer work.

name: Yokogawa Electric
ai_use_case: reinforcement-learning autonomous control of fermentation temperature scheduling
short_description: Japanese industrial automation and measurement group. Its autonomous control AI, Factorial Kernel Dynamic Policy Programming (FKDPP), was applied to beer fermentation in a 2025 proof of concept run by Yokogawa Digital with Craft Bank, a Kyoto Prefecture craft brewer: brewers manually implemented the AI-generated temperature setting schedule and cut fermentation from 336 hours to 240 hours, a 28 percent reduction, as stated in Yokogawa's own release. The AI claim is specific and quantified rather than promotional. Yokogawa also sells conventional beer fermentation instrumentation, including continuous monitoring by liquid density meter, which carries no ML claim. Recorded as pilot, not shipping: this is a published proof of concept, not a productised brewing offering.

name: Collo (ColloidTek Oy)
ai_use_case: real-time liquid fingerprinting for changeover and CIP optimisation
short_description: Collo sells an inline electromagnetic-field sensor plus a software platform (Collo Insights, Collo Signals, Collo Lab Analyzer) that reads a continuous fingerprint of a liquid in process. The company states it pairs radio frequency sensor technology with AI analytical methods, and that the platform learns from operational data by correlating sensor readings with historical trends and other process variables. It is sold to dairy, food and beverage plants for changeover and CIP optimisation and real-time process control. Collo won the World Beverage Innovation Award in the Processing and Production category at drinktec 2025 and exhibited at drinktec.

name: MarshallAI
ai_use_case: deep learning machine vision for production line quality assurance
short_description: MarshallAI is a deep learning computer vision platform that runs on any camera or sensor and integrates with MES, SCADA and ERP systems. In manufacturing it does automated optical inspection for defect detection, assembly verification, and OCR of barcodes and expiry or batch codes, with the site showing AI-powered OCR read from an aluminium can. It exhibited at BrauBeviale Nuremberg, which is where it enters the beverage landscape. Bittium invested in the company in 2017.

name: vision-tec gmbh
ai_use_case: machine learning bottle and embossing recognition on returnable beverage lines
short_description: vision-tec builds inspection and rejection systems for beverage filling and returnable crate handling: crate checks, bottle checks, pallet checks and robot cells. The company states it has used machine learning in image processing for years to identify individual bottle shapes inside a crate, a problem that has grown harder as the number of proprietary bottle designs increased, and gives embossing recognition as a worked example where the model learns characteristic features from a few sample images. Exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec.

name: Figura Analytics
ai_use_case: particle fingerprinting of drinks samples with machine learning shape analysis
short_description: Figura Analytics is a Loughborough University spinout that built a patented nanopore flowcell using resistive pulse sensing to count and characterise every particle in a liquid sample in minutes, producing a fingerprint of what a normal sample should look like. Shape software is then applied to flag potential contaminants. Drinks analysis is one of its named target markets alongside healthcare, and co-founder Rhush Maugi is described as driving the software development and machine learning platform. Backed by SFC Capital, Innovate UK and angel investors since the January 2021 spinout. It exhibited at drinktec.

name: PRECOGIT GmbH
ai_use_case: none claimed, SAP-based digitalisation consulting for breweries
short_description: PRECOGIT is a consultancy and implementation partner for digitalisation in the brewing and beverage industry, working on SAP technology with pre-built templates for process manufacturing so customers evaluate against a working demo system before committing. Services run from a fixed-price scoping workshop through implementation to support, with a stated focus on manufacturing execution systems and warehouse management. Founded in October 2021 by Dr Michael Eberhard, a brewing and beverage technologist, and Christian Gradt, an SAP specialist. It makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Kestrel Vision
ai_use_case: data driven inspection of containers and filled packs
short_description: Kestrel Vision is a holding group of six inspection companies (Tiama, Pressco, Filtec, Vimec, Somex and GlassFORM.ai) that describes itself as the leading global player in data driven control and inspection for rigid packaging manufacturing and filling, with food and beverage as one of three named end markets. Its products inspect glass and other rigid containers both at the glassworks and on the filling line. The GlassFORM.ai unit is the group's explicitly AI-branded arm; the group site otherwise frames the offer as data and service rather than machine learning. Exhibited at BrauBeviale and drinktec.

name: miho Inspektionssysteme GmbH
ai_use_case: none claimed, optical and 3D inspection on beverage filling lines
short_description: miho is a German Mittelstand maker of inspection systems for beverage filling and returnable container logistics, active for over 45 years. Its product range covers empty bottle sorting before the unpacker (foreign body, lying and inverted bottle detection with 3D measurement), embossing recognition, bottle shape and colour discrimination with sorting into up to eight channels, and residual caustic detection. The site describes optics, high frequency measurement and 3D metrology; it makes no machine learning claim. Exhibited at BrauBeviale and drinktec.

name: BBULL Technology GmbH
ai_use_case: none claimed, inspection and track and trace on beverage packaging lines
short_description: BBULL Technology supplies inspection and rejection equipment plus a track and trace system for beverage packaging lines, covering glass bottles, beverage cans, one-way and refillable PET bottles, food cans, jars and cups. The track and trace product is the data-relevant part of the range: serialised code application and reading across the line for quality and conformity records. The company is part of the BBULL group, which also includes BBULL Computer. It makes no AI or machine learning claim. Exhibited at BrauBeviale and drinktec.

name: CDR (CDR BeerLab)
ai_use_case: none claimed, benchtop photometric beer and wort analysis
short_description: CDR BeerLab is a compact benchtop analysis system that lets a brewery run a wide range of beer, wort and water quality tests in-house on one instrument, without sending samples to an external laboratory. It is aimed at brewers of all sizes for monitoring every stage of the brewing process, and the company publishes method validations against reference techniques. The output is measurement data for quality control; there is no AI or machine learning claim. Exhibited at BrauBeviale and drinktec.

name: Gabert Rebstock Software (GRS)
ai_use_case: none claimed, industry ERP for breweries and beverage wholesalers
short_description: GRS sells vertical business software for beverage producers and the beverage trade, with separate module sets for breweries, mineral water bottlers, juice producers and beverage wholesalers. Brewery functions include field sales information, order processing, customer information, beer duty accounting, indirect customers, returnable container and loan inventory tracking, purchasing and warehouse, dispatch, event pitch costing and statistics, alongside financial, asset and cost accounting. It is a German-language system of record with no AI or machine learning claim. Exhibited at BrauBeviale.

name: Vineyard Robotics (Orchard Robotics)
ai_use_case: computer vision yield estimation per vine
short_description: Vineyard Robotics is the vineyard division of Orchard Robotics, which describes itself as an AI farming company. Its FruitScope Vision camera system mounts to a tractor or ATV and is driven down vineyard rows at 1 to 12 mph, using computer vision models to count and size buds, shoots, flowers and clusters on every individual vine. Data lands in FruitScope Vault, a system of record, and FruitScope OS, a vineyard management software suite. The company states it has built large multi-season crop datasets and is developing Canary, an AI decision layer that is not yet released.

name: Wise Systems
ai_use_case: autonomous route planning and delivery optimisation
short_description: Wise Systems sells autonomous routing and last mile delivery software, with beverage distribution as one of its named industry verticals. The company runs a dedicated AI page stating that machine learning is the foundation of every product rather than a bolt on feature, and that the system learns each operation's actual driving and service patterns from the first route and keeps adapting. Products include Route Planner Engine, Dispatcher, Strategic Planner and Performance Manager. It presented at the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase run by NBWA for beer and beverage distributors.

name: Cirrus Tech
ai_use_case: warehouse automation and control software for beer distributors
short_description: Cirrus Tech is a single source integrator of warehouse automation, control software and distribution software built specifically for beer and beverage wholesalers, and says it has been doing this for over 25 years across 18 beverage automation projects. Offerings span crane systems through fully automated buildings, plus 24/7 US based support with remote diagnostics. It makes no machine learning claim: the automation described is materials handling and control systems, not predictive modelling. It presented at the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: VXP Technologies (Volume x Profit)
ai_use_case: sales execution analytics and incentive tracking for beer distributors
short_description: VXP builds sales analytics and incentive management software for beer and beverage distributor sales teams, covering supplier incentive tracking, variable compensation tracking, distributor targeted objectives and finished product loss reduction. It says over 1,500 distributor sales reps use the platform. The site lists a Sales Execution Agent feature but does not describe an underlying machine learning model, so this reads as workflow automation and reporting rather than ML. VXP presented at and sponsored the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: Repify AI
ai_use_case: automated sales incentive and execution tracking for beverage distributors
short_description: Repify AI is a sales execution platform for beer and beverage distributors that ties incentive programmes to tracked field actions such as volume drives, display execution and new point of distribution win backs, then automates commission payout. It states over 500,000 order to payout matches automated and pricing from 25 dollars per user per month. Despite the name, the site describes rule based automation and matching rather than any specific machine learning model, and no ML claim should be read into it. It presented at the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: iSellBeer
ai_use_case: sales performance management and display execution reporting
short_description: iSellBeer sells a sales performance management app for beer distributors, focused on evidencing retail execution: reporting floor displays, tracking incentive programmes and settling chain feature execution disputes with suppliers. It is a system of record for field execution data rather than an analytics or AI product, and the site makes no machine learning claim. It presented at and sponsored the reception of the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: Elevated BI
ai_use_case: power bi reporting for beverage wholesalers
short_description: Elevated BI is an independent BI consultancy serving beverage wholesalers, run by Austin Bristow who previously managed Power BI reporting at fairlife from 2018 to 2024. Its BevBridge product refreshes distributor RAS data daily into ready made Power BI dashboards as a single source of truth for sales and operations. This is plain business intelligence and consulting with no AI or machine learning claim. It presented at the 2026 BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: IntelliCulture
ai_use_case: vineyard equipment telematics and spray pass verification
short_description: IntelliCulture is a GPS and farm management platform purpose built for specialty crop farms including vineyards, connecting existing GPS hardware or its own. It tracks what equipment is actually doing in the block rather than just where it is, verifying every spray pass, computing true cost per acre, automating OSHA inspection records and GHG reporting. The company says it covers 750,000 acres of nut, vineyard, orchard and specialty crop farms. The analytics are telematics derived; no machine learning claim is made. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 708.

name: VinoCheck
ai_use_case: direct to consumer wine compliance and tax filing automation
short_description: VinoCheck is wine compliance software for wineries selling direct to consumer. It calculates destination based sales tax, wine specific fees and pass through taxes on orders, runs real time compliance checks against volume limits, dry areas and ABV restrictions, and generates sales tax, excise tax and direct shipper filings in one click. It offers a free backtest against a winery's historical order data. This is rules driven compliance automation with no AI claim. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 342.

name: OrderPort
ai_use_case: winery direct to consumer system of record and reporting
short_description: OrderPort is a connected winery management platform covering tasting room point of sale, wine club and allocation, ecommerce, reservations, marketing, payments and real time reporting across sales, club, guests and operations. It is a direct to consumer system of record for wineries and a meaningful source of winery transaction data. The site makes no AI or machine learning claim. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 146.

name: Lumo
ai_use_case: precision irrigation automation and block level water monitoring
short_description: Lumo is a precision irrigation platform combining smart valves, pump automation and an Ops Center used by Napa and Sonoma wine estates and other West Coast specialty crop growers. It measures block level flow rates to close what it calls the irrigation execution gap, covering scheduling, field execution, real time monitoring and water use reporting. The company reports over 200 farms and 99 percent customer retention. The product is sensor driven automation and analytics, not machine learning. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 333.

name: Verdi
ai_use_case: retrofit irrigation automation with sensor driven scheduling
short_description: Verdi sells low cost retrofit irrigation automation for specialty crops including vineyards: smart valves, block level and row level controllers, wireless sensors and gateways plus irrigation software. It claims over 5,000 devices installed, one day retrofit onto existing systems, 30 percent water savings and sensor driven automation where field conditions drive decisions. The company states an ambition to bring agriculture into the AI age but describes sensor threshold automation rather than a shipped machine learning model. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 200 and sponsored the 2026 Unified Wine and Grape Symposium.

name: Ranch Systems
ai_use_case: vineyard telemetry, soil moisture and irrigation control
short_description: Ranch Systems has built cloud connected agricultural telemetry since 2005, selling RM400, RS130, RS330 and RS10 telemetry devices, data loggers, weather stations and the myRanch cloud dashboard. Deployments cover irrigation valve and pump control, soil moisture, weather, tank and pond monitoring, remote cameras and water resource management for districts. It also offers custom agtech software development for other companies. The platform is sensor telemetry and alerting with no machine learning claim. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 426.

name: HotSpot AG
ai_use_case: irrigation, fertigation and frost protection automation
short_description: HotSpot AG sells farm management hardware and software that automates irrigation, fertigation and frost protection systems for growers, water districts and municipal agencies, with remote control and water efficiency reporting against changing water policy. It exhibits to the wine sector at WIN Expo Sonoma, booth 716. The offering is remote control and telemetry automation; the site makes no AI or machine learning claim despite the AG in the name referring to agriculture.

name: Avterra
ai_use_case: vineyard sensor data integration and irrigation decision guidance
short_description: Avterra is a small vineyard technology consultancy on California's Central Coast that integrates data from existing or newly installed telemetry and sensor devices into a single portal, then advises on when and how much to irrigate. It positions itself explicitly as vendor neutral, pulling from a multitude of telemetry devices rather than selling one stack, and leans on over 30 years of vineyard management and irrigation consulting experience. The guidance is human expert interpretation of integrated data, not an algorithm. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 431.

name: FOSS
ai_use_case: analytical instruments and calibration models for wine and beer quality
short_description: FOSS is an analytical instrument maker whose industry lines include a dedicated Wine and beer segment alongside dairy, grain, meat and laboratories. It sells analysers, calibrations and consumables plus a digital services and analytics package layer, and the FOSS IQX platform. The chemometric calibration models behind its instruments are statistical rather than what the company markets as AI. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 236.

name: DH Wine Compliance
ai_use_case: alcohol licensing, reporting and compliance consulting
short_description: DH Wine Compliance is an alcohol industry compliance consultancy in Sonoma County offering licensing, regulatory reporting, consulting and training classes to wineries. It is a services firm, not a software vendor, and makes no technology or AI claim; it matters to the beverage data landscape as one of the compliance intermediaries that actually produce winery regulatory filings. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 338.

name: Wine Compliance Alliance
ai_use_case: winery compliance file management and TTB training
short_description: Wine Compliance Alliance works with wineries to organise and manage the regulatory record of each wine from grape to bottle, covering new licensing, ongoing compliance maintenance and TTB training courses such as harvest tracking and reporting. It either manages the files on the winery's behalf or trains the winery to do it. This is a consulting and training practice with no software product and no AI claim. It exhibited at WIN Expo Sonoma at booth 120.

name: Chunpoong Brewery (춘풍양조장)
ai_use_case: aiot fermentation control for makgeolli
key_people: Wonho Kim (Owner), Joong Sul Bae (Co-founder, CEO of Beonam Brewery)
short_description: Seoul makgeolli brewery that built the Makgeolli Brewing Technology System (MBTS), an IoT sensor layer feeding an AI model that controls the parallel saccharification and fermentation process in real time. The model was trained on decades of process data supplied by Beonam Brewery, a traditional producer operating since 1919 whose CEO Joong Sul Bae co-founded Chunpoong. Its own site describes applying semiconductor-style precision process control and AIoT to fermentation science, and it is the first makgeolli brewery in Seoul open to the public.

name: SAKENOVA (Sakeai Inc. / サケノヴァ)
ai_use_case: iot sensing and data analytics for sake fermentation
key_people: Daichi Niiyama (Founder, CEO and Master Brewer)
short_description: Premium sake brand run by Sakeai Inc., founded 2020 in Niigata by Daichi Niiyama, a former AI engineer who became the brewery's toji. The company states in its own December 2025 release that it uses IoT sensors and AI-optimised fermentation to visualise the process and cut manufacturing labour cost by about 40 percent. Its public site describes rigorous temperature management and analysis but does not detail the model, so the machine-learning claim rests on the company's own announcement rather than published technical evidence.

name: Kyoto Electronics Manufacturing (KEM / 京都電子工業)
ai_use_case: none claimed, oscillating tube density and alcohol analysis
short_description: Japanese laboratory instrument maker that has built oscillating-tube density analysers since 1978. Its DA-155 sake alcohol analyser has long been sold to Japanese sake breweries, most of them small family businesses, and the derived ALM-155 benchtop alcohol meter serves oenology, spirits and beer labs. The company makes no AI or machine-learning claim; it is a measurement and lab-data source for Asian brewing and distilling QC.

name: Atago (株式会社アタゴ)
ai_use_case: none claimed, refractometry and inline concentration measurement
short_description: Japanese maker of refractometers, Brix meters, inline concentration monitors, pH meters and viscometers, with a dedicated product selector for Japanese sake alcohol measurement alongside beer and wine applications. Its instruments are a standard source of gravity and concentration data on Asian brewing and sake production floors. The company makes no AI or machine-learning claim.

name: YoLong Brewtech
ai_use_case: none claimed, plc brewery control and process automation
short_description: Chinese brewery equipment manufacturer in Xiangshan County, Ningbo, supplying nano, micro, brewpub and commercial brewing systems plus in-house automated control systems. Its control panels are built on Siemens, Allen-Bradley and Omron platforms with CE and UL certification, and range from semi-automatic temperature controllers for nano breweries up to full PLC and HMI brewhouse automation. No AI or machine-learning claim is made; the value is process data capture and batch-to-batch consistency control.

name: Micet Group (Micet Craft)
ai_use_case: none claimed, brewery automation and control systems
short_description: Jinan-based manufacturer of small batch, microbrewery and commercial brewing systems, plus distillery, cidery and winery vessels, sold internationally in eleven site languages. It supplies brewery automation and control systems covering temperature, pressure, flow and pH control from raw material intake through packaging, and publishes technical guidance on PLC automation for breweries. The company makes no AI or machine-learning claim.

name: Explorex
ai_use_case: consumption intelligence for taproom and keg operations
short_description: Indian restaurant and brewery operating system, run as Explorex Technologies Pvt Ltd in Bangalore with a US entity in San Francisco, and says it serves over 300 breweries. The brewery product covers taproom POS, QR ordering, real-time liquor and keg inventory tracking, GST billing and Swiggy and Zomato integration. It markets itself as an AI operating system for dining out and offers a Consumption Intelligence module, but names no specific machine-learning model on its brewery pages.

name: Flutebyte Technologies
ai_use_case: none claimed, distillery erp with excise record keeping

It targets Indian distilleries still running on manual registers and disconnected spreadsheets, and markets excise-ready reporting and a live production dashboard tracking yield efficiency, active batches and tank levels. No AI or machine-learning claim is made; it is a system of record and compliance tool.

name: Midhunatech (Midhuna Controls)
ai_use_case: none claimed, distillery erp with scada and plc data acquisition
short_description: Indian vendor of an enterprise distillery ERP integrated with SCADA, taking live PLC and DCS data from ethanol distillery plants into production, quality, accounting, HRMS and supply chain modules. It advertises weighbridge automation, biometric integration, excise compliance and CPCB-ready environmental reporting, with live dashboards for fermenter status, ethanol output and recovery percentage. No AI or machine-learning claim is made; the value is plant-floor data acquisition and regulatory reporting.

It is positioned for the Indian distillery and ethanol blending market rather than as a global product. The site claims trust, security and compliance as differentiators and makes no AI or machine-learning claim.

It is led by Vijay Rekhi, former Managing Director of United Spirits Limited, now Diageo India, and works on blending, brand development and launch, and business scale-up. Services span feasibility and capacity analysis, equipment configuration, contract brewing and IMFL bottling, recipe formulation and pilot scale work, QC, production and bottling SOPs, and head brewer services. It makes no AI or data-product claim.

name: Disruptive Advantage
ai_use_case: beverage and food AI, GenAI and data engineering consulting
short_description: Consultancy delivering AI, generative AI and data engineering into beer, whisky, wine and the wider food and beverage sector, operating across India, Australia and the United Kingdom, alongside a practice built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 with resourcing and outsourcing services. Named focus areas are fermentation and quality prediction, production and commercial analytics, demand planning and sustainability reporting, with GenAI applied to operator knowledge and evidence assembly. PROVENANCE: the beverage and AI scope here is a first-party statement by Ankur Napa, the company's Growth Officer and a tracked individual on this radar. It is NOT independently evidenced: the company website is a short brochure for the Dynamics 365 practice and carries no beverage, AI or machine learning claim of any kind. Recorded as provisional until a public services page or a named client case study exists.

Helps breweries, wineries and distilleries improve fermentation consistency, product quality, operational efficiency and sustainability using data engineering and AI on Microsoft Fabric, Databricks and Azure. Named focus areas are fermentation prediction and risk detection, quality control analytics and anomaly detection, production and sales dashboards, raw material optimisation, AI-assisted recipe and process modelling, commercial planning, and sustainability analytics covering water, energy, CO2 and waste. DP-600 certified Microsoft Fabric Analytics Engineer. Leads the Bangalore Microsoft Fabric User Group for Microsoft and the Bangalore and Newbie Tableau User Groups, and mentors with the Data Visualization Society. Founder of iWort and ships open brewing calculators and analytics apps. Previously AB InBev, SABMiller and United Breweries.

short_description: Lead Data Analyst at vinSUITE, listed on the company's current team page. vinSUITE is a direct to consumer platform for wineries covering wine club, tasting room POS, ecommerce and analytics; the analytics product is reporting and BI rather than a stated machine learning capability.

name: AlcOS
ai_use_case: agentic compliance filing and distributor chargeback validation
short_description: AlcOS is an operations and compliance platform for independent and craft alcohol brand owners in the US, covering beer, wine and spirits portfolios. It tracks TTB federal filings, 50 state ABC obligations, product registrations, price posting and license renewals on an auto-generated calendar, and uses AI agents to prepare and file reports from the brand's own invoice and inventory data, with manual override. A second AI component stores each distributor contract as structured data and validates every chargeback and deduction against the contract terms, price posting records and excise data, returning approve or deny recommendations with stated reasoning rather than a score. The product is at request-early-access stage and the site names no founders, HQ or funding; no independent coverage could be verified.

name: Polestar Analytics (Polestar Solutions)
ai_use_case: trade promotion optimisation and demand forecasting for alcoholic beverages
short_description: Polestar Analytics is an analytics and planning consultancy with a named practice for alcoholic beverage companies, spanning beer, wine and spirits producers. For that vertical it builds market mix models, trade promotion optimisation, pricing analytics, sales and store optimisation, incentive compensation and supply chain control tower solutions. The methods it names are concrete rather than generic: non-linear response modelling, machine learning promotional attribution, ARIMA demand forecasting, Bayesian optimisation and Isolation Forest anomaly detection. It operates as Polestar Solutions and Services (India) and Polestar Insights (US), founded 2012 with offices across eight locations.

name: StayinFront
ai_use_case: on-device image recognition for liquor retail execution
short_description: StayinFront sells field sales CRM and retail execution software to consumer goods companies, and publishes a dedicated position on the global liquor industry. Its StayinFront On-Device AI product runs digital image recognition directly on a rep's device, converting shelf photos into realograms that are compared against the planogram to score distribution, share of shelf, stock and promotional compliance while the rep is still in the store. Related products include Intelligent Guided Selling, Dynamic Routing and Remote Supervision, all of which the company describes as AI-assisted. It reports over 85,000 users in more than 50 countries; the on-device liquor deployment it describes is with an unnamed global CPG company, so the specific beverage alcohol customers are not disclosed.

name: BottleCapps
ai_use_case: loyalty and personalisation for liquor retail e-commerce
short_description: BottleCapps builds branded online storefronts and mobile apps for liquor retailers, beverage alcohol brands and suppliers across the USA and Canada, with email, SMS and push marketing and order management across channels, on a flat 300 to 500 dollar monthly subscription with no transaction markup. Its own marketing describes an AI layer over loyalty that reads behavioural micro-signals such as shifts in purchase frequency, category experimentation, seasonality and basket pairings across POS, email, mobile and e-commerce, and predicts taste migration to drive members-only allocations rather than blanket discounts. That claim appears only in company blog copy and carries no model, benchmark or customer evidence, and the main product site makes no AI claim at all, so treat the machine learning as unsubstantiated. HQ, founding year and leadership are not published on the site.

name: NEC Corporation
ai_use_case: generative AI craft beer recipe and brand copy co-creation
short_description: NEC runs a long-standing applied AI programme with Coedo Brewery in Japan called Agentic AI x Craft Beer, first released in 2020 and relaunched on generative AI. NEC's own large language model, NEC cotomi, generated the recipes, product statements, brand introductions and accompanying short fiction for a four-beer range built around drinkers in their 20s, 30s, 40s and 50s, with Coedo's brewers keeping design authority over what was actually brewed. The work sits under NEC BluStellar and won a Newsweek AI Impact APAC and EMEA award in the marketing and creative category in December 2025. The AI is NEC's, not the brewery's, so this is a vendor entry rather than an operator one.

name: Yeastime
ai_use_case: ultrasound fermentation acceleration with remote monitoring
short_description: Yeastime S.R.L. is an Italian fermentation hardware startup selling a non-invasive, retrofittable ultrasound device that clamps onto existing tanks and bioreactors, claiming up to 30 percent higher fermentation productivity with lower time, cost and energy. It publishes a brewery testimonial from Birra Gaia and co-finances three PhD programmes with the University of Tor Vergata on ultrasonic effects in fermentation. It ships a remote management platform and dashboard alongside the hardware, but makes no substantiated machine learning claim anywhere on its site; this is process hardware plus telemetry, and it is listed here because tank-level fermentation data is part of the beer data landscape. Backers named on the site include EIT Food, CDP Venture Capital, Big Idea Ventures, Plug and Play, MassChallenge and StartLife.

name: Hop Control
ai_use_case: hop aroma profile prediction from essential oil composition
short_description: Hop Control is a hop aroma and dry hopping calculator built by the Italian craft brewery Birrificio Dada s.r.l. for breweries and homebrewers. It composes the essential oil profiles of every hop addition in a recipe, weighting them by boil time and dry hop contact, and outputs a predicted final aroma as a radar chart so brewers can model a hop schedule without trial brews. The database covers over 330 hop varieties with alpha and beta acids plus full aroma oil and sensory data, and the tool is available on web, iOS and Android for 19.99 euro per year after a seven day trial. The company is explicit that this is a deterministic algorithm grounded in published hop essential oil research and validated against test brews at Birrificio Dada, not machine learning; it makes no AI claim.

name: Vigneto Sicuro (Trace Technologies)
ai_use_case: vineyard disease and weather risk prediction
short_description: Vigneto Sicuro is a subscription app for winegrowers built by Trace Technologies S.r.l., an Abruzzo startup. It pulls real-time climate data for a vineyard block selected on a map, with no hardware installed in the field, and runs prediction models the company describes as artificial intelligence to produce a downy mildew (peronospora) and powdery mildew (oidio) risk index several days ahead, plus a localised weather forecast. Products are sold as Peronosporazero, Oidiozero and Meteowine. The claimed 99 percent accuracy figure is the vendor's own marketing and is not independently substantiated.

name: VINAI
ai_use_case: sales forecasting for wineries and distributors
short_description: VINAI is a Spanish cloud management platform for wineries, distributors and Horeca buyers that bundles an ERP with its own wine marketplace. It sells a distinct artificial intelligence module that predicts sales from historical and market data, alongside stock, customer and order, traceability (libro de campo) and labelling modules. The labelling module manages the QR codes required by the new EU wine e-label rules, so the product straddles analytics and compliance.

name: Winestro (Weinbau-online GmbH & Co. KG)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; winery and wine trade management software
short_description: Winestro.Cloud, formerly Weinbau-online.de, is a German cloud system of record for wine estates, sparkling wine producers, Vinotheken, wine merchants and small distilleries. It covers vineyard block work, the cellar book and bottle book, orders, room bookings, a web shop (Winestro.Shop), parcel labels and EU e-labels. The company states it works with more than 2,300 wine estates and merchants over more than 15 years. It makes no substantiated machine learning claim: the platform is transactional software, and AI appears only as blog commentary.

name: EZ Lab Blockchain Solutions
ai_use_case: supply chain traceability and digital product passports
short_description: EZ Lab is an Italian innovative SME that builds blockchain-backed supply chain traceability and Digital Product Passport platforms, with wine and beverages (Vino e bevande) as a named vertical alongside agrifood, fashion and cosmetics. Its wine offering creates the EU-mandated digital wine label, records origin and production data on chain for consumer verification, and adds anti-counterfeiting and NFT marketing layers. The company lists blockchain, smart contracts, NFTs and AI as its technology stack but does not name a specific model; the substantiated core is traceability and compliance, not machine learning. It says it delivered the world's first blockchain traceability of a winery in 2016.

name: Scantrust (U-label)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; eu wine and spirits e-label compliance
key_people: Nathan J. Anderson (Co-founder and CEO), Justin Picard (Co-founder and CTO)
short_description: Scantrust is a Swiss connected-packaging company that started in secure QR codes for anti-counterfeiting and now runs U-label, the EU wine and spirits electronic label platform developed with and endorsed by the European wine industry body CEEV and spiritsEUROPE. Producers create QR-linked e-labels that satisfy EU 2021/2117 ingredient and nutrition disclosure, in all EU languages plus Norwegian, with scan-location-aware recycling modules for Italy and Spain and real-time label edits without reprinting. The only automated language capability disclosed is machine translation for custom content; there is no substantiated machine learning claim. The company has offices in Lausanne, Berlin, Tallinn, Amsterdam, Shanghai and elsewhere.

name: TerraNIS (Oenoview)
ai_use_case: satellite mapping for precision viticulture
short_description: TerraNIS is a French Earth observation SME founded in March 2014 by two former Airbus/Spot Image space applications specialists. Its wine product Oenoview, co-developed and sold with the oenological consultancy Groupe ICV, turns high resolution satellite imagery into vineyard maps used for harvest planning and lot allocation, fertilisation, vine water status and young vine growth checks. Processing rests on in-house remote sensing algorithms; the company describes using an artificial intelligence approach in specific work such as mapping biodiversity features in Champagne vineyards, rather than as the core of the product. Around 20 staff, roughly a quarter of revenue in R&D, with a subsidiary in Chile.

name: SMAG (Agreo Vine & Wine)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; vineyard and cellar traceability software
short_description: SMAG is a French agricultural software house, active on the agricultural web since 2001, whose Agreo Vine & Wine product is a customisable vineyard and winery management system for wine trading houses, cooperative cellars and estates. It handles step-by-step production plans, production and service contracts, traceability from vineyard to cellar, work time analysis, input use and environmental certification paperwork, with a mobile app that auto-detects the plot being worked. The company markets an AgrOptimization System built on agricultural big data but makes no substantiated machine learning claim for the wine product.

name: ISAGRI (ISAVIGNE / ISACUVE)
ai_use_case: no ai claim; cellar traceability and wine sales administration
short_description: ISAGRI is a long-established French agricultural software and hardware vendor with a dedicated vigneron product line. ISACUVE Web manages traceability of wines in the cellar in a full web version, ISAVIGNE handles invoicing and wine export paperwork, and Geofolia covers plot-level traceability, alongside weather stations, capacitive soil probes and a crop disease decision tool. It is a system of record and regulatory compliance stack for French wine growers, with no substantiated machine learning claim.

name: NEUROPUBLIC (gaiasense)
ai_use_case: smart farming advisories for vineyards
short_description: NEUROPUBLIC is a Greek informatics company founded in 2003 in Piraeus that built and operates gaiasense, described as the first and only large-scale agricultural IoT network in Greece, using thousands of wireless telemetric stations it designs and manufactures itself. It lists data science, artificial intelligence, Earth observation and IoT as its core technology services, and gaiasense issues fertilisation, irrigation and spraying advisories from that sensor and satellite data. Its wine work is the SMARTWINERY project (November 2023 to October 2026), an interregional partnership with the University of Murcia, Spanish winery equipment maker Agrovin and the Spanish wine technology platform PTV, aimed at helping small and medium wineries improve production sustainability through data.

name: Agrovin
ai_use_case: no ai claim; winemaking process control equipment
short_description: Grupo Agrovin is a Spanish oenological products and winery equipment maker with more than 65 years of trading and a large patent and R&D portfolio. Its own-technology systems cover the whole production chain (Ultrawine and Ultrawine Perseo extraction, Tank Control, Ulises, Dosisol One, Electrowine, Oxi_Out, FreeK and DosiOx), plus a dedicated no- and low-alcohol wine range. It makes no substantiated machine learning claim on its own site; it matters to the wine data landscape as the process control and sensing layer inside cellars, and is the winery equipment partner named as a data-driven innovation SME in the EU SMARTWINERY project.

name: Bragato Research Institute
ai_use_case: predicting wine quality from wine chemistry
key_people: Jeffrey Clarke (CEO), Darrell Lizamore (Principal Research Scientist, Grapevine Improvement)
short_description: Bragato Research Institute is the research arm of the New Zealand wine industry, wholly owned by New Zealand Winegrowers and set up in 2015 as the country's first Regional Research Institute. Its Pinot Noir programme applies machine learning to predict relationships between wine chemistry and perceptions of wine quality. Other data work includes grapevine genomic sequencing for the Sauvignon Blanc 2.0 clone programme, 5 km granularity climate change projections for all nine New Zealand wine regions using NIWA data, and an industry-wide research data catalogue and structured database.

name: The Australian Wine Research Institute (AWRI)
ai_use_case: no substantiated ml claim; wine analytical chemistry and genomics data
short_description: The AWRI is the Australian wine industry's research, development and extension body, based at the Waite campus in South Australia.
