The site makes no machine learning or AI claim on the beverage pages; it is orchestration software and robotics integration. Presented at the 2026 NBWA BIECC Innovation Showcase and exhibited at booth 216.

name: Aiiro Systems (Sakenowa)
ai_use_case: nlp flavour extraction and taste-based recommendation for sake
short_description: Aiiro Systems Inc. (Aiiro Systems Kabushiki Kaisha, 藍色システムズ株式会社) operates Sakenowa (さけのわ), a Japanese sake check-in app and open data service running since 2013. Its own about page states that the Flavor Chart (registered Japanese trademark 6520969) and the Flavor Search feature are produced by a computer program that analyses posted user comments using natural language processing, then aggregates the result into per-brand flavour scores. The company publishes the derived data free as the Sakenowa Data HTTP API, exposing six-axis flavour vectors, flavour tags, and brand, brewery and ranking endpoints for third parties to build on. Incorporated 2019-06-10 in Kudanminami, Chiyoda, Tokyo; the service predates the company.

name: Holostik India
ai_use_case: liquor track and trace and excise revenue stamps
short_description: Holostik is a New Delhi anti-counterfeiting and secure packaging manufacturer with a dedicated liquor vertical, supplying security holograms, excise revenue stamps, QR and RFID smart labels, tamper-evident closures and a track-and-trace platform to Indian alcohol producers and state excise authorities. Its liquor page frames the problem in Indian excise terms: unrecorded alcohol at 51 percent of consumption and about 15,262 crore rupees of lost tax revenue, with the stated aim of letting tax collectors and supply-chain inspectors detect fraud. The company states over 30 years of operation and a DSIR-approved R&D lab. It makes no substantiated machine-learning claim: the digital layer is serialised codes, authentication scans and supply-chain visibility dashboards, not a model.

name: Sage Software Solutions India
ai_use_case: brewery and distillery erp with excise compliance
short_description: Sage Software Solutions Pvt Ltd is the independent Indian distributor of The Sage Group plc and runs named Brewery ERP and Alcohol and Distilleries ERP verticals for the Indian market, alongside a broader food and beverage practice. The offering covers batch production, fermentation and distillation records, inventory and lot traceability, bottling, and Indian state excise compliance on Sage X3 and Sage 300, with Sage Intacct and Sage Copilot marketed for finance. It is a system of record and an implementation partner, not an AI vendor: the AI branding on the site belongs to Sage's own products, and no beverage-specific machine-learning model is claimed. Relevant to the beverage data landscape because it is one of the few named ERP routes for Indian breweries and distilleries.

name: NeuroTags
ai_use_case: qr code authentication and consumer data capture for spirits and wine
short_description: NeuroTags runs a paired QR code anti-counterfeiting and consumer-engagement platform and maintains a named Spirits and Wines vertical on its own site. Each unit carries an open and a protected code so a single scan both authenticates the bottle and registers the drinker, feeding a customer data platform, loyalty gamification and supply chain visibility for brands that otherwise see nothing past the distributor. The site references a fast private blockchain and mentions AI in passing but substantiates no machine-learning model; the product is serialised codes plus analytics. Included for the compliance and brand-protection slice of the alcohol data landscape.

name: COLAClear
ai_use_case: OCR label reading with a deterministic TTB compliance rules engine
short_description: COLAClear pre-screens US wine, spirits and beer labels against the federal and state rules that drive TTB COLA rejections, returning a colour-coded pass, review or fail report with Code of Federal Regulations citations in seconds. It runs over 30 checks covering class and type designation, alcohol content, standards of fill, the mandatory government health warning, sulfite declaration and grape variety, plus California and Oregon state rules. Public beta launched 4 May 2026 and is free during beta. On the AI question the vendor's own methodology page is explicit and conservative: label text is extracted by optical character recognition supplied by Google Cloud Vision, the checks are deterministic text-matching and pattern-validation against fixed regulatory requirements, and the page states the rule set does not rely on case law interpretation, regulatory inference or LLM-generated content. Launch press describing language-model reasoning is not supported by the vendor's own documentation. Founded by Zillah Bahar.

name: Ivy Mobility
ai_use_case: agentic sales coaching and image-recognition retail execution for beverage route-to-market
short_description: Ivy Mobility sells an enterprise consumer-goods commercial execution platform combining Enterprise Cloud DMS, sales force automation and retail execution, used across beverage and wider CPG distribution. The vendor's own site describes production-ready agentic AI as an intelligence layer over the DMS, naming an Agentic Sales Coach, a tele-caller agent and a distributor operator agent. Its AppExchange listing for Ivy Retail Execution additionally describes image recognition, augmented reality and an AI-based recommendation engine for perfect-store merchandising. The company states it has served P&G since 2011 across 20-plus markets and powers over 11,000 concurrent distributors and 170,000 field users.

name: MaltIQ
ai_use_case: computer-vision bottle identification and recommendation for whisky collectors
short_description: MaltIQ is a consumer whisky app that identifies bottles from a phone camera and makes personalised recommendations. The vendor's own site describes an AI Sommelier that returns recommendations from a stated preference profile and a Smart Scanner using computer vision for instant bottle identification with details and tasting notes, alongside collection tracking and investment tools. Distributed on the Apple App Store and Google Play with a seven-day trial; developer named as Petr Kursin. Headquarters and founding year are not stated by the vendor.

name: Greater (Greater Industries Labs)
ai_use_case: order, route and inventory decision optimisation for beverage distributors
short_description: Greater describes itself on its own site as an AI operating system for beverage distribution that recommends the most profitable decision for every item, account, rep, truck and route in real time, covering order composition, routing efficiency and asset utilisation. The company presented at the 2026 NBWA Beer Industry Electronic Commerce Coalition Innovation Showcase and exhibited at booth 605 as Greater Industries Labs, Inc. The site states the outcome claims but does not name the underlying models or techniques.

name: Divinea
ai_use_case: none claimed
short_description: Divinea runs an Italian wine-tourism and direct-to-consumer platform (Wine Suite) through which consumers book cellar-door tastings and experiences at member wineries, and through which wineries manage those bookings and the resulting customer relationships. Verified directly on the vendor's site, which lists live bookable experiences across Montalcino, Sicily, Alto Adige and Tuscany. The vendor makes no machine-learning or AI claim anywhere on its public site; it is recorded here as winery DTC and hospitality software, not as an AI vendor.

name: Hamilton Company
hq_location: Reno, NV, USA and Bonaduz, Switzerland
ai_use_case: no ai claim; inline process sensors for brewhouse and fermentation
short_description: Hamilton Company builds inline process analytics sensors used through the brewhouse and fermentation, measuring dissolved oxygen, dissolved CO2, pH and conductivity in real time, with ArcAir software for sensor management and GMP compliance. Verified directly on the vendor site, which runs a dedicated brewing applications section. Hamilton makes no machine-learning claim: this is instrumentation and real-time measurement, recorded here as the sensing layer that brewery process data originates from, not as an AI vendor.

name: Q-Interline
ai_use_case: no ai claim; FT-NIR analysis with chemometric calibration for malt, wort and spirit
short_description: Q-Interline is a Danish FT-NIR instrument maker whose Quant at-line analyser and InSight Pro inline analyser measure liquids and powders for product quality control and production optimisation, with calibrations transferable between at-line and inline. Relevant to malt, wort and spirit analysis. The vendor describes chemometric calibration models, which are statistical rather than machine learning, and makes no AI claim anywhere on its site.

name: Lallemand Brewing
ai_use_case: no ai claim; brewing yeast and fermentation science
short_description: Lallemand Brewing is the brewing division of Lallemand Inc, producing dried pure culture brewing yeasts and fermentation products and running an extensive technical education and research programme spanning thiols, yeast strain behaviour and fermentation management. Verified directly on the vendor site after a browser pass cleared its Cloudflare challenge. Lallemand makes no public machine-learning or AI claim for its strain development; it is tracked here as the fermentation science and ingredient layer underneath brewery data, not as an AI vendor.

name: Whiskystats
ai_use_case: no substantiated ai claim; whisky secondary market indices and bottle valuation
short_description: Whiskystats publishes secondary-market price indices and valuation analytics for collectible whisky, tracking the roughly 500 most traded bottles each month across auctions. Its flagship Whiskystats Whisky Index requires at least ten trades in a month before an index change is computed and caps any single brand at ten percent weight, alongside regional and distillery indices. This is a curated auction-price dataset with published statistical methodology; no machine-learning claim appears anywhere on the site.

name: 4T2 Sensors
ai_use_case: no ai claim; inline fluid identification and CIP sensing
short_description: 4T2 Sensors, based in Birmingham UK, builds CIPSense, a fluid sensing sensor marketed for inline clean-in-place monitoring and fluid identification in food and beverage plants. A drinktec 2025 exhibitor. The vendor site is largely visual and states accuracy and process insight without describing any model, so it is recorded here as sensing hardware with no substantiated machine-learning claim.

name: Partender
ai_use_case: no ai claim; bar liquor inventory and consumption analytics
short_description: Partender turns bar liquor inventory into a tap-and-swipe mobile workflow, where staff tap the liquid level on each bottle to complete a full count in around fifteen minutes, then generate purchase orders sorted by distributor. It reports pour variance with a stated accuracy of up to 99.2 percent and highlights top movers and dead stock. This is measurement and reporting over on-premise beverage data with no machine-learning claim on the vendor site.

name: eBottli
ai_use_case: no ai claim; wine and spirits traceability ERP, MES and WMS
short_description: eBottli sells an integrated ERP, MES, WMS and automation platform for manufacturers needing real-time visibility, traceability and paperless operations, with a wine and spirits focus and a combination of software and smart hardware. Verified on the vendor site after a browser pass. The product is positioned on digitisation, connection and asset tracking; no machine-learning or AI claim is made anywhere on it, so it is tracked as a system of record rather than an AI vendor.

name: Barrel Proof Technologies
ai_use_case: IoT sensor telemetry with analytics for cask verification and insurance
short_description: Barrel Proof Technologies fits patented non-invasive IoT sensors to aging whiskey barrels so sealed contents can be verified without opening them, aimed at inventory verification, risk assessment, asset financing and price discovery. The company states four issued patents and positions the sensor telemetry as the data layer under an insurance and finance product. Its own site names IoT sensors, analytics and blockchain together but does not describe what the analytics component actually models, so the AI claim is recorded as stated by the vendor and not independently substantiated.

name: Bertsch Holding
ai_use_case: no ai claim; brewhouse and process plant engineering
short_description: Bertsch Holding is an Austrian industrial group in Bludenz, Vorarlberg, founded in 1925, whose BERTSCHfoodtec division builds process plant and brewhouse systems for the food and beverage industry alongside energy and apparatus engineering. Verified via a browser pass after the site returned 403 to every non-browser client. No digital, control-software or machine-learning product is claimed on its public site; recorded as the plant engineering layer.

name: CRB Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim; food and beverage facility design, construction and consulting
short_description: CRB is a US engineering, architecture, construction and consulting firm with a dedicated food and beverage practice covering facility design, construction, consulting and systems integration for producers scaling up processes. Verified on the vendor site after a browser pass cleared its Cloudflare challenge. Its food and beverage pages describe production rates, energy efficiency, speed to market and food safety compliance, with no machine-learning or AI service claimed. Recorded against the thin Consulting theme.

name: Distilled ID
ai_use_case: no ai claim; distillery management and blockchain provenance
short_description: Distilled ID, founded in Edinburgh in 2018, provides distillery and cask management software that tracks spirit from grain to bottle and issues a consumer-facing Storybook with a certificate of authenticity, using blockchain for provenance and offering product and consumer analytics at individual bottle level. Verified on the vendor site after a browser pass. The platform is traceability, provenance and reporting; no machine-learning claim is made.

name: WineSpotAi
ai_use_case: AI customer service agent for wineries: answers wine club and tasting room enquiries, handles routine support and personalisation across SMS and web chat.
short_description: Temecula, California vendor selling an AI-powered customer support and personalisation layer to winery DTC teams.

name: The Weinheimer Group (VINTAGE2)
ai_use_case: VINTAGE2 is an AI marketing readiness and generative-engine-optimisation model for wineries: audits how a winery brand is represented and retrieved by AI assistants and search, then restructures brand content for machine discoverability.
short_description: Austin, Texas consultancy selling an AI brand visibility framework aimed specifically at wineries.

name: Blended Technologies
ai_use_case: Winery production, inventory and compliance software with an in-product AI assistant, Barry, layered over winemaking, case goods and cost of goods data.
short_description: Napa winery management platform covering winemaking, compliance, finance and case goods, now shipping an AI assistant.

name: Activ8 Commerce
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Wine and distillery DTC stack: point of sale, club and allocation management, ecommerce, CRM, inventory, fulfilment, reporting and dashboards. Reporting is conventional BI, not modelled.
short_description: Pleasanton, California winery DTC platform combining POS, wine club, ecommerce and reporting.

name: eCELLAR
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Winery DTC platform with a centralised customer database across club, POS, reservations and ecommerce, marketed on customer analytics and data-driven segmentation rather than any model.
short_description: Calistoga, California winery DTC commerce and customer data platform.

name: Pour Now
ai_use_case: No AI claim on the product site. Compliant path-to-purchase routing for alcohol brands: turns any brand touchpoint into a working buy link across wine, beer and spirits, replacing static where-to-buy lists.
short_description: Napa startup founded by Paul Mabray building a compliant where-to-buy and checkout layer for drinks brands.

name: Advanced Viticulture
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Vineyard consulting and management built on sensor telemetry: soil moisture probes driving irrigation decisions, plus an air quality sensing line and the Avterra product. Data-led agronomy, no modelling claim.
short_description: Windsor, California viticulture consultancy pairing vineyard management with soil moisture and air quality sensing.

name: myEnologist
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Subscription wine and juice lab analysis using FOSS WineScan instrumentation, returning a full data panel per sample so wineries can trend key parameters continuously instead of testing ad hoc. Instrumented data, no model.
short_description: Napa lab analysis, consulting and cellar supply business selling continuous wine chemistry monitoring on a monthly contract.

name: WECO
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Optical sorting machines including a dedicated wine grape sorting line, plus moisture monitoring. Machine vision hardware sold on sorting accuracy and yield, with no stated learned model.
short_description: Woodland, California optical sorting manufacturer, part of Duravant, with a wine grape sorting product line.

name: Terra Bioindustries
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Enzymatic upcycling of brewers spent grain into protein, fibre, malt syrup and fermentation feedstock. Sells TERRA Malt back into brewing. Process biotech, no model.
short_description: SOSV / IndieBio backed biotech turning brewery spent grain into B2B food ingredients and a brewing malt syrup.

name: ALTR
ai_use_case: No AI claim. Velvet Blade patent-pending membrane system for precision ethanol separation, starting with wine, so producers can dial alcohol down while preserving flavour. Separation engineering, no model.
short_description: Rockstart AgriFood backed team of scientists, engineers and winemakers building precision alcohol reduction for wine.

name: Margin
ai_use_case: AI for beer, wine and liquor store retail operations: invoice receiving from a phone photo, and AI-generated purchase orders that predict demand across thousands of SKUs to cut deadstock.
short_description: Y Combinator S23 POS and operating system for beer, wine and liquor retailers, built by liquor store owners.

name: Flaviar
ai_use_case: No AI or machine learning claim. Whiskey and premium spirits club offering taste-based personalised recommendations to signed-in members, presented as a taste profile feature rather than a stated model.
short_description: Y Combinator S14 whiskey and fine spirits tasting club selling sample packs and full bottles by subscription.

name: PepsiCo
ai_use_case: digital twin plant and supply chain simulation
short_description: PepsiCo announced a multi-year collaboration with Siemens and NVIDIA at CES 2026 to build physics-based digital twins of its plants and warehouses, using Siemens Digital Twin Composer on NVIDIA Omniverse. AI agents simulate, test and refine line configurations before anything physical is built, modelling machines, conveyors, pallet routes and operator paths. PepsiCo reports a 20 percent throughput increase on initial deployment and 10 to 15 percent lower capital expenditure. Early pilots are underway in US manufacturing and warehouse sites, with plans to scale globally.

name: The Coca-Cola Company
ai_use_case: GenAI marketing
short_description: Coca-Cola runs Project Fizzion, a design intelligence system co-developed with Adobe and announced in May 2025. It encodes brand guidelines into a machine-readable StyleID that automatically applies brand rules inside Adobe Creative Cloud, built on Adobe Firefly generative AI, and is used to keep localized campaigns consistent across more than 200 markets. Coca-Cola states content production up to 10 times faster and describes Fizzion as still in pilot phase. The company also has a five-year cloud and generative AI partnership with Microsoft. The AI here is marketing and brand operations, not production or formulation.

name: Nestle
ai_use_case: operations automation and digital twins
short_description: Nestle is the owner of Nespresso, Nescafe, Perrier and San Pellegrino. From 2025 it began upgrading its global digital core on SAP, starting in Zone Asia, Oceania and Africa, explicitly to deploy AI at scale across operations, and states it is pursuing AI, robotics and digital twins. A Deep Tech Center at the Nestle System Technology Center in Orbe, Switzerland opens in the first half of 2026 to develop sensors, robotics, AI and mixed reality for research and operations, including smart coffee machines and dynamic quality assurance. Beverage relevance is via coffee and water rather than a beverage-specific AI product.

name: Danone
ai_use_case: supply chain
short_description: Danone owns evian, Volvic and Badoit alongside its dairy business. In July 2024 it announced a multi-year collaboration with Microsoft to build an AI-enabled supply chain covering forecasting, real-time adjustments and digital twinning of core skills across procurement, production and distribution. In April 2025 it adopted the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, targeting roughly 30 percent less time between data collection and decision. Its Industry 5.0 Academy aims to upskill 20,000 operations employees in AI and digital by 2026.

name: Databricks
ai_use_case: data and AI platform for beverage and CPG operators
short_description: Horizontal data and AI platform, not a beverage company. Included because it is the underlying platform for a growing share of beverage and CPG analytics work. It ships an industry Lakehouse for Retail and Consumer Goods with solution accelerators for demand forecasting, on-shelf availability and recall traceability. Named food and drink users include Danone, which adopted the Data Intelligence Platform in April 2025, plus Gousto, Reckitt and Restaurant Brands International. The AI is the platform capability, not a beverage-specific model.

name: Snowflake
ai_use_case: data and AI platform for beverage and CPG operators
short_description: Horizontal cloud data platform, not a beverage company. Included because it carries a meaningful share of beverage and CPG data workloads. It ships an AI Data Cloud for Retail and Consumer Goods aimed at manufacturers, distributors and CPG vendors, with secure data sharing as the core mechanic. Named drinks-side users include Mark Anthony Group, owner of White Claw and a group of British Columbia wineries, plus US Foods and 84.51 on the retail data side. The AI is the platform capability, not a beverage-specific model.

name: Prefe
ai_use_case: retail distribution and pricing intelligence
short_description: Prefe is an Italian wine tech startup that runs an instant intelligence system tracking more than 8,000 retail outlets every day, so wineries can manage distribution and pricing across large grocery chains. It was selected as one of eight finalists in the 2026 Wine Tech Challenge, an Italian open innovation programme run with major wine companies.

name: Vivelys
ai_use_case: fermentation and maturity decision support
short_description: French oenology technology company selling decision-support systems across the whole wine chain: grape maturity monitoring, native yeast selection, must oxygenation, real-time fermentation density tracking and automated micro-oxygenation aging, plus a digital cellar notebook. It also sells into beer. The site describes sensor-driven process control and expert models rather than machine learning, and the company makes no explicit AI or ML claim.

name: Vitirover
ai_use_case: autonomous vineyard mowing robots
short_description: Vitirover builds small solar-powered four-wheel-drive autonomous mowing robots that keep vineyard rows and other complex terrain herbicide free, sold as a managed service combining robot fleets with human finishing teams and supervised through its Viticloud platform. The robot was invented by the founder to maintain the family estate Chateau Coutet in Saint-Emilion. Navigation is GPS-based; the company claims autonomy and fleet supervision, not machine learning.

name: PlantCT (SmartVineyard)
ai_use_case: vineyard disease forecasting from in-canopy sensors
short_description: PlantCT, sold internationally under the SmartVineyard name, is a Hungarian in-vineyard plant-protection station: leaf wetness, humidity and temperature sensors report every 20 minutes to a cloud backend that runs disease forecast models and shows hyper-local risk on web and mobile. Subscriptions start around 19,900 HUF a month with add-on forecast models. The forecasts are documented as agronomic risk models built on measured microclimate; the company makes no machine learning claim.

name: vintrace
ai_use_case: winery production system of record
short_description: vintrace is cloud winery management software built in Australia that tracks fruit from grape to bottle: work orders, blending, vessel and barrel tracking, compliance and mobile cellar entry. It is now part of Encompass Technologies, which acquired the Slovenian vineyard software eVineyard in 2025 and rebadged it as vintrace Vineyard Management to link block-level vineyard data to winery production. The core product is a system of record; the AI branding on the parent platform sits in the Encompass distribution products, not in vintrace winemaking.

name: Agovor
ai_use_case: autonomous electric vineyard tractors
short_description: Agovor builds the GOVOR eTractor, a compact fully electric autonomous towing robot designed to work between vineyard, orchard and berry rows for mowing, spraying and hauling, with swappable smart trailer attachments and around 10 hours of battery runtime. Named users include Wither Hills Vineyard in Blenheim. It was shown at WinePro 2026 in Blenheim as vineyard autonomy; the company claims remote automation and fleet operation rather than machine learning.

name: Australian Vintage (CTZN)
ai_use_case: genai blend curation and brand marketing
short_description: Australian Vintage is a listed Australian wine producer whose brands include McGuigan, Nepenthe and Tempus Two. In 2024 it launched CTZN, marketed as Australia's first AI-curated, human-crafted wine, with grape varietal combinations selected by AI algorithms and the blends then made by its winemakers, following the earlier French AI wine work by Aubert et Mathieu. The AI is used for varietal selection and brand storytelling; the company does not describe a proprietary model, training data or production ML system.

name: Stravito
ai_use_case: rag assistant over consumer research and insights
short_description: Stravito is an enterprise customer intelligence platform that centralises market research, consumer studies and internal reports and lets teams query them in natural language through Stravito Assistant, which returns source cited answers grounded in the company's own library. HEINEKEN and Carlsberg are named customers, and Stravito publishes two HEINEKEN case studies, one titled 'How HEINEKEN is Amplifying Insights with Generative AI'. Pepsi-Lipton and Danone are also named on the customer logo wall. The AI is retrieval over a private document corpus with citations rather than a model trained on brewing data.

name: Leena AI
ai_use_case: agentic llm assistant over enterprise policy and knowledge
short_description: Leena AI builds agentic AI assistants that answer employee IT, HR, finance and procurement questions by retrieving from a company's own policy documents, tickets and systems. Pernod Ricard, the spirits and wine group, is named as a customer with 19 thousand employees and 15 plus integrations, and Coca-Cola is a published case study for IT support automation. Founded in India in 2018 by Adit Jain, Mayank Goyal and Anand Prajapati, with engineering offices in Gurugram and Bengaluru and investors including Y Combinator, Greycroft and Bessemer. The site does not disclose which underlying models the agents use.

name: TraceGains
ai_use_case: ai over supplier specs, coas and formulation data
short_description: TraceGains runs a supplier document and specification network for food and beverage manufacturers, covering supplier specs, certificates of analysis and compliance documents. It markets TraceGains AI for finding answers across that document set and AI Formulation for working with ingredient data and formulas in one environment. Named beverage customers on its own customers page include E. and J. Gallo Winery, Florida Natural, Tampico and Oatly. The site does not disclose the underlying models or how retrieval is grounded.

name: Poka
ai_use_case: frontline knowledge capture and retrieval for plant operators
short_description: Poka is a connected worker platform for manufacturing plants that digitises operator know how, work instructions and problem solving into a searchable knowledge base, and now markets Industrial AI, AI Agents and an AI Studio on top of it. The pitch is explicitly knowledge retrieval, the knowledge of the best operators made available to every shift. Coca-Cola, Danone and Tetra Pak are named customers, and the company claims over 3000 sites and a million users. Founded by Alex Leclerc and Antoine Bisson, with Schneider Electric named as a strategic investor.

name: L2L (Leading2Lean)
ai_use_case: ai over shop floor data and digital sops
short_description: L2L is a connected manufacturing operations platform covering maintenance, production monitoring and digital work instructions, and it markets Execution AI that turns shop floor data into suggested fixes. HEINEKEN is a named customer on the homepage with a stated 50 percent reduction in training time from digital SOPs. L2L now absorbs SwipeGuide, the Amsterdam digital work instruction vendor whose domain redirects to l2l.com. The AI claim is about surfacing fixes from operational data, not a documented LLM retrieval stack.

name: Moveworks
ai_use_case: enterprise llm assistant over internal knowledge and systems
short_description: Moveworks sells an enterprise AI assistant that resolves employee IT and HR requests by retrieving from internal knowledge bases and acting across connected systems. Coca-Cola Consolidated, the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the United States, is named on the customers page, with a claimed ability to serve three times the employees over five years without adding agents. The beverage relevance is a bottler as a customer of a horizontal product rather than any drinks specific model.

name: New Vintage Labs
ai_use_case: ai analyst over winery direct to consumer data
short_description: New Vintage Labs is a one person software venture building what it calls an AI DTC Analyst for wineries running on the Commerce7 ecommerce platform, with products listed as coming to the Commerce7 App Store. The pitch is vertical AI agents that automate repetitive winery tasks and answer questions about direct to consumer sales data. The site was mid rebuild when checked, no named customers, no HQ and no detail on the models or retrieval approach, so the AI claim is unverified beyond the marketing description.

name: Beverage360 (formerly HoochWare)
ai_use_case: demand forecasting inside an operations platform, no ml detail disclosed
short_description: Beverage360 is a cloud operations platform for craft beverage producers, serving distilleries, breweries and wineries with inventory, warehouse, production, order fulfilment and automated TTB compliance reporting. It claims over 300 producers on the platform. The site lists analytics and forecasting for demand planning but discloses no model, method or machine learning detail, so treat it as reporting and planning software rather than a proven AI product. The product grew out of the HoochWare distillery software line.

name: Cofficient
ai_use_case: resold netsuite cash flow forecasting and finance ai
key_people: Paul Tindal (Director), Paul Grant (Director), Ben Hille (CTO)
short_description: Cofficient is a Glasgow based Oracle NetSuite implementation partner that has built a Distillery Management Software layer on NetSuite for Scotch whisky producers, covering cask tracking, re-gauging, re-racking, wood and liquid association, blending, bottling and duty reporting. Its AI content is resold NetSuite functionality, marketed as AI for CFOs and cash flow forecasting, not modelling that Cofficient built for distilling. It is a consultancy, so the beverage AI value here is delivery and domain configuration rather than original research.

name: Ezy Systems (EzyWine)
ai_use_case: none, winery erp with budgeting and forecasting reports
short_description: Ezy Systems, established in 1993 in regional Victoria, sells an all in one winery management system covering vineyard, winemaking, bottling, stock, sales and finance, marketed as farm to consumer. The site offers budgeting, forecasting and sales analysis reporting but makes no AI or machine learning claim. The company was acquired by Jonas Software, part of Constellation Software.

name: BrooDoo (Top Bev)
ai_use_case: none, brewery production tracking and keg management
short_description: BrooDoo is brewery management software from Top Bev Limited in New Zealand, priced per litre produced. It records brews, transfers, packaging events, sales and shipments, gives full product traceability and files one click New Zealand Customs excise submissions, with accounting and POS integrations to Xero, MYOB and Vend. A sister product, BrooDoo Kegs, handles keg tracking. There is no AI or machine learning claim; the listed demand planning is conventional scheduling.

name: BrewLedger
ai_use_case: none, brewery operations ledger
short_description: BrewLedger is a mobile first brewery operations platform built around an immutable, append only inventory ledger, covering production, inventory, TTB compliance and taproom workflows with QuickBooks integration at a flat monthly price. It was founded in 2025 by John Jusko under the StoreGuard LLC holding company in Ohio, and also publishes an MIT licensed self hosted version. The company makes no AI claim; its own 2026 comparison article notes that none of the six brewery platforms it compares advertise AI.

name: BevTrack (Taps + Tables)
ai_use_case: none, brewery field sales crm
short_description: BevTrack is brewery sales and distribution tracking software from Taps + Tables, a web firm operating out of Charleston and Nashville. Reps log account visits in about 30 seconds, record orders, plan routes and report against manually set targets across self distribution and wholesaler markets. Pricing starts at 95 dollars a month. The site makes no AI or predictive claim, so it is plain field sales data capture and reporting.

name: Ground Signal
ai_use_case: nlp menu reading and on-premise account intelligence
short_description: Ground Signal measures the US on-premise channel for beverage alcohol suppliers, distributors and retailers, tracking brand and cocktail placements across more than 150,000 bar and restaurant accounts. Its Signal.AI product uses natural language processing on menu text to classify drinks into a standard cocktail catalog, so a menu item called Midnight Special is matched to Espresso Martini from its ingredient description. Machine learning is also used for account categorisation and venue profiling, and menu data is refreshed monthly. Coverage is strongest on spirits and cocktails, with beer and wine less prominent.

name: Aigora
ai_use_case: genai knowledge base and synthetic panels for sensory and consumer research
key_people: Dr John Ennis (CEO and Founder), Dr Vanessa Rios de Souza (Director of Client Solutions)
short_description: Aigora builds AI infrastructure for consumer insights and sensory science teams at large food and drink companies. Its named products are THEUS, a source-traceable knowledge layer over a company's historical research reports and study data, Forethought, which runs synthetic consumer panels grounded in that cited evidence to simulate product and claim decisions before fieldwork, and custom Decision Systems. The firm states it has published or presented work with Diageo, PepsiCo, Danone, General Mills, Symrise and DSM-Firmenich, which puts it directly on the drinks consumer-intelligence layer. Founded by Dr John Ennis, a mathematician working in sensory science.

name: Clarkston Consulting
ai_use_case: advisory on data, analytics and ai for wine, spirits and beer brands
short_description: Clarkston Consulting is a management and technology consultancy with a named Wine, Spirits and Beer industry practice alongside Data and Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Category Management and Trade Promotion service lines. It advises drinks producers on where AI is actually being used in the category, publishing analysis that places current wine and spirits AI adoption mainly in new product formulation and marketing rather than operations. Clarkston is an adviser and integrator, not a data owner or panel provider, and sells no AI product of its own.

name: Beverage Information Group
ai_use_case: beverage alcohol market data publishing and data analysis services
short_description: Beverage Information Group is a drinks industry data and media business operating under EPG Brand Acceleration, publishing Beverage Dynamics for off-premise retail, Beverage Wholesaler for distribution, Cheers for on-premise, and StateWays for control states. It sells data analysis services and market guides covering beer, wine and spirits across all three tiers. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site, and is included here because it is part of the drinks market-measurement landscape rather than because of any modelling capability.

name: National Beer Wholesalers Association (NBWA)
ai_use_case: forward-looking beer demand index from distributor purchase surveys
key_people: Lester Jones (Vice President of Analytics and Chief Economist)
short_description: NBWA is the US trade association for independent beer and beverage distributors and publishes the Beer Purchasers' Index, a monthly net-rising survey index of distributor beer purchasing built on the Purchasing Managers' Index model and segmented by beer category. The BPI is the only forward-looking industry indicator of expected beer demand one month ahead, and NBWA also releases Compiled Industry Data and Distributor Reported Data. This is survey-based statistical measurement with no machine learning claim.

name: Beer Institute
ai_use_case: us beer shipment and taxable removals statistics
short_description: The Beer Institute is the US national trade association for brewers, importers and supplier industries, and is the reference publisher of Key Beer Industry Statistics including monthly domestic taxable removals, import and export volumes, packaging mix and non-alcohol beer growth trends. Its estimates are the standard denominator that brewers and analysts use to size the US beer market alongside NIQ and Circana scanner data. It makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Distilled Spirits Council of the United States (DISCUS)
ai_use_case: us spirits volume, revenue and category market data
short_description: DISCUS is the US spirits industry trade association and publishes the sector's primary market data set, including State Spirits Data, Spirit Data by Category, distilled spirits import and export data, US spirits tourism data and the Annual Economic Briefing that sets the reference volume and revenue numbers for American whiskey and other categories. It also runs DISCUS Academy education. The data is compiled and reported statistics, with no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Wine Australia
ai_use_case: wine export, production and market insight dashboards
short_description: Wine Australia is a Commonwealth Government statutory authority established under the Wine Australia Act 2013 that measures and publishes the Australian wine sector's market data. Its Market Insights function covers wine markets by region, Australian wine exports, grape and wine production, and a set of Market Insights dashboards and calculators used by producers and exporters, alongside the Wine Export Approval system. It also funds grape and wine research. The published tools are reporting and analytics rather than machine learning.

name: Cesky svaz pivovaru a sladoven (Czech Beer and Malt Association)
ai_use_case: czech beer production, consumption and export statistics
short_description: The Czech Beer and Malt Association is the national body for Czech breweries and maltings, with contributing members drawn from hop growers, glass and label makers and brewing equipment suppliers. It compiles and publishes the reference statistics for the Czech beer market, including annual per-capita consumption, domestic production and export volumes, and runs consumer surveys on segments such as non-alcoholic beer. Its 2026 releases reported Czech beer consumption falling to a record low and weakening exports, alongside continued growth in non-alcoholic beer. The current organisation dates from 1991 and continues professional brewing bodies founded in the second half of the 19th century. No AI or machine learning claim is made.

name: SCENTMATIC (KAORIUM for Sake & Wine)
ai_use_case: scent to language translation for sake and wine
short_description: Japanese scent technology company whose KAORIUM system converts aroma into language. The KAORIUM for Sake & Wine product is sold as a sommelier AI menu tool for sake breweries, restaurants and retailers, suggesting sake and wine by translating flavour and aroma into descriptive words for the customer. The company describes itself in its own schema markup as a sensory experience and AI company, founded 2019 by Toshiharu Kurisu. Beyond drinks it also sells KAORIUM into education, sport and retail.

name: REVORN Co., Ltd.
ai_use_case: ai olfactory sensing and aroma visualisation
short_description: Tokyo startup building its own odour sensing hardware plus a cloud AI platform that digitises smell, described on its site as smell times AI. In May 2025 it published what it calls a world first: visualising the aroma of the Japanese craft beer brand ISEKADO with its AI olfactory sensor. It holds patents on an odour database that links nouns, adjectives and scent data, and its aroma work is listed on the Japanese sake business landscape map under the name Koudo. Leadership includes several former Japan Tobacco flavour and sensory scientists.

name: RATOC Systems (Moromi Diary Cloud)
ai_use_case: sake fermentation temperature monitoring and record keeping
short_description: Osaka IoT vendor whose Moromi Diary Cloud is a sake brewing DX service used by more than 70 breweries. Sensors log tank temperature every ten minutes across the koji, yeast starter and mash stages, push alerts when temperature leaves range, plot BMD curves and original extract trends, and generate the reports required under the sake tax law. It integrates with Kyoto Electronics SD-700 and AT-710 and Anton Paar Alcolyzer analysers and with existing cooling equipment. The product makes no AI or machine learning claim: it is sensing, visualisation and reporting.

name: SLOKER Inc. (Hansan Brewery)
ai_use_case: ai process model and digital twin for traditional korean liquor
short_description: Korean brewing technology startup that built what Korean press describes as the country's first AI transformation brewery, in Hansan, Seocheon. Sensors collect temperature, Brix, dissolved oxygen, pressure, humidity, agitation and fermentation rate in real time, feeding a manufacturing operating system that predicts fermentation state, alcohol strength and process end point. The company says it pairs vision sensors with a digital twin to rehearse the process virtually and uses Bayesian optimisation to derive production settings. Its product is Hansan Sogokju, a 1,500 year old traditional Korean rice spirit, brewed with master brewer Na Jang-yeon.

name: iGulu (AlBrew Corp)
ai_use_case: automated brewing control with app and cloud recipe platform
short_description: Shanghai company selling smart all in one brewing machines together with recipe and ingredient kits, in two lines: Pro Brewing M and N series for restaurants, bars, hotels and event venues, and home units sold internationally as iGulu F1 and S1. Its own description of the product system is smart device plus multiple recipes plus an app cloud platform, with patents around the device structure, control system and brewing flow. Products were recognised at CES, CES Asia and IFA in 2017. No machine learning claim is made: the intelligence described is automated process control and app connectivity.

name: Damai Craft (Zhixi Information Technology)
ai_use_case: craft beer recipe and ingredient reference database
short_description: Chinese craft and homebrewing platform run by Henan Zhixi Information Technology, offering a recipe builder, a community feed and reference libraries for hops, malt, yeast and BJCP styles, delivered on the web and as a WeChat mini program. It is one of the few Chinese language beer data references of its kind. It makes no AI claim, and the site's own article feed has not been updated since 2022 although the databases and recipe tool remain live.

name: Advanced Sys-tek Limited
ai_use_case: brewery and distillery plant automation and reconciliation
short_description: Gujarat automation company, best known in oil and gas terminal automation and fiscal metering, that also sells automation for distilleries, breweries and bottling plants covering receipt, production and dispatch. The system captures real time process data from field sensors and transmitters, measures density, concentration and volume flow at inlet, intermediate and outlet points, and produces reconciliation, stock loss and quality assurance records with integration into track and trace and central remote monitoring. It also sells a Terminal Analytics software product. No AI or machine learning claim is made.

name: Cotmac Electronics
ai_use_case: brewery and distillery process automation and industrial software
short_description: Pune based factory and process automation integrator with a dedicated food processing team delivering brewery and distillery automation on the Siemens platform in India, alongside dairy, juice and carbonated drinks work. Its offer includes process automation, industrial software, Siemens software, machine vision and digitalisation consulting, and it describes IoT use across procurement, production and consumer insight. It is one of the larger Indian system integrators serving alcoholic beverage plants. No AI or machine learning product claim of its own.

name: SpectraA Technology Solutions Limited
ai_use_case: brewery process equipment engineering and lab supply
short_description: Bengaluru engineering company, incorporated in 2009 and converted to a public limited company in 2021, that designs, fabricates, installs and commissions plant for breweries, craft and microbreweries, distilleries, malt spirit and IMFL blending, and food and beverage plants, with operations in India and Singapore. A related arm supplies laboratory instruments, chemicals and glassware to those plants. It is an exhibitor at the Brews and Spirits Expo in Bengaluru. Its craft brewery page uses the phrase intelligent automation as marketing language; there is no machine learning claim on the site.

name: Prodeb Brewery Technology Belgium
ai_use_case: turnkey microbrewery and distillery equipment with process control
short_description: Bengaluru manufacturer of turnkey microbrewery, craft and commercial brewery, distillery and spirit blending plant, claiming more than 100 brewing systems installed worldwide and supplying pub breweries across India as well as Europe and the Americas. Its scope includes brewhouse, fermentation and bright beer tanks, control panels, CIP, yeast propagation and process control management systems, plus spirit and RTD blending and flavour injection lines for whisky, brandy, gin and rum. It exhibits at the Brews and Spirits Expo Bengaluru and at drink technology India. No AI claim.

name: Phytech
ai_use_case: ai based irrigation and vine stress recommendations
short_description: Phytech runs an IoT platform combining plant based sensors, in field irrigation hardware and satellite imagery, and states plainly that it delivers AI based agronomic recommendations that can be executed automatically. It is listed as a supplier in the Wine Industry Network directory and publishes vineyard case studies, including Gorton Drive Estates in the Swan Hill region of Victoria, Australia. The company reports over 1000 grower customers across wine grapes and other permanent crops. The AI is a recommendation engine over sensor and irrigation telemetry, not a claim about generative models.

name: Bonsai Robotics
ai_use_case: vision based autonomy for vineyard and orchard machinery
short_description: Bonsai Robotics builds what it calls AI first, vision based autonomy for off road agricultural equipment, sold both as OEM integrations and as its own Amiga machine line. The Bonsai Intelligence platform manages mixed autonomous fleets and the company describes advanced perception and embodied AI trained on more than a million acres of captured field data. It is listed in the Wine Industry Network supplier directory and its published work covers vineyards and permanent crop farms. Its own blog describes foundation models applied to agriculture.

name: VinterActive
ai_use_case: ai winery concierge agents for dtc marketing and service
short_description: VinterActive sells preference based direct to consumer marketing tools to wineries, including myWineClubApp, and now ships AI Marketing Agents. Its AI Winery Concierge is a branded conversational agent trained on the winery's own voice, running across web, mobile and social channels, priced from 299 dollars per month with Facebook, Instagram and voice add ons. The company was founded in 2002 and is listed in the Wine Industry Network supplier directory. The AI is a deployed conversational agent, not an in house model.

name: Corksy
ai_use_case: dtc wine commerce data with ai club retention analysis
short_description: Corksy is a direct to consumer platform for wineries covering ecommerce, website building, wine club and subscription management, point of sale, reservations and an analytics dashboard. It positions AI as a way to read the club, customer and shipping data wineries already hold, and ran a joint webinar with Sovos ShipCompliant in August 2026 on using AI to predict club joins, spot churn and analyse shipment deliverability. Corksy does not describe a specific machine learning model in its product pages, so treat the AI as applied analysis on its own data rather than a disclosed ML system.

name: WiseConn
ai_use_case: irrigation automation telemetry and ndvi imagery, no ai claim
short_description: WiseConn builds DropControl, a wireless monitoring and control platform for precision irrigation, with its own node hardware and an NDVI imagery analysis tool. It was founded in Chile in 2006 by Guillermo Valenzuela, Jose Ulloa, Luis Felipe Escobar and Cristobal Rivas, opened a Fresno office in 2015 and later added Mildura, Madrid and other locations, and reports around 500,000 acres monitored. It is listed in the Wine Industry Network supplier directory and publishes vineyard specific guidance on soil moisture and vine water status. WiseConn makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim; it is sensing, automation and reporting.

name: Azmera Consulting
ai_use_case: erp selection and implementation consulting, no ai claim
short_description: Azmera is a systems and process consultancy serving wineries, distilleries, breweries and agricultural businesses, covering ERP selection and implementation, IT program leadership and process improvement. Its main product line is Odoo by Azmera, with beverage specific extensions branded Odoo for Wine and Odoo for Spirits, and it also implements JD Edwards for larger grape to bottle operations. In August 2026 it announced an Odoo for Wine integration with InnoVint covering production lots, vessels, dry goods, custom crush billing and overhead allocation. Azmera makes no artificial intelligence claim; it is a system of record and consulting business.

name: PEMDAS Winery Solutions
ai_use_case: winery financial modelling and business consulting, no ai claim
short_description: PEMDAS Winery Solutions is a one person winery business consultancy run by Genevieve Rodgers, covering acquisition evaluation, profitability analysis and startup planning. The work is financial modelling and operational planning grounded in wine business benchmarks, sold alongside downloadable planning tools. It publishes analysis on climate volatility and harvest timing risk. There is no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim anywhere in the offering; it is included because winery financial and operational data modelling is part of the beverage data landscape.

name: RedChirp
ai_use_case: compliant two way business texting for wineries, no ai claim
short_description: RedChirp is a compliant two way business messaging platform aimed at regulated industries, with wineries named as a core segment alongside healthcare and financial services. Named winery customers on its own site include Judd's Hill, Cuvaison and Hess Persson Estates, and it has acquired Vimbibe. Pricing starts at 99 dollars per month and it integrates with existing winery web and commerce stacks, partnering with Corksy on winery messaging. RedChirp describes automation and workflow, not artificial intelligence, and makes no machine learning claim.

name: SGS Food Nexus (Foodakai and Digicomply)
ai_use_case: ai food safety and regulatory intelligence over global documents
short_description: SGS Food Nexus is the merged product of Foodakai, built by the Greek company Agroknow, and SGS Digicomply. It monitors global food safety incidents, recalls, regulatory changes and hazard data, with the site stating the data is processed by AI and reviewed by SGS experts. Bacardi, Heineken and AB InBev are named among its drinks industry clients. The site does not specify whether the AI is LLM based retrieval or classical text classification, so the mechanism should be treated as unverified.

name: Liquid Vision AI
ai_use_case: distributor depletion data cleanup and sales analytics
short_description: Liquid Vision AI, Inc. sells an AI sales analytics platform for beverage alcohol brands, including beer, that consolidates fragmented distributor and depletion reports into a single view. The company describes the product as turning fragmented distributor data into strategic intelligence, with a free trial and a self-serve signup. The public site is a client-rendered web app, so the only machine-readable company detail is the structured data it publishes: a New York City address at 500 8th Avenue and the parent entity Liquid Vision AI, Inc. No funding, team or customer detail is disclosed publicly, and the specific modelling technique behind the AI claim is not described.

name: Fobi AI
ai_use_case: liquor retail store level data exchange and forecasting
key_people: Rob Anson (CEO), David Nicholls (VP Liquor Beverage)
short_description: Fobi AI is a publicly listed Vancouver data and digital wallet company whose Fobi Data Exchange licenses real time, store level liquor retail data and industry performance analytics from the Canadian hospitality and private liquor channel. In April 2024 it signed a data licence agreement with Asahi Canada to power that brewer's analytics and insights in the private retail channel in Western Canada, delivering an automated dashboard with competitive landscape views, forecasting and demographic customer profiling. Fobi is not a beverage specialist: its wider business is mobile wallet passes and retail transaction analytics across many sectors, with beverage clients such as BevWorks Brands. The forecasting and profiling are the platform's own analytics, not a third party engine.

name: Craftable (FNBTech)
ai_use_case: invoice extraction and ranked purchasing actions for bar beverage programs
short_description: Craftable, operated by FNBTech, Inc., is a hospitality back office platform for purchasing, inventory, accounts payable and cost reporting, and it grew out of the Bevager beverage inventory product (bevager.com now redirects to the Craftable app). It serves bars, restaurants, hotels and casinos where beer, wine and spirits purchasing is the largest controllable cost. Named AI features are Invoice AI, which scans supplier invoices and extracts line items for three way matching, Operator AI, which issues daily ranked opportunities and suggested actions, and an in app assistant called Crafty that answers profitability questions against live data. The company reports over 10,000 operators and more than ten years of trading, so a founding date around 2014 or earlier, but does not publish a headquarters city or founding year.

name: Research Institute of Brewing and Malting (Vyzkumny ustav pivovarsky a sladarsky)
ai_use_case: none claimed; accredited brewing and malting analysis
short_description: The Research Institute of Brewing and Malting is the only Czech institute that has worked systematically on brewing and malting since the second half of the nineteenth century, with accredited laboratories in Prague and Brno. It runs analytical testing on cereals, hops, malt, wort, beer, water, metals, pesticides and contaminants, certifies brewery sensory assessors, supplies brewing yeast from a collection established in 1946, and is authorised to recommend varieties for the protected geographical indication Czech Beer. It publishes the open access peer reviewed journal Kvasny prumysl, which is indexed in Web of Science and DOAJ and is a primary reference source for Czech brewing method data. It makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is reference analytical and sensory data infrastructure, not a modelling vendor.

name: Hop Research Institute Zatec (Chmelarsky institut)
ai_use_case: none claimed; hop breeding, HPLC analysis and variety data
short_description: The Hop Research Institute in Zatec is owned by the Hop Growers Union of the Czech Republic and was established in 1950, succeeding a hop station from 1925, with research sites at Steknik near Zatec and Trsice near Olomouc. Its five departments cover hop genetics and breeding, chemical analysis, biotechnology, pest and disease protection and cultivation technique, and it is the breeding origin of the Czech aroma and bitter varieties used across the brewing supply chain. Commercial services include HPLC hop chemistry analysis, pesticide efficacy and fertiliser trials, cultivation consulting and brewing verification in an experimental brewery. It makes no AI or machine learning claim: it matters here as the source of Czech hop chemistry and variety reference data that brewing supply chain models depend on.

name: Craftpeak
ai_use_case: none claimed; direct to consumer beer commerce and membership clubs
short_description: Craftpeak builds websites, online stores and membership club software for craft breweries, covering online pre order, taproom pickup, local delivery and shipping. It was acquired by the taproom point of sale company Arryved in June 2022, and the stated aim was to merge the online and on premise customer identity into one omnichannel profile for a brewery. It remains a distinct product and domain for brewery direct to consumer route to market. Craftpeak makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site: it is a commerce and content platform, and the customer data it captures is the interesting part for the beer data landscape.

name: DigitalPour (Brewmium)
ai_use_case: none claimed; draft inventory and keg profitability analytics
short_description: DigitalPour, operated by Brewmium, LLC, runs draft inventory management, digital tap list displays and a consumer facing pocket beer menu app for breweries, taprooms, growler stations and beer bars. It integrates with point of sale systems so pours decrement keg inventory in real time and the menus and app update automatically, and it reports revenue and per keg profitability analytics plus automated happy hour pricing. There is no AI or machine learning claim on the site: the value is keg level draft consumption data, which is one of the few reliable on premise beer depletion signals. The company does not publish a headquarters city or founding year.

name: BeerMenus
ai_use_case: none claimed; beer availability catalogue and on premise menu marketing
short_description: BeerMenus, Inc. runs a consumer beer discovery service and a business product for bars, restaurants, bottle shops and breweries, comprising listed venue pages, digital TV tap menus and automatically generated print menus. The company reports 57,127 listed places, 449,021 catalogued beers and an audience of more than 7.3 million beer drinkers, which makes it one of the larger public catalogues of what beer is actually available where in the United States. It is route to market marketing infrastructure rather than an analytics vendor, and it makes no AI or machine learning claim. Headquarters and founding year are not published on the site.

name: Scotch Whisky Research Institute
ai_use_case: instrumental and sensory flavour analysis
short_description: SWRI is the research and technology organisation of the Scotch whisky industry, funded by member distillers who account for the majority of Scotch production by volume. Its five research programmes are sustainable raw materials, sustainable processes, optimised maturation, flavour management and consumer confidence, run from purpose built laboratories in Edinburgh and in member distilleries. Flavour management work centres on developing sensory methods and instrumental analyses, including gas chromatography olfactometry, to measure and control flavour as producers change processes for sustainability. The institute makes no artificial intelligence or machine learning claim on its public site; it is included here as the primary analytical chemistry and maturation science body for the category.

name: Scotch Whisky Association
ai_use_case: industry export and production statistics
short_description: The Scotch Whisky Association is the trade body for the Scotch whisky industry, with members representing over 95 percent of Scotch production across more than 2,500 brands. It publishes the category's reference statistics through its Facts and Figures programme, covering exports, distillery counts and market data used across the trade. Members include Diageo, Chivas Brothers, Edrington, William Grant and Sons, Whyte and Mackay and Suntory Global Spirits. The SWA makes no AI or machine learning claim; it is included because it is the authoritative public data source for Scotch whisky volumes and export values.

name: Whisky Hunter
ai_use_case: secondary market auction price intelligence
short_description: Whisky Hunter is a subscription market intelligence platform for the secondary whisky market, built on a database of auction results. As of 11 August 2026 the site reported 27 auction houses tracked, 5,392,761 past sale records and 5,993 lots live, with per bottle price history, average price trends and percentage change over multi year windows. Paid tiers add advanced market data and cask sales history, and the site exposes both a REST API and an MCP endpoint for programmatic access. It makes no machine learning claim; the product is statistical aggregation of auction and retail price data.

name: Whisky Returns
ai_use_case: bottle investment analytics and liquidity scoring
short_description: Whisky Returns publishes secondary market investment analytics for collectable whisky bottles, covering more than 740 whiskies with price history, annualised returns, all time highs and lows, estimated demand and a liquidity score indicating how easily a bottle resells. The site states that it uses data science on validated price sources and that its content is mostly generated by automated scripts rather than reviewed by humans. It is operated by Adattenger Kft, a Hungarian registered company, and also sells a video course on whisky investing. No specific machine learning model or algorithm is described.

name: Decant Index
ai_use_case: cask valuation and portfolio performance data
short_description: Decant Index, formerly Whisky Partners, is a London based whisky and wine cask investment marketplace with over 60,000 registered users and 2,350 recorded exits. Its platform side is the data product: per cask litres of alcohol, strength and cost per litre, regauge reports, comparable market pricing where available, and portfolio valuations with annualised IRR and total net return. Casks are held in HMRC approved bonded warehouses in Alloa, Scotland. The company describes no proprietary algorithm, index methodology or AI, and the published return figures are marketing claims rather than audited data.

name: BAXUS
hq_location: Woodland Park, New Jersey, United States
ai_use_case: collection pricing data and vaulted bottle authentication
short_description: BAXUS is a peer to peer marketplace for fine and rare spirits and wine where sellers ship bottles to a vault for review, then trade tokenised claims on them rather than shipping between buyers. Alongside the marketplace it runs a collection dashboard giving portfolio breakdown by category and current pricing data on held bottles. It is built on Solana and raised a $5M seed round led by Multicoin Capital with Solana Ventures, Narwhal Ventures and FJ Labs, announced May 2024. Founder and CEO Tzvi Wiesel is a former professional spirits trader. The public site makes no machine learning claim; the data offering is pricing aggregation over vaulted and traded inventory.

name: Moonshine University
ai_use_case: distillery consulting, analytical testing and sensory evaluation
short_description: Moonshine University is a Louisville based distilling education and consulting business serving spirits start ups and working distillers, run from a campus at 801 South 8th Street alongside beverage developer Flavorman. Beyond courses such as the 5-Day Distiller Course, it sells analytical testing, sensory evaluation, product development, consulting and regulatory and compliance advisory to distilleries, plus the Stave and Thief Society bourbon certification. Course topics include spirit maturation and distillery operations, taught by working master distillers. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; it is included as a spirits technical consulting and lab services provider in the beverage data landscape.

name: Escarpment Labs
ai_use_case: genome sequencing guided yeast strain development
short_description: Escarpment Labs propagates and sells brewing yeast cultures to craft brewers across Canada and the US, and runs its own strain development programme using yeast breeding, adaptive laboratory evolution and CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. Its published R and D method states that it collects whole genome sequencing data alongside aroma compound production and growth rate data, and uses that sequencing data and analytics to improve its predictions and strain pairings. This is genomics plus statistical analytics, not machine learning: the company makes no AI or ML claim anywhere on its site. It also sells brewery QC and cell counting services.

name: Biome Makers
ai_use_case: soil microbiome dna analysis with machine learning
key_people: Adrian Ferrero (CEO and Co-founder), Alberto Acedo (CSO and Co-founder)
short_description: Biome Makers sequences soil microbiome DNA and turns it into functional soil health scores through its BeCrop platform, which the company says combines advanced genomics, microbial network science and AI. Its own site states that BeCrop uses the soil microbiome DNA and machine learning to analyse not only which microbes are present but also their interactions among them, with the crop and ecosystem. It started in wine and still works heavily with vineyards: published vineyard work includes Bodegas Barbadillo defining a functional soil profile for its vineyards and Les Vignerons de Buzet measuring the agroforestry effect on vineyard soil microbiome, plus a Napa Valley grower case study. Serves growers, agronomists and input manufacturers across 170 plus crops.

name: Improvin'
ai_use_case: farm level barley supply chain emissions modelling
short_description: Improvin' builds farm level data infrastructure for agri-food supply chains: collecting, standardising and modelling grower data so processors can track sourcing and emissions. Its beverage relevance is the malting barley layer. Viking Malt is a named customer and runs the platform across more than 1200 European barley farmers, and Viking Malt describes it on its own site as an AI-driven platform for measuring and reducing the carbon footprint of its malting barley. Improvin's own site makes no explicit AI or machine learning claim, referring only to multi-source modeled data, so the AI framing here is the customer's word, not the vendor's.

name: Hop Products Australia
ai_use_case: molecular marker assisted hop breeding
short_description: Hop Products Australia is Australia's hop grower and breeder, part of the BarthHaas group, and the source of Galaxy, Enigma, Vic Secret, Ella, Eclipse and Topaz. Its breeding programme dates to the 1950s and is described on its own site as expert pairing of plants for desirable traits, with no AI, machine learning or genomic prediction claim. It does use molecular genetics: HPA reports adopting DArT (Diversity Arrays Technology) molecular markers, converted to PCR markers, to identify hop plant sex early in the growth cycle, work led by the Slovenian Institute of Hop Research and Brewing through an international hop industry DArT collaboration. Marker assisted selection, not modelling.

name: Diversity Arrays Technology
ai_use_case: genotyping and genomic selection for crop breeding
short_description: DArT is a genotyping service provider that describes itself as coupling modern genetic technologies with the power of big data analytics. It sells DNA extraction, sequencing, genetic mapping, QTL and GWAS association mapping, and genomic selection as a breeding service, backed by its own analysis software. Its beverage relevance is the ingredient breeding layer: DArT molecular markers were run through an international hop industry collaboration to determine sex phenotype in hop seedlings, adopted by Hop Products Australia, and the same platform is used across cereal breeding including barley. The company markets statistical genomics and data analytics rather than machine learning.

name: Charles Faram
ai_use_case: searchable hop variety knowledge database
short_description: Charles Faram is a UK hop merchant and breeder supplying brewers worldwide from bases in Worcester, Yakima, Ontario and Poland, and the source of Jester, Olicana, Harlequin, Godiva and Opus. It makes no AI or machine learning claim: its Hop Development Programme is described as conventional crossing of new world hops with British rootstocks, evaluated by an in house sensory panel and brewer trials, with no mention of DNA markers, genomic selection or predictive models. Its data asset is the Hop Oracle, a searchable knowledge database of brewing, historical and agronomic information across hop varieties. Included for the ingredient data landscape, not as an AI vendor.

name: Abstrax Tech
ai_use_case: analytical aroma fingerprinting of hop varieties
short_description: Abstrax Tech is a flavour and aroma chemistry company that launched an Abstrax Hops division supplying TTB approved hop derived natural flavours, dry hopping aids and hop extracts to brewers. Its technical claim is analytical, not computational: Terplytics and what it calls a 3D Metabolite Fingerprint, a per varietal record of naturally occurring terpene and aroma compounds built from GC analysis of fresh and kilned hops, plus molecular distillation and emulsion technology. It sells a product line branded AI Terp Effects, but no substantive machine learning method, training data or model is described anywhere for it, and the supporting study used a 30 person human sensory panel. Treat the AI here as a product name.

name: Aroxa (Cara Technology)
ai_use_case: sensory panel data management software
short_description: Aroxa, a trademark of Cara Technology Limited, supplies certified single compound flavour standards, taster training and blind coded proficiency schemes used by breweries and distilleries to calibrate tasting panels. Its software product SensCheck is a browser based sensory system that runs customisable online questionnaires, stores tasting data in place of paper forms and scores taster performance on flavour identification and scaling. There is no AI, machine learning or predictive analytics claim on the product pages. Included because it is where a large share of the industry's structured sensory data is actually captured.

name: Brewmation
ai_use_case: plc brewhouse and cellar control with remote access
short_description: Brewmation builds turnkey brew houses, distilling systems, cellar tanks and the control panels that run them, sold mainly to US craft breweries and small distilleries. Its advanced package is a PLC and touchscreen system offering temperature control and trending, pump and rake control, sparge control, kettle power control, recipe process parameter storage and remote access for monitoring a brew session or changing cellar tank setpoints. Cellar panels are modular 8 or 12 point units daisy chained over CAN bus, with a Remote Access Module sold as an upgrade. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is conventional PLC automation and data trending, and it matters here as a layer where craft brewing process data originates.

name: Premier Stainless Systems
ai_use_case: brewhouse and cellar automation panels with data trending
short_description: Premier Stainless Systems has supplied brewhouses, fermenters, brite tanks and keg washers to craft breweries since 2000 and sells a brewhouse and cellar automation line alongside the vessels. Its 16 and 32 zone automated cellar panels provide remote setpoint access and alarms, zone and glycol data trending, glycol header pressure and temperature alarming, automated step chilling and data entry for tank status and beer information. The brewhouse touchscreen upgrade uses an Allen Bradley CompactLogix PLC with a Beijer HMI and adds recipe storage for control setpoints and hop addition alerts, flow totalizers, alarm history with a troubleshooting guide and an Ewon WiFi module for remote access. No AI or machine learning is claimed anywhere in the offering; it is process control plus historised trend data.

name: Deutsche Beverage and Process
ai_use_case: brewery process automation and remote hmi monitoring
short_description: Deutsche Beverage and Process builds custom brewhouses from 2 to 100 barrels plus stills, mash houses, cellar tanks, CIP skids and blending equipment for breweries, distilleries and other beverage producers, and runs its own UL certified control panel shop. Its named automation features include hot and cold liquor tank auto-fill on hydrostatic level sensors, SPX blending valve automation for mash and sparge flow and temperature, lauter transfer automation, wort grant level control, auto knockout, grain handling automation on load cells and fermentation temperature gradient and lagering automation with logging and timer delays. Operators reach the HMI over VPN from a mobile device for remote monitoring, with moving parts locked out remotely for safety. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim; this is sensor driven sequence control and data logging.

name: Kothe Distilling Technologies
ai_use_case: potstill monitoring and remote control
short_description: Kothe Distilling Technologies is the Chicago based supplier and training arm for Kothe copper potstills, serving North American craft distilleries with stills, fermenters, mash tanks and a hands on distilling certificate course. Its automation package covers potstill monitoring and management through a computer interface and touchscreen, bundling the electronic valves, sensors, software and wiring, with RJ45 Ethernet for remote access to the still from another location. Options include density and flow measurement, email notification, advanced logging, regulated cooling and steam pressure preheat control. No AI or machine learning is claimed. The site notes that its German manufacturing partner Kothe Destillationstechnik GmbH is in a strategic restructuring while the Chicago entity continues independently.

name: Czech Brewery System
ai_use_case: microbrewery measurement and control systems
short_description: Czech Brewery System s.r.o. of Opava supplies complete microbrewery and small industrial brewery lines, plus cider production equipment, covering malt handling, wort brewing, fermentation, filtration, filling and support systems. Within the support systems it sells a named measure and control range: brewhouse automation for wort boiling and cooling, control systems for wort brew machines with automatic monitoring of the hot brewing process, temperature measurement and regulation for fermentation, maturation, storage and yeast tanks, and laboratory equipment for chemical analysis of beer. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim; it is a plant and instrumentation supplier and one of the few Czech Republic entries on this surface. Registered in the Czech business register under ICO 05783011 since February 2017.

name: DESTILA Brno
ai_use_case: brewhouse control panels with remote service access
short_description: DESTILA of Brno is a Czech manufacturer of breweries, restaurant microbreweries and filtration equipment for beer and wine, claiming more than 75 years of history and over 140 breweries commissioned. Its brewhouses ship with a control system that ranges from manual graphic panels to a touchscreen control panel at several levels of automation, up to fully automated brewhouse control, and its CIP and keg washing equipment run in automatic mode under the same panels. The company advertises quick service of the control system through remote access, which is the only connected element of the offer. No AI or machine learning claim is made anywhere. The current operating entity DESTILA Brno s.r.o. is registered under ICO 21751595 and the older DESTILA, s.r.o. is in liquidation.

name: Vaisala
ai_use_case: inline refractometry for wort, distillate and grape must
short_description: Vaisala sells the Polaris process refractometer and CO2 probes as inline instruments for brewing, distilling and winemaking, with dedicated application pages for wort and Plato measurement in the brewhouse, rum distillation, grape and wine process control, wine interface detection and CO2 monitoring during fermentation. In a published case, Nikka Whisky installed a Polaris refractometer at its Moji plant in 2020 to read alcohol concentration continuously at the still outlet during shochu production, replacing manual sampling and letting the plant automate the point at which distillation is terminated.
