This is measurement and control, not analytics: Vaisala makes no machine learning or predictive claim for these products, and the value proposition is a stable continuous signal where the brewery or distillery previously took discrete lab samples.

name: KROHNE
ai_use_case: flow and energy metering for brewing and distilling
short_description: KROHNE Messtechnik supplies flow, level and analysis instrumentation with a large published set of beverage-alcohol application reports: custody transfer filling of beer into kegs, flow measurement of bright beer at high CO2 content, PVPP beer stabilisation, volume flow and alcohol concentration on a whisky filling line, and energy balancing across brewing lines. Its named reference is the Krombacher Brewery Group in Kreuztal-Krombach, where KROHNE metered hot water, steam and compressed air so the brewery could attribute utility consumption to individual processes and control compressors against actual demand. KROHNE makes no machine learning claim for this work; it is the instrumentation layer that feeds a brewery energy and process historian.

name: Bruker
ai_use_case: nmr wine authentication against a reference database
short_description: Bruker sells Wine Profiling, an automated 1H-NMR method that combines high resolution spectroscopy with multivariate statistical chemometrics scored against a large reference database of authenticated wines. Wine-Profiling 4.0 verifies geographic origin down to appellation, grape variety in single varietal wines, vintage consistency and quality grade, flags atypical samples and water addition, and quantifies more than fifty compounds including the official OIV parameters, in about twenty minutes per sample with no NMR expertise required of the operator. The reference database was built with WinespinAnalytics, Eurofins Analytics France and Estacion Enologica de Haro, and the OIV incorporated the NMR method into its Compendium of International Methods of Analysis in 2021. Bruker also applies ESR spectroscopy to beer freshness and oxidation monitoring for breweries. The models are classical chemometrics rather than deep learning, and Bruker describes them that way.

name: Metrohm
ai_use_case: titration, ion chromatography and nir quality control for beer and wine
short_description: Metrohm builds analytical instruments for beverage quality control: titrators, ion chromatographs, pH meters, voltammetry analysers, the OMNIS NIR analyser and the 2060 TI process analyser for continuous online monitoring. Feldschloesschen Getraenke AG, the largest brewery in Switzerland, runs a Metrohm setup that combines ion chromatography and titration under the tiamo software to determine bitterness, citric acid, pH and alcohol in a single method, with external density and colour instruments folded into the same run. On the wine side Metrohm covers acidity, sulfur dioxide, alcohol and sugar, including NIR determination of ethanol during fermentation. It is a laboratory and process analytics vendor and makes no machine learning claim; the NIR work is conventional spectroscopic calibration.

name: Worximity
ai_use_case: real time oee and downtime analytics on beverage packaging lines
short_description: Worximity sells a real time production monitoring and OEE platform, the TileBoard, that instruments existing food and beverage lines and turns machine states into downtime, throughput and changeover analytics with continuous improvement consulting alongside it. Arterra Wines Canada deployed it at its Niagara Falls winery, its largest of three commercial sites, and reported packer line stoppages falling from 4,043 to 1,554 over four months, a 16 percent productivity gain, changeover time cut from eight hours to five, and about 358,000 dollars in annual savings. The Quebec microbrewery La Voie Maltee uses the same TileBoard on its canning line and reported a 14 percent drop in stops per hour and a 9 percent production rate improvement within two months. Worximity makes no machine learning claim: the product is descriptive line analytics and reporting, not prediction.

name: E Tech Group
ai_use_case: plc, scada and mes integration for wineries, distilleries and breweries
short_description: E Tech Group is a US automation systems integrator with a dedicated food and beverage practice split into Beverages and Breweries and a separate Wineries and Distilleries segment, delivering PLC, SCADA, MES, batch control and data historian work. Its published beverage-alcohol case studies name Boochcraft in Chula Vista, where it automated heating and cooling control with redundancy and doubled tank count from twenty to forty, and cover ISA-88 batch process work for a global spirits producer, automated Brix monitoring at a California winery using IO-Link masters over Modbus TCP, red fermentation and pump-over automation at California wineries, and winery wastewater SCADA. The firm advertises digital twins, simulation, AI and machine learning and IIoT among its capabilities, but none of the published beverage case studies implement a model; the delivered work is control and data infrastructure. E Tech absorbed Banks Integration Group, the Northern California integrator, which became E Tech Group in January 2023.

name: McEnery Automation
ai_use_case: brewery historian and mes standardisation
short_description: McEnery Automation is a CSIA member systems integrator whose brewing work is a named practice area rather than a sideline: its principals present at the Master Brewers Association conference and sponsor its events. Its published brewery projects are a research pilot brewery control system built on ControlLogix, FactoryTalk ViewSE and FactoryTalk Historian with recipe management for unlimited master recipes and a bridge into an existing Oracle MES, a packaging line automation project at a flagship brewery, and a brewing MES standard rolled out across eighteen North American sites of a global beverage producer. That MES standard runs FactoryTalk Historian with OSIsoft PI Asset Framework, Coresight, DataLink and the PI Integrator for Business Analytics over SQL Server, collecting more than 50,000 tags per site and feeding LineView OEE dashboards, statistical process control and PI Notifications for predictive maintenance alerts. The end customers are described only as major global brewers and are not named. There is no machine learning in the delivered stack.

name: ProMach
ai_use_case: packaging line integration and production line digital intelligence
short_description: ProMach is a packaging machinery group that sells into craft beer through its ProBrew and TechniBlend brands, covering brewhouse automation, carbonated filling with the ProFill and ProFill V can fillers, labelling, laser coding and end of line equipment. Named brewery customers include Narragansett Brewing and Flying Embers, the latter scaled to a canning line running 200 cans per minute. In September 2024 ProMach formed a dedicated Wine and Spirits Solutions Group pulling together Fogg, the newly acquired Italian wine filling maker MBF, Zalkin, P.E. Labellers, ID Technology, Zarpac, Statera and Sentry for bottle, small format and ready to drink work. The data element is ZPI, its Production Line Digital Intelligence systems for integrated lines; ProMach makes no machine learning claim for it, and the offering is line monitoring and integration rather than a model.

name: SACMI
ai_use_case: beverage packaging lines and container vision inspection
short_description: SACMI Imola is an Italian cooperative machinery group whose Food and Beverage and Closures divisions serve breweries and wineries, alongside a separate Control and Vision Systems business that inspects containers and closures. It bought the bankrupt oenology plant maker Defranceschi of Laives in August 2016 and combined it with its own bottling line expertise to sell turnkey wineries covering grape presses, destemmers, storage tanks and quality control equipment. Named beverage customers include Caviro, the largest wine producer in Italy, which quadrupled bag-in-box capacity over three years on SACMI monobloc fillers running 1,500 bags per hour with headroom to 2,500. SACMI also runs a US craft brewer partnership programme and exhibits at the Craft Brewers Conference, Unified Wine and Grape Symposium and China Brew Beverage. The published beverage material makes no machine learning claim.

name: Tetra Pak
ai_use_case: plant performance improvement programmes for beverage producers
short_description: Tetra Pak sells processing and carton packaging into wine and ready to drink spirits, with Tetra Prisma Aseptic and Tetra Brik Aseptic used for wine and the American brand buzzbox packing premium cocktails in 200 ml cartons. Its operational service line matters more to the data landscape than the packaging: Inbrew Beverages, one of the fastest growing alcohol producers in India, ran Tetra Pak Plant Perform as a long term performance agreement across four Indian plants and reported 98 percent mechanical efficiency, waste held under 0.5 percent and about 184,000 euro in annual savings. Plant Perform is structured performance analysis and a customised implementation plan against measured line data rather than a machine learning product, and Tetra Pak does not claim a model for it in this case.

name: Kegstar
ai_use_case: keg fleet pooling and tracking
short_description: Kegstar runs a shared stainless steel keg pool for brewers on a pay-per-fill basis, handling collection, cleaning, quality inspection and redistribution so brewers do not own a keg fleet. It is the international division of MicroStar Logistics, operating in the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Australia and New Zealand, and the combined MicroStar and Kegstar pool is stated at over 6 million kegs. Keg movements are managed through its TAP management platform. The company makes no machine learning or AI claim on its site; the platform is presented as tracking and fleet administration.

name: Authena
ai_use_case: iot unit level traceability and condition monitoring
short_description: Authena AG is a Swiss deep tech company providing gateway free, unit level supply chain traceability using NFC seals, IoT sensors and a blockchain record. For wine and spirits it seals individual bottles, records origin and ownership transfers, and logs shipping conditions including temperature, humidity and geolocation along the route. It supplied the technology for Brauerei Locher's Saentis Malt limited edition Swiss whisky, where each bottle carries a tamper evident NFC seal. The site states that AI is combined with IoT and blockchain but does not describe a specific machine learning model.

name: Selinko
ai_use_case: nfc digital product identity and track and trace
short_description: Selinko gives individual products a secure NFC based digital identity used for authentication, track and trace across the distribution network, grey market detection and consumer engagement. Wines and spirits are one of its core sectors, with a published case study for Burgundy producer Laurent Ponsot, and the company says over 40 luxury brands use it. It was founded in 2012 after its founder hit counterfeiting problems distributing his Tuscan wine estate in China, and was acquired by Japanese printing and security group TOPPAN in early 2024. No machine learning claim is made; the product is secure tagging plus a data platform.

name: Copper Peak Logistics
ai_use_case: dtc wine fulfillment and weather aware shipping
short_description: Copper Peak Logistics is a wine focused third party fulfillment provider with warehouses in Napa, California and St Louis, serving winery direct to consumer shipping, wine clubs and allocations. Its proprietary CopperLink platform handles order tracking, club and allocation scheduling, inventory, and weather and ship complete order management, with compliance filters and open API integration to ecommerce and compliance systems such as ShipCompliant. It released a rebuilt version of CopperLink built on the Infoplus WMS backbone. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; the intelligence is rules based order filtering and weather holds.

name: WineDirect Fulfillment
ai_use_case: dtc wine fulfillment and temperature protected packaging
short_description: WineDirect Fulfillment is the wine direct to consumer fulfillment and warehousing business that remained after the WineDirect software platform became Commerce7, and it is now Commerce7's preferred fulfillment partner. It runs a multi site national network including a Paso Robles facility, with a fulfillment portal for order and inventory management and integrations into winery ecommerce systems. Its logistics work is heavily temperature driven, including its EcoCool and CoolPack heat protection packaging and regional white glove final mile partnerships. No AI or machine learning capability is claimed.

name: Arrive55
ai_use_case: temperature controlled final mile wine delivery
short_description: Arrive55 is a fine wine cold chain carrier formed in 2024 by the merger of The Wine Mover and Vinum55 Logistics, providing white glove final mile delivery held at a constant 55F from winery gate to collector cellar. It serves wineries, auction houses and retailers, and acts as the climate controlled last mile layer for third party fulfillment providers including WineDirect Fulfillment. It states that pallets are monitored in real time during long haul and that chain of custody is temperature verified, which is the data product. No machine learning claim is made.

name: NextBillion.ai
ai_use_case: route optimization for beverage distributors
short_description: NextBillion.ai sells route optimization, distance matrix, driver assignment and truck navigation APIs, and markets a specific solution for alcohol and beverage distributors covering multi depot delivery, load optimization and dispatch planning. Its optimization engine is constraint based with more than 50 constraints and the company states its route optimization learns from a fleet's past performance. This is one of the few genuine machine learning entries on the beverage delivery and telematics side rather than pure tracking. It is a horizontal vendor, so beverage is one named vertical among several.

name: RAMP RFID
ai_use_case: rfid keg tracking
short_description: RAMP RFID is an RFID systems integrator covering returnable asset tracking, inventory tracking and automated vehicle identification, with food and beverage as a named industry. It delivers KegFlow, a keg tracking solution built for brewing that uses UHF RFID tags able to survive keg washing and sterilisation, plus reading stations on filling lines and portals at warehouse gates, so brewers can locate individual kegs at each supply chain stage. RAMP states KegFlow was developed by its partner Alizent and is used by brewers including Carlsberg and AB InBev. Alizent's own KegFlow site no longer resolves, so RAMP is the live channel for the product. The claim is algorithms and reporting over RFID reads, not machine learning.

name: Kisling Consulting (KCWEIN 365)
ai_use_case: winery erp, no ai claim
short_description: Kisling Consulting GmbH is a Heilbronn based Microsoft Dynamics partner that publishes KCWEIN 365, an industry ERP for wineries, cooperatives and wine distributors built on Dynamics 365 Business Central. The modules cover wine production, cellar operations, purchasing, quality and reporting for the German wine trade. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is a system of record and an ERP consulting practice, not analytics.

name: Information Power (Vinea)
ai_use_case: vineyard data capture and sensor analytics
short_description: Information Power Limited publishes Vinea, a web and mobile vineyard management platform sold to New Zealand grape growers, wine companies and vineyard labour contractors, and listed on Microsoft AppSource. It assembles crop, viticultural practice, terroir, place and weather data so growers can monitor yield, quality and production cost and make time critical intervention decisions, and it handles payroll, invoicing and compliance records for labour managers. The vendor describes sensor data analytics and a digital twin of the vineyard but makes no explicit machine learning or predictive model claim.

name: Bricklead (Primus-Wine)
ai_use_case: wine and spirits erp, no ai claim
short_description: Bricklead is a French Microsoft ISV in the Dimood Group that builds certified Dynamics 365 Business Central apps for food and beverage manufacturers, covering production, supply chain, quality, lot management and finance. On AppSource it publishes the Primus-Wine range (Primus-Wine, Primus-Gamma, Primus-BI, Primus-EDI, Primus-Intrastat, Primus-Web-Services), described by the publisher as the ERP for wine, alcohol and spirits on Business Central. Bricklead itself makes no proprietary AI claim: the only AI mentioned is Microsoft's own Business Central Copilot features.

name: Commedia (Wine AI)
ai_use_case: wine label image recognition
short_description: Commedia SRL is a Microsoft certified communication and ICT agency based in Lecce with offices in Matera and Milan, working on web, SharePoint and Sitefinity development and digital transformation projects. It publishes Wine AI on Microsoft AppSource and the Azure Marketplace, described by the publisher as an artificial intelligence app that recognises wines from their labels. The AI claim appears only in the marketplace listing; Commedia's own website does not carry a Wine AI product page, so the model and its accuracy are unverified.

name: RITE Enterprises (Cloud Retailer)
ai_use_case: liquor retail pos and inventory forecasting
short_description: RITE Enterprises, Inc. of Sartell, Minnesota sells Cloud Retailer, a point of sale and inventory platform built for beer, wine and spirits retailers, and lists it on Microsoft AppSource as the Liquor Store Profit System. It handles sales, inventory, alcohol compliance tracking, loyalty, dual pricing, ecommerce integration and reporting, and the company says it has served alcoholic beverage retailers since 2004 and processed over one billion dollars of sales in the last twelve months. Demand forecasting is discussed in its own marketing but no machine learning model is claimed, so treat this as retail analytics rather than AI.

name: TryCatch Solutions (WT Manager)
ai_use_case: wine production management, no ai claim
short_description: TryCatch di Alex Bertini is a small Italian ICT firm doing cloud, custom application development and business intelligence work. It publishes WT Manager on Microsoft AppSource, a cloud platform the publisher describes as simplifying the wine production process for teams, alongside its SOMC sales management product. Neither the AppSource listing nor the company site makes any AI or machine learning claim.

name: UB Technology Innovations
ai_use_case: conversational analytics over spirits depletion and pricing data
short_description: UB Technology Innovations is a Microsoft Solutions Partner in Anaheim, California doing data, cloud and AI enablement work on Azure, Microsoft Fabric, Power Platform and Copilot. Its AppSource consulting offer, AI Conversational Commercial Analytics, is built on a delivered engagement for a multi brand spirits supplier where depletion, pricing and third party market data were unified in a cloud platform and exposed as plain English self service commercial insights. This is a services and Copilot style natural language layer over a beverage alcohol data estate rather than a packaged product.

name: Computronix (POSSE ABC)
ai_use_case: liquor licensing and compliance system of record, no ai claim
short_description: Computronix, founded in 1979 with offices in Edmonton and metro Denver, builds government workflow software for North American regulators and publishes POSSE ABC on Microsoft AppSource. POSSE ABC is the system of record for alcoholic beverage control agencies, managing liquor licensing, licensee self service, compliance and enforcement case management, and it sits alongside the broader POSSE PLS permitting and licensing platform. It makes no AI or machine learning claim, but it holds much of the regulatory data on breweries, distilleries and wineries in the US states that run it.

name: Budejovicky Budvar
ai_use_case: erp digital core and distribution route management
short_description: Budejovicky Budvar is the Czech national brewery, founded in 1895 and exporting to more than 70 countries. It replaced about a quarter of its legacy applications with SAP S/4HANA Cloud private edition, implemented by NTT DATA Business Solutions, and now runs more than 200 domestic and export distribution routes on the single system, reporting 22 percent higher finance team productivity and 99.7 percent IT availability. The brewery makes no machine learning claim: this is a system of record and reporting modernization, with SAP Extended Warehouse Management named as the next step.

name: CitySoft Consulting
ai_use_case: winery erp with ai document capture
short_description: CitySoft Consulting is an Australian SAP Business One and Sage partner that has packaged a dedicated winemaker solution on SAP Business One, covering blending rules, labelling, quality control, sampling, wastage, wine club management, wine tax tracking and capture of grape variety, vintage and region. The AI in the stack is bought in rather than built: Affinda document AI automates purchase to pay, and CitySoft resells Boyum B1 Usability Package AI and Nectari AI for SAP Business One reporting. CitySoft itself makes no proprietary machine learning claim for the wine solution.

name: McCoy & Partners
ai_use_case: sap s/4hana digital core for distilling
key_people: John Dineen (IT Solution Business Analyst Team Lead, Irish Distillers)
short_description: McCoy & Partners is a Dutch SAP consultancy with offices in Eindhoven, Utrecht, Madrid and Manila. It moved Irish Distillers Limited, the largest Irish whiskey distiller and a Pernod Ricard subsidiary behind Jameson, Redbreast and Midleton Very Rare, from SAP ECC and APO to SAP S/4HANA on Microsoft Azure using its Smart Re-Use method, in support of a stated ambition to grow from 12 to 20 million cases a year on the existing bottling plant through exception based processes and automation. No machine learning is claimed: the work is ERP transition, finance and supply chain planning.

name: Softwin Technologies
ai_use_case: distillery erp and production analytics
short_description: Softwin Technologies is an SAP Gold Partner based in Indore, India, that sells a packaged SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud offering for the distillery industry covering spirits production from raw material to finished goods, including fermentation and distillation stage tracking, bottling and packaging, excise and regulatory compliance, and real time inventory. It is a system of record and reporting play for Indian alcobev producers; the site claims advanced analytics and real time insight but names no machine learning model.

name: Zap (Zap Data Hub)
ai_use_case: erp data warehouse automation with analytics copilots
key_people: Max Smith (Data and Analytics Manager, Beavertown Brewery)
short_description: Zap builds a data warehouse automation and governed analytics platform for ERP data, with a supported connector for SAP Business One alongside Sage, Syspro and Dynamics. Beavertown Brewery, the London craft brewer, uses Zap Data Hub on top of SAP Business One to replace manual SQL and spreadsheet reporting across sales, supply chain and finance, and for specialist beer duty and traceability reporting. Zap AI is the vendor's own LLM layer, offering an analytics copilot, a modeling copilot and a natural language query experience called Talk Data To Me, which the company states is in active rollout.

name: Bestowal Systems and Services
ai_use_case: vineyard yield forecasting and winery supply planning
short_description: Bestowal Systems and Services is an Indian SAP supply chain consultancy specialising in SAP IBP, SAP Digital Manufacturing, SAP Analytics Cloud and BTP. In February 2026 it published a vineyard to bottle blueprint for vertically integrated wineries combining SAP IBP for grape yield forecasting and harvest planning, SAP Digital Manufacturing for fermentation, blending and bottling execution, and Industry 4.0 sensing via IoT soil and tank probes plus drone and satellite imagery, with AI models proposed for yield variation, vintage quality and optimal harvest window. It is presented as a solution architecture rather than a named live winery deployment, so treat the AI as designed, not proven in production.

name: BW Design Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim; plant engineering plus digital transformation and controls
short_description: BW Design Group is an engineering, architecture and construction firm whose Food and Beverage market page names Beer and Malt, Wine, Spirits and Soft Drinks as distinct practice areas. Alongside process and facility engineering it sells a Digital Transformation and Controls capability plus Operations Technology and operations consulting, covering the project lifecycle from strategy through commissioning. The firm makes no machine learning claim on these pages: the digital offering is described as controls and digital transformation, not analytics or AI. In 2026 it announced the acquisition of Malisko Engineering, an automation system integrator whose own publications cover unified namespace and on-premises LLMs for plant floor operators.

name: Hixson Architecture, Engineering and Interiors
ai_use_case: no ai claim; beverage plant design with controls and automation
short_description: Hixson is a design and engineering firm founded in 1948 that has specialised in food and beverage manufacturing plants for about 60 years. Its beverage practice lists alcohol and beer among the product types it designs for, alongside juices, soft drinks, dairy, coffee and tea, and its in-house disciplines include process engineering, controls and automation, industrial refrigeration and industrial wastewater. There is no AI or analytics claim anywhere in its published capability list; it is a plant design and controls firm, relevant to the beverage data landscape as the layer that specifies the control and instrumentation from which brewery data later comes.

name: CHARVAT Pacovske strojirny
ai_use_case: no ai claim; brewery and distillery process plant engineering
short_description: Pacovske strojirny, part of the SAFICHEM group, is a Czech engineering manufacturer in Pacov with a named brewing practice: it designs and builds brewhouse vessels, whirlpools and cellar equipment for microbreweries from 125 hectolitres a year up to industrial breweries of a million hectolitres, and also builds industrial and small distilleries. It offers assembly, trial operation, operator training and an emergency service line for breweries and refrigeration plant. The company makes no AI, analytics or software claim; it is included as a Czech process engineering supplier underneath the brewing data layer, in a country the radar barely covers.

name: Net Zero Now
ai_use_case: brewery carbon accounting and net zero reporting
short_description: Net Zero Now runs a sector-specific carbon accounting platform and has offered a dedicated brewery pathway since 2022, built with keg pooler Konvoy and Toast. Breweries enter operational, ingredient and packaging data and get Scope 1, 2 and 3 footprints, science-based targets and a reduction plan; named brewery users include Adnams and Renegade Brewery, and the platform integrates with the BrewMan brewery management system. It makes no machine learning claim: the site describes standard GHG Protocol calculation and reporting tools, not models. The company is now part of Ecologi.

name: Revida Water
ai_use_case: winery wastewater reuse as a service
short_description: Revida Water designs, builds and operates containerised onsite water reuse systems that turn winery process wastewater into irrigation, wash and in one verified case drinking water. It sells treatment on a per gallon subscription rather than selling equipment, and its reference deployment is the Teaching and Research Winery at UC Davis, where treated harvest wastewater was independently lab verified against US EPA drinking standards in 2025. It matters because more than 1,500 California wineries now fall under the state Winery General Order for effluent. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim; it is a treatment and operations business, not a data product.

name: Sustainable Wine Roundtable
ai_use_case: wine sustainability benchmarking and packaging data
short_description: The Sustainable Wine Roundtable is an independent global membership body, over 130 members across 25 countries, that builds shared sustainability measurement for wine. Its Global Reference Framework standardises what gets measured, its Sustainable Vineyard Practice Survey collects producer evidence, and its Bottle Weight Accord tracks and reduces average glass weight across signatories, now covering more than 2.5 billion bottles a year and an estimated 440,000 tonnes of CO2 mitigated. Members include Treasury Wine Estates, Systembolaget, Waitrose, The Wine Society, Naked Wines and Amorim. It makes no AI claim; this is standards, survey and benchmark data, not modelling.

name: The Porto Protocol
ai_use_case: shared climate solutions database for wine
key_people: Adrian Bridge (Founder, CEO of Taylor's Port and The Fladgate Partnership)
short_description: The Porto Protocol is a wine industry climate action network founded by Taylor's Port, with 252 members across 20 countries. Its core asset is the Solutions HUB, an open catalogue of 125 documented climate solutions, case studies and data covering water management, packaging, ecosystem restoration and mitigation across the wine value chain. Members include Jackson Family Wines, Catena Zapata, Spier, Salcheto, Amorim and Geisenheim University, and it signed a partnership with International Wineries for Climate Action in 2024. It makes no AI claim: the platform is a curated knowledge base, not a model.

name: California Sustainable Winegrowing Alliance
ai_use_case: winery sustainability self-assessment and certification data
short_description: CSWA is the nonprofit created in 2003 by Wine Institute and the California Association of Winegrape Growers to run the California Sustainable Winegrowing Program. It maintains the California Code of Sustainable Winegrowing, a self-assessment workbook that vineyards and wineries complete, and administers the Certified California Sustainable Winegrowing third party certification covering water, energy and greenhouse gas practice. It is one of the largest structured sustainability datasets in the wine industry. It makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: VIVA Sustainable Wine
ai_use_case: wine carbon and water footprint certification
short_description: VIVA is Italy's public sustainability standard for the wine sector, run by the Ministry of Environment and Energy Security with scientific support from the OPERA research centre at Universita Cattolica del Sacro Cuore. Producers are measured on four indicators: Air, which is a product and organisation carbon footprint calculated to ISO 14067 and ISO 14064-1, Water, based on evapotranspiration and water footprint methods, Vineyard, and Territory. Certified scope now covers 69,110 hectares and 5.4 million certified bottles. It is an LCA and certification scheme with no AI claim.

name: Sustainable Winegrowing New Zealand
ai_use_case: national winegrowing sustainability data collection and benchmarking
short_description: SWNZ is the national sustainability programme run by New Zealand Winegrowers, launched in 1995 and now certifying 98 percent of New Zealand's producing vineyard area and over 90 percent of wine produced. Members submit annual data online across six focus areas including water, waste, soil, plant protection and climate change, vineyard members also file a full spray diary, and independent auditors verify before certification renews. Energy, water and greenhouse gas scorecard records feed the New Zealand Sustainability Dashboard, which returns individualised benchmark reports matched on region, size, variety, climate and soil, plus regional and national reports. No AI claim; this is structured benchmarking, not modelling.

name: Peerox GmbH
ai_use_case: ai assistant for machine fault resolution
short_description: Peerox sells MADDOX, a self-learning assistance system for machine operators and maintenance staff in food and beverage production lines. The company describes MADDOX as a KI-based (AI-based) assistance system that connects to machine data so it can suggest fixes for the specific fault state a line is in, and it captures operator knowledge that would otherwise stay in notebooks and heads. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 under the digital solutions and MES categories. The AI is a recommendation and knowledge-retrieval layer over machine and incident data rather than a process control model.

name: INTRAVIS GmbH
ai_use_case: deep learning vision inspection of packaging
short_description: INTRAVIS builds vision inspection systems for plastic packaging, including the preforms, caps, closures, bottles and labels used by beverage producers, and lists food and beverage as its lead industry. Its software line (IntraVision, IntraVisualizer, IntraRecommender) includes a dedicated Artificial Intelligence offering, and the company states that deep learning algorithms boost its inspection systems for quality control, with tethered caps cited as an application. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 in the inspection and analysis category. The AI is applied to defect classification in images, not to the beverage process itself.

name: Softysol GmbH
ai_use_case: brewery process control and mes software
short_description: Softysol designs and implements process control (PCS) and manufacturing execution (MES) software for process industries, with brewing and beverage named as target industries covering malt, beer, kvass and spirits. Its portfolio includes Plant iT and brewmaxx alongside its own modules for CIP, lab and traceability, raw material intake, energy, OEE and recipe handling. It exhibited at BrauBeviale under software and IT solutions for production control. The company makes no machine learning or AI claim; this is a system of record and automation layer.

name: GRUEN GQM GmbH
ai_use_case: mes and quality management software for beverage producers
short_description: GRUEN GQM (written GRUEN GQM GmbH, part of the GRUEN Software Group) sells MES software specifically for the food and beverage industry, covering production planning, recipe management, production management, laboratory information management (LIMS), warehouse management, quality assurance and energy management. It states over 30 years in the beverage industry and more than 150 installations. It exhibited at BrauBeviale in the software and IT solutions categories. No AI or machine learning claim is made anywhere on the product pages; it is plain process and quality data software.

name: DFx Technology Ltd
ai_use_case: connected beer dispense monitoring
short_description: DFx Technology sells Intelligent Dispense hardware plus the DFx LiveView cloud platform, aimed at breweries, pub companies and dispense equipment OEMs. The platform lets an operator monitor an entire dispense estate in near real time, spot faults remotely, and extend line cleaning intervals through controlled keg-to-tap cooling, with claims of up to 84 percent less product waste and 25 percent better energy efficiency. It exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec. The company claims no machine learning; LiveView is telemetry, remote diagnostics and reporting.

name: Masitek Instruments Inc.
ai_use_case: instrumented container sensors for bottling line analytics
short_description: Masitek makes smart in-line sensor products (ShockQC, VerticalQC, PressureQC+Scuff) shaped like real containers that travel a filling line and record impact, pressure and scuffing so producers can find where breakage and damage originate. It runs dedicated beer, wine and alcohol and spirits industry lines and names Carlsberg, Heineken and O-I Glass among its customers, stating the top four breweries globally deploy its sensors. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 under digital solutions and inspection. The output is measurement and diagnostic analytics; no machine learning claim is made.

name: Maselli Misure S.p.A.
ai_use_case: inline and laboratory beverage analysers
short_description: Maselli Misure builds inline and laboratory analysers for the beverage industry, with product families dedicated to beer (Brix, alcohol, CO2 and oxygen analysers) and to wine (maturation, receiving area and fermentation process analysers), plus refractometers and spectrophotometers. It exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec under measurement data acquisition and IT solutions for production control. The company is a measurement instrument maker and makes no AI or machine learning claim; it matters here as a source of inline process data in beer and wine plants.

name: Peco InspX
ai_use_case: x-ray and fill level inspection of beverage containers
short_description: Peco InspX builds x-ray systems, fill level monitors and dud detectors for beverage and food packaging lines, with a dedicated beverage applications section covering empty and filled cans, glass containers, can seam defects and foreign material detection. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 under inspection, control and analysis. The site references detection algorithms but makes no machine learning or AI claim; it is inspection instrumentation generating per-container quality data.

name: DAUSCH Technologies GmbH
ai_use_case: inline beverage quality measurement with dashboarding
short_description: DAUSCH Technologies builds inline analysis systems for liquid production, including LiquiGuard Gen3, a LiquiGuard Gen3 variant with a Quality Dashboard, SyrupGuard Gen3 and a beer-specific BeerGuard unit. Its stated mission is raising product quality while saving raw materials, energy and time by optimising the process, under the slogan we analyse, you profit. It exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec under measurement data acquisition. No AI or machine learning claim is made; the data product is inline measurement plus a quality dashboard.

name: DirectSens GmbH
ai_use_case: enzymatic biosensors for sugars and fermentation products
short_description: DirectSens makes enzyme-based biosensor systems that measure sugars and fermentation products in food and beverage production, with named products for alcohol, glucose, and maltose plus glucose. The company develops and manufactures in Austria and also sells its LactaZyme and GlucoZyme enzymes into diagnostics. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 under laboratory analysis and inspection. There is no AI claim; it is analytical sensing hardware that produces fermentation measurement data.

name: Ruland Engineering & Consulting GmbH
ai_use_case: mes and process automation for beverage plants
short_description: Ruland Engineering & Consulting builds process plants for beverage and juice production and sells its own Ruland Process Management System (RPMS), a modular MES that controls, monitors and documents production, handling raw material management, tank farm and container management, and recipe handling. RPMS is the bridge between the plant PLCs and the customer ERP system. The company exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec under software and IT solutions for production control, and its consulting arm covers plant engineering and process technology. No AI or machine learning claim is made.

name: ALBERT FREY AG
ai_use_case: brewery and distillery process control software
short_description: Albert Frey AG is a German mid-size plant builder for breweries, soft drink plants and distilleries that also develops its own ALFlex automation software suite, with modules for machine and process control, trending, reporting, recipes, container handling, traceability (ALFlex Trace) and robotics. It also offers process control and laboratory analytics services and remote maintenance. It exhibited at both BrauBeviale and drinktec under software and IT solutions for production control. No AI or machine learning claim is made; ALFlex is process control and production data software.

name: ProcesTeh d.o.o.
ai_use_case: automation and mes software for filling lines
short_description: ProcesTeh is a Croatian automation house supplying software, electrical engineering, retrofits and filling plants to beverage producers, working with AutomationX and as part of the GAW Group. It exhibited at drinktec 2025 under automation and process control, digital solutions, and networking, control and MES solutions. Its own site gives little product detail beyond the software and retrofit service lines, and it makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: ORTEC
ai_use_case: route and load optimization for beer distribution
key_people: Mat Witte (Senior Vice President, ORTEC Americas)
short_description: ORTEC is a Dutch optimization software company that sells a purpose-built Beer and Beverage Distribution Solution Suite to US beer wholesalers, covering order management, route planning, truck load building, real-time execution monitoring and KPI analytics. Its 2025 Integrated Routing and Loading product is embedded inside SAP ERP and optimizes routes and load plans simultaneously. The company describes the underlying technology as mathematical optimization and advanced analytics with prescriptive planning and predictive ETAs informed by traffic, weather and resource availability, not as machine learning. ORTEC Americas is based in Atlanta and exhibits at the NBWA Annual Convention.

name: Descartes Systems Group
ai_use_case: route optimization and fleet analytics for beverage distributors
key_people: Matt Fannon (Director of Routing, Silver Eagle Distributors, customer quoted)
short_description: Descartes sells route planning, route execution, fleet performance management and EDI software, with a dedicated food and beverage distribution practice and named beer and beverage customers including Silver Eagle Distributors, one of the largest Anheuser-Busch distributors, Pepin Distributing, Mitchell Companies and Swinkels Family Brewers. Its published Silver Eagle case study is about closing the planned versus actual data gap across 180 trucks and five depots delivering roughly 36 million cases a year. Descartes markets a Fleet Analytics and AI module that it says uses artificial intelligence and analytics to improve planning and execution, but it does not describe the model or method on the beverage pages. It presented at the 2026 NBWA BIECC Innovation Showcase.

name: Symbotic
ai_use_case: robotic warehouse automation software for beverage distribution centres
short_description: Symbotic builds automated storage, retrieval and case-picking systems for distribution centres and describes itself as harnessing robotics and AI-powered software to simplify the flow of goods. It runs a food and beverage industry practice covering mixed perishable and shelf-stable case handling, dynamic inventory management balanced against sales velocity, and high-density storage for seasonal demand spikes. The food and beverage pages make no specific machine-learning claim beyond the company-level AI-powered software positioning. Symbotic presented at the 2026 NBWA BIECC Innovation Showcase for beer and beverage distributors and reports over 1,050 patents issued or pending and more than 1 billion dollars of R&D funded to date.

name: Westfalia Technologies
ai_use_case: warehouse execution software for beverage distribution
short_description: Westfalia Technologies designs and installs automated storage and retrieval systems and automated order picking for warehouses, with a dedicated beverage distribution industry practice and published case studies with Breakthru Beverage and Allied Beverage. Its software layer is Savanna.NET, a warehouse execution system that sequences and controls the automated equipment. Westfalia makes no machine learning or AI claim on its beverage or company pages, so it belongs in the beverage data landscape as an automation and execution system of record rather than an AI vendor. It exhibits at the 2026 NBWA Annual Convention and Product Showcase, booth 1000.

name: AeriTek
ai_use_case: iot telemetry on refrigerated beverage merchandisers
short_description: AeriTek is the North American refrigeration group behind the Imbera, Minus Forty, QBD, Torrey, Federal and Continental merchandiser brands, and sells refrigerated beverage coolers into beer and beverage distribution, convenience retail and unattended retail. Its SmartConnect platform connects Minus Forty merchandisers to a cloud dashboard tracking cabinet and evaporator temperature, door opening status and alarms, with remote lock and setpoint control and historical temperature reporting; SmartLock is a temperature-triggered health lock. The company also integrates Intuitivo APOP telemetry for large cooler fleets. AeriTek makes no machine learning claim: this is connected-asset telemetry and rules-based food safety monitoring, which matters to the beverage radar as a cold-chain data source at the point of sale. It exhibits at the 2026 NBWA show, booth 217.

name: Yellow Dog Software
ai_use_case: bar and beverage inventory back office, no ai claim
short_description: Yellow Dog Software sells back office inventory management for food and beverage, retail and concessions operations, and runs a dedicated Oracle Simphony and Oracle POS integration practice, including an Oracle sales rep referral page. For drinks it covers bar and wine inventory, bar top and wireless keg scales through its Barventory integration, recipe and pour costing, waste tracking and vendor EDI. The company describes itself as 100 percent inventory focused, privately owned by its founder and CEO with no investors and no debt. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site: this is a system of record and counting layer, not a modelling product.

name: Barventory
ai_use_case: connected keg and bottle scales for real time draught and liquor stock, no ai claim
short_description: Barventory builds connected weighing hardware and an app for bars and taprooms: a wireless keg scale that reports how much beer is left in a keg and how much has been poured, a bar top scale with barcode scanning that identifies a bottle and records its weight, and a Smart Coaster Pro. It was founded in 2018 by bar owners and operators to replace pen and paper liquor counts. The output is a live inventory and reordering list rather than a forecast, and the company makes no AI or machine learning claim. Its data feeds third party back office systems, and it is carried as the bar scale integration inside Yellow Dog Software, which sits alongside Oracle Simphony in hospitality sites.

name: Terillium
ai_use_case: oracle fusion demand and supply planning for beverage production and distribution
key_people: Warren Bach (CEO), Dave Woodworth (President), Shane Eisenhauer (VP, Fusion Cloud)
short_description: Terillium is an Oracle-only ERP consultancy of more than 250 consultants covering Oracle Fusion Cloud, JD Edwards and NetSuite. Its beverage work is documented in a published case study for Admiral Beverage, where it deployed Oracle Fusion Cloud Demand and Supply Planning against an existing JD Edwards platform using its own pre-built JDE to Fusion planning integration, to lift forecast accuracy and cut stockouts at distributor facilities. The forecasting is Oracle's planning engine, not Terillium software, and neither the case study nor the firm claims machine learning. Relevant as the consulting layer that actually puts statistical demand planning into drinks supply chains.

name: Redfaire
ai_use_case: oracle jd edwards and oci for brewery and distillery production, shelf life and distribution data
key_people: Brian McInerney (CEO and Co-founder), Barry Yelverton (CTO and Director of Product Development)
short_description: Redfaire is an Oracle JD Edwards and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure partner of roughly 180 people, headquartered in Limerick with UK and US offices, and a founding partner of the Redfaire International network. Its published beverage reference is Adnams, the Suffolk brewer and distiller, migrated from legacy System 21 to JD Edwards on OCI from 2019, unifying brewery, distillery, distribution centre, retail stores and hotels on one data set with automated beer shelf life expiry alerts and daily rather than weekly planning decisions. It serves a Beverages and Dairy segment inside its Food and CPG practice and markets an AI workshop and AI-driven JD Edwards insights via the eyko reporting tool, but the Adnams work itself involves no machine learning claim.

name: BirchStreet
ai_use_case: hospitality procure to pay and food and beverage inventory, ai claimed but unspecified
short_description: BirchStreet runs a hospitality procure-to-pay platform for hotels, casinos, clubs and food service, covering eProcurement, invoicing, recipe management, analytics and inventory. The inventory module explicitly covers beverage, using line-on-the-bottle scanning at outlets and POS-driven depletion to track bar stock. The former bar and liquor inventory brand AccuBar now resolves to this product: accubar.com redirects to birchstreetai.com/products/inventory-management. The company markets itself as AI-embedded and AI-powered but publishes no detail on what the models do, so the AI claim should be treated as unverified marketing language.

name: Vintegrate
ai_use_case: winery erp and direct to consumer system of record, no ai claim
short_description: Vintegrate is a winery-specific enterprise system built on Microsoft Dynamics NAV and .NET, sold as four modules: Vintegrate Winemaking for tracking and directing cellar processes, Back Office, Vintegrate 360 for direct-to-consumer covering POS, wine club, ecommerce and events, and a network security offering. It is a division of KLH Consulting and is run out of Sonoma County, California, so it sits outside the Oracle stack despite competing for the same winery ERP work. It makes no AI or machine learning claim: it is a system of record and the wine production and DTC data source underneath one.

name: Bizom (Mobisy Technologies)
ai_use_case: route-to-market retail execution intelligence
short_description: Bizom is an Indian route-to-market and retail intelligence platform for consumer goods brands, covering sales force automation, distributor management and retail ordering. Its own site names Heineken, AB InBev, Pernod Ricard, Coca-Cola and Red Bull among the brands it serves, making it a significant distribution-data layer for beer and spirits in India and 35 other markets. The AI is shipping product: Bizom Marshal conversation intelligence, an RI Copilot recommendation engine, image-based smart merchandising for shelf audits and generative-AI outlet deduplication. IndiaMART took a stake in the company in 2023.

name: AGRIVI
ai_use_case: vineyard farm management and AI advisory
short_description: AGRIVI is a Croatian digital agriculture company whose farm management software runs field operations, inputs, cost and traceability for enterprise farms. A Winery add-on extends it to vineyard blocks and cellar activity, giving per-variety cost per kg and per-vineyard ROI; Croatian producer Saints Hills, with vineyards in Istria and Dalmatia, uses it for field operations and cellar management. The AI claim sits in AGRIVI Engage, a white-labelled WhatsApp and Viber advisory agent for growers; the vineyard and cellar modules themselves are record keeping and analytics rather than machine learning.

name: Yalo
ai_use_case: conversational b2b ordering agents for beverage distribution
short_description: Yalo is a Mexico City conversational commerce company that puts B2B ordering for consumer goods brands inside WhatsApp, apps and voice calls, aimed at the traditional trade in Latin America and Asia. Its own site names Heineken and Coca-Cola FEMSA among customers, which places it directly in the beer route-to-market layer in Mexico and Brazil where small shops order by message rather than through a rep. The AI is a shipping sales agent called Oris that recommends SKUs and completes orders in chat, with Yalo publishing uplift figures on average ticket and SKUs per order. The company had raised about $75M as of its B Capital led round.

name: Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF)
ai_use_case: route-to-market sales force recommendations
short_description: Coca-Cola FEMSA is the largest Coca-Cola franchise bottler in the world by volume, running route-to-market across Mexico, Brazil and the rest of Latin America. Its Juntos+ B2B omnichannel platform reached 1.3 million monthly active users, and the company built Juntos+ Advisor on top of it, an AI tool for pre-sales agents that produces guided visit missions, personalised assortment recommendations and promotion prioritisation. Management describes the AI enablers as fully rolled out and scaled in Brazil and deployed across its four largest markets, with geoefficiency of visits rising to 96.5 percent in Mexico and 95.6 percent in Brazil. The models are Coca-Cola FEMSA's own build on its own transaction data, not a bought-in product.

name: xkzero (XMC)
ai_use_case: none
short_description: xkzero is an independent software publisher in Lincolnshire, Illinois whose XMC platform runs direct store delivery for wholesale distributors, including dedicated configurations for beer distribution, wine and spirits, energy drinks, coffee and water. It covers mobile route sales, delivery, proof of delivery, inventory and ERP integration, and names beverage distributors such as Power Distributing, Romano Beverage and Red Bull distributors among its customers. It makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site; it is a system of record for the DSD tier and matters to the beverage data landscape as a source of route and depletion data rather than as an AI vendor.

name: Orion Breweries
ai_use_case: no AI claim; brewery IT and business systems moved to cloud
short_description: Orion Breweries is Okinawa's brewer, founded in 1957 as Okinawa Beer Company and now the Orion Group, spanning beer production and sales plus hotel and tourism businesses. Its AWS customer story, published with AWS partner Ryucom, covers migrating on-premises internal business systems to AWS in about six months around a head office move, freeing IT staff from server rebuilds and hardware maintenance and hardening business continuity against typhoons. The evidence is an infrastructure migration only. Orion makes no machine learning or analytics claim in that story or on its own corporate site, so this is a beer operator in the cloud rather than an AI adopter.

name: Diver BI Group
ai_use_case: no ai claim, beverage alcohol bi and reporting
short_description: Diver BI Group is an international partner network of eight member firms that implements the Diver Platform business intelligence stack, with a dedicated beverage alcohol practice covering distributors and suppliers. Its drinks applications cover depletion and inventory sharing with suppliers, retail account level performance by premise type and brand, territory mapping and order fulfilment analysis. Named beverage alcohol case studies include Allied Beverage, Martignetti Companies, Lipman Brothers, Empire Merchants, Fedway Associates, Mutual Distribution and Southern Wines and Spirits. The company makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on its site: this is dashboards, reporting and data governance.

name: Treasury Wine Estates
ai_use_case: sales and demand forecasting, consumer trend agents
key_people: Kate Whitney (Chief Digital and Technology Officer)
short_description: Treasury Wine Estates is one of the largest listed wine groups in the world, owning Penfolds, Wolf Blass, 19 Crimes and Beringer. In June 2026 it made digital, data and AI a named pillar of its Ascent transformation, covering a single source of truth for reporting and scorecards, sales automation, promotion tracking and advanced forecasting, with about 100 million dollars a year of cost reduction targeted by FY29. It has also put AI into commercial decision making: two internal agents called Aivi and Viti interrogate trend data to flag varieties likely to come into fashion, and it deployed Complexica's What-if Simulator and Optimiser for territory mapping, call frequency and service level optimisation. The AI is partner-built but operated by TWE against its own sales and consumer data.

name: VineOps
ai_use_case: prescriptive depletion and distributor performance briefings
short_description: VineOps sells commercial intelligence to mid-market wine and spirits suppliers, importers and brand owners in the three-tier system. It automates collection, normalisation and reconciliation of depletion reports across dozens of distributors, then produces daily briefings, distributor scorecards, slow-moving SKU alerts and depletion allowance reconciliation. The AI claim is specific and prescriptive rather than a dashboard: plain-language recommendations naming an action, a reason and a deadline, delivered to the rep who has to act. Small vendor operating out of Oakling Systems, positioned explicitly against both generic BI and enterprise platforms.

name: DashBrew (KegMetrics)
ai_use_case: no ai claim, brewery production and keg fleet analytics
short_description: DashBrew is an independent product developer for the craft beer industry, founded in 2016 by former Microsoft engineer Greg Shaw, and builds KegMetrics. The product covers keg fleet tracking and workflow management plus analytics over batches, yields and throughput, and connects distributor data back to brewery output to show what is actually moving. It is pitched at craft, regional and production breweries and at cider, kombucha, RTD and non-alcoholic producers. DashBrew makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere: this is operator dashboards and reporting, deliberately positioned against generic BI tools.

name: TARGIT
ai_use_case: bi platform with an ai insights feature, winery kpi dashboards
short_description: TARGIT is a Danish business intelligence and analytics vendor, acquired by Forterro in 2025, that runs a named winery vertical: TARGIT for Wineries covers KPI dashboards from the vine through the tasting room to the consumer's cart. Its published winery reference is Hess Collection Winery, whose business analyst is quoted on moving from waiting for reports to discussing the data. The winery material itself is dashboards and reporting with no machine learning in it; the AI claim sits at platform level as TARGIT Insights, an AI-driven analytics capability in the Decision Suite, not as anything winery-specific.

name: Vineyard Vantage
ai_use_case: vineyard health and frost prediction, ai recommendations
short_description: Vineyard Vantage sells precision viticulture analytics to small and mid-size wineries, started in 2023 in partnership with Brix and Columns Winery in Virginia. It combines IoT sensors with real-time dashboards covering hyperlocal weather, frost prediction, leaf wetness, growing degree days and zone-level vineyard health. The company claims proprietary AI models and AI-powered recommendations on top of that sensor data, and also offers blockchain-stored vintage reports. It reports serving about a dozen vineyards across Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, so this is early commercial deployment rather than scale.

name: Small Batch Standard
ai_use_case: no ai claim, craft brewery financial benchmarking
short_description: Small Batch Standard is a financial agency built specifically for craft breweries, providing brewery bookkeeping, tax and financial consulting to over 100 breweries in the United States. Its data product is a Benchmarks Assessment that segments participating breweries by revenue band, from under 750 thousand dollars to over 10.1 million, and reports financial performance against peers. It matters to the beverage data landscape as one of the few sources of pooled craft brewery financial benchmarks, but it makes no AI or machine learning claim of any kind: this is accounting, reporting and peer comparison.

name: Trusty
ai_use_case: blockchain supply chain traceability with anomaly detection
short_description: Italian food and drink supply chain traceability platform, originally built by IBM Business Partner Apio and deployed with Var Group on the IBM Food Trust platform for producers such as Colli del Garda. It sells a wine and spirits module covering nutritional and ingredient labelling under EU Regulation 2021/2117, and reports work with more than 220 companies across 45 countries. It makes no machine learning claim: the platform is described as blockchain based and API integrated, with real time anomaly detection whose underlying method is not specified.

name: E. & J. Gallo Winery
ai_use_case: precision irrigation from satellite and sensor data
short_description: The largest family owned winery in the United States, founded in Modesto in 1933, with more than a dozen wineries in California and Washington and over 90 wine brands sold in more than 100 countries. It worked with IBM Research and irrigation maker Netafim on a precision irrigation trial at a Modesto vineyard that used satellite and weather data to water small vine blocks rather than ten acre plots, led on the IBM side by researcher Hendrik Hamann. It makes no current AI claim of its own: gallo.com describes water conservation experiments and ISO 14001 certification but no machine learning, and the IBM irrigation work is a decade old.

name: Epical
ai_use_case: maintenance data and reporting for brewing operations
short_description: Nordic data and asset management consultancy with more than 400 employees across nine offices, and the IBM Platinum Business Partner that delivered IBM Maximo Manage, Mobile and Scheduler to Swedish brewing group Spendrups Bryggeri across three breweries. It also built the business intelligence dashboards Spendrups uses to measure maintenance results from Maximo data. Its brewing work carries no AI claim: the AI services it advertises are for other clients, such as call classification and summarisation for Ropo.

name: Ollie
ai_use_case: brewery production and sales management software
short_description: Ollie is brewery management software for craft producers from 1 BBL to 20,000+ BBL, covering production planning, inventory, order fulfilment, TTB compliance reporting, QuickBooks integration and sales analytics. It is now part of Next Glass, alongside Ekos, Untappd and Oznr. Checked its own site and its Next Glass product page: Ollie makes no AI or machine learning claim, it is a system of record with reporting and dashboards.

name: Fermly
ai_use_case: subscription brewery QA/QC lab with a batch data platform
key_people: Frances Tietje-Wang (Founder, TTB certified brewing chemist), Danny Wang (Co-Founder, Information Architect)
short_description: Fermly is a TTB certified craft beer QA/QC laboratory that ships monthly subscription sample boxes and returns results into a cloud data portal, covering ABV, pH, dissolved oxygen, bitterness and microbial contamination. Its lab data feeds brewery management systems: it has an integration with Beer30 from The 5th Ingredient so lab metrics sit alongside production and cost data. Fermly makes no AI or machine learning claim; it is a testing service plus a data platform.

name: Thirstie
ai_use_case: direct to consumer alcohol e-commerce and fulfilment
short_description: Thirstie runs branded direct to consumer e-commerce storefronts and digital gift cards for beer, wine and spirits brands, routing orders through a network of licensed retailers to stay inside three tier rules. Republic National Distributing Company took a strategic stake in December 2022, and Thirstie was acquired by Cocktail Courier in 2024. The site advertises data capabilities on first party consumer purchase data but makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: DSDLink
ai_use_case: b2b beverage ordering between retailers, distributors and suppliers
short_description: DSDLink is a B2B e-commerce ordering app that lets on-premise and off-premise retailers place beer and beverage orders directly into their distributor's system, with separate hubs for retailers, distributors and suppliers. It is operated by Encompass Technologies and sits in the same category as Provi and BEES. The DSDLink site makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Brokreacja (Browar Brokreacja)
ai_use_case: announced ai based sales and personalisation model for craft beer
key_people: Mateusz Gorski (CEO, Brokreacja Sp. z o.o. and Bromarket Sp. z o.o.), Lukasz Gorski (CEO, Foothills S.A.)
short_description: Brokreacja is a Krakow craft brewery whose subsidiary Browar Brokreacja S.A. supplies craft and non alcoholic beer to Lidl, Kaufland and Carrefour in Poland. In August 2025 NewConnect listed Foothills S.A. signed a letter of intent to acquire Brokreacja Sp. z o.o. and Bromarket Sp. z o.o. and rename itself Brokreacja Holding S.A., with Bromarket building a brewery and distillery worth over PLN 20m net (PLN 14m net grant) that uses artificial intelligence in the sales process. Management describes the AI as a new sales model to personalise the offer; this is an announced project, not a shipped system, and the brewery's own website makes no AI claim.

name: Sennos (formerly Precision Fermentation)
ai_use_case: predictive fermentation monitoring and analytics
short_description: Sennos sells in tank fermentation sensors and the BrewIQ analytics platform to breweries, giving continuous readings on fermentation state so brewers can shorten tank turns and catch failures early. The company describes an AI and analytics engine trained on tens of thousands of real fermentations that converts live sensor data into predictive insight. Precision Fermentation rebranded as Sennos in March 2025, launched the M3 in tank sensor stack in April 2025 and raised $15m to expand beyond brewing into alternative proteins, biofuels and pharma. This is a refresh of an already tracked company, not a new one.

name: Munhowen
ai_use_case: beverage distribution with b2b and dtc e-commerce
short_description: Munhowen is Luxembourg's largest beverage distributor, a family company founded in 1908 and now part of Brasserie Nationale, serving horeca, grocery retail, sub distributors and office accounts from a 13,000 square metre warehouse in Ehlerange. It runs shop.munhowen.lu as a B2B ordering platform for horeca and distributors and drinx.lu as a consumer e-shop, plus Le Chai for wine. Its sites make no AI or machine learning claim; the digital layer is ordering and logistics, not analytics.

name: RaspberryPints
ai_use_case: taproom digital taplist and menu synchronisation
short_description: RaspberryPints is digital taplist and beer menu software for breweries, taprooms and bars, syncing TV displays, website embeds, QR codes and printable PDFs from one dashboard, with keg and inventory tracking, Untappd feeds and a public API for POS integrations. It grew out of a 2014 open source Raspberry Pi taplist project into a hosted SaaS with a free tier. It makes no AI or machine learning claim; FlowBox pour level hardware is listed as coming soon.

name: CSB-System
ai_use_case: ai agents for erp process automation and vision inspection
short_description: CSB-System SE is a German process-industry ERP vendor (over 550 staff, 50 countries) whose Food and Beverages line includes a dedicated beverage industry solution covering procurement, recipe optimisation against targets such as brix and Oechsle, production, quality management, traceability and multichannel sales. In August 2026 CSB launched its Agent Platform, specialised AI agents that analyse information, make rule-based decisions and prepare business processes, alongside CSB Vision for industrial image processing. The AI is general ERP and inspection automation across food and drink, not a beer, whiskey or wine specific model.

name: goerp.ai (Mawai Infotech)
ai_use_case: none
short_description: goerp.ai is the ERP suite of Mawai, an SAP Gold partner in Noida, India, established in 1998. It sells a dedicated alcohol and distillery edition covering sugarcane and ethanol inputs, master production scheduling, recipe and BOM management, quality control, brewing stage monitoring, regulatory compliance and supply chain for producers of spirits, ale and malt beverages. Despite the .ai domain the product pages describe only conventional ERP modules and dashboards; no machine learning capability is claimed for the drinks solution.

name: Liquor Logic
ai_use_case: none
short_description: Liquor Logic is a South African production and point of sale platform for breweries, distilleries, wineries and cideries, with separate editions for each and for bars and bottle stores. The brewery edition covers batch tracking, live fermentation monitoring, gravity readings, keg management, taproom POS and distribution routing; the distillery edition covers distillation runs, barrel ageing, bonded storage and excise reporting. Pricing starts at R549 per month with a 30 day trial. It is a system of record and makes no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on the site.

name: Brewfather (Warpkode AS)
ai_use_case: in app brewing assistant grounded in the brewer's own recipes, inventory and equipment
short_description: Brewfather is an all in one brewing app from Warpkode AS in Norway, covering recipe design, batch tracking, guided brew days, water chemistry and mash pH calculation, and live fermentation monitoring with Tilt hydrometer and other device integrations. It serves home brewers and small commercial brewers on web, iOS and Android. Its Premium Plus tier ships Brewfather AI, a conversational assistant built into the app and grounded in the user's own recipes, inventory and equipment profiles, metered at 500 AI credits per month, which can draft a recipe to a target style, gravity and hop bill.

name: BeerSmith
ai_use_case: none
short_description: BeerSmith is long running recipe formulation and brew session software for beer, mead, wine and cider, sold as BeerSmith 4 for Mac, PC and Linux plus a web version. It is aimed at home and small craft brewers and covers recipe design, ingredient and equipment profiles, mash and water calculations and brew day timers, with a companion Beer Recipe Cloud community recipe site at beersmithrecipes.com. The calculations are deterministic brewing formulas; the product makes no AI or machine learning claim.

name: Winerim
ai_use_case: wine list recommendation and margin optimisation
short_description: Winerim sells a cloud digital wine list for restaurants, hotels and wine bars in Spain. Its AI recommender analyses the diner's stated preferences, the dish chosen and the service context to suggest a wine from that venue's own list, alongside stock management, margin analytics and aggregated market intelligence. The company also publishes free diagnostic tools for wine list Pareto analysis and margin leakage.

name: Irokoo
ai_use_case: none, vineyard ERP on Odoo
short_description: Irokoo is a French Odoo Gold partner that packages Odoo as an all in one management system for wine estates, covering vineyard and cellar operations, traceability, French excise and duty filings (DRM, CRD, GAMMA/CIEL), direct sales, cellar door point of sale, wine tourism bookings and CRM. It also markets Odoo AI agent integration as a separate service line. Checked, and there is no machine learning claim in its wine product: it is a system of record built on Odoo.

name: Oenobiote
ai_use_case: none, rapid microbiology testing instruments
short_description: Oenobiote builds rapid microbiology instruments and test kits for the drinks industry, sold to producers, analysis laboratories and researchers. Its Chronos RT-qPCR thermocycler returns a result in about 20 minutes so a winery can run spoilage organism tests in house rather than outsourcing them, with a test range covering vineyard to bottle and separate lines for wine, beer and no and low alcohol drinks. Checked, and the company makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is analytical instrumentation that generates the data.

name: Vignee
ai_use_case: vineyard decision support from plot data and photos
short_description: Vignee is a modular French web and mobile app for wine growers covering work planning, plot mapping with growing degree day harvest estimates, plot level weather from five cross referenced models, cellar and vinification records with exportable DGDDI registers, stock and local intelligence. A paid Vision IA / Pilotage IA module, priced at 15 euros on top of the per hectare base, analyses the estate's vineyard data including plot photographs and returns prioritised attention points, positioned by the vendor as decision support that suggests and alerts rather than decides.

name: BIENESIS
ai_use_case: none, sensor triggered retractable vineyard canopy
short_description: BIENESIS, spun out of the Michelin Innovation Lab and working with the French wine trade since 2022, builds La Canopee, a retractable robotic canopy for vine rows. Two robotic arms unfold a six metre technical fabric over the vines in under a minute against spring frost, hail, sunburn, water stress and treatment washoff, then fold back into an A4 sized housing, driven by in-plot sensors and a mobile app and energy autonomous up to 80 km/h winds. The company said in June 2026 it had begun deploying more than 800 canopies across France and Italy under its Constellation 2026 programme, citing two seasons of Burgundy trials with company reported yield gains of 23 to 129 percent. Checked, and BIENESIS makes no AI or machine learning claim: the connected object is sensor and rule driven.

name: Consejo Regulador DOCa Rioja
ai_use_case: harvest yield forecasting across an appellation
short_description: The governing council of Spain's DOCa Rioja appellation has since 2022 been building its own predictive models over nearly 66,000 hectares of vineyard. It digitised more than 25 years of its own phenology and production records and combined them with topography, climate data, satellite multispectral imagery and field observations, then trained 170 candidate models on roughly 1,650 input variables and kept the best performers, reporting harvest estimate accuracy of 96 percent in parcels with detailed field data. Auxiliary models detect cover crops, missing vines, phenological stage and frost or hail damage, and the council has launched a Sistema Digital de Informacion Agroclimatica y Prediccion de la Cosecha app that puts the agroclimatic data, production prediction models and high resolution parcel cartography in growers' hands. This is an appellation body running the AI itself, not a vendor.

name: M&Wine
ai_use_case: mineral fingerprinting for authenticity and blending decisions
short_description: M&Wine measures and quantifies more than 40 mineral elements in a wine sample, from major minerals down to metallic ultra traces across eight orders of magnitude, and treats that multi mineral profile as a stable fingerprint of terroir and cellar practice. Its platform applies machine learning to a reference base the company states has passed 60,000 cuvees to predict grape variety, region, country and category, to build what it calls a Digital Wine Passport for authenticity, and to run IAssemblage, an AI blending assistant, plus DeepRed. The Jumeau Numerique du Vin platform took a silver medal at the SITEVI 2025 Innovation Awards in Montpellier.

name: Onafis
ai_use_case: predictive alerts on fermentation and ageing drift
short_description: Onafis sells continuous sensing and a cloud platform for tracking harvest, fermentation and ageing across wine, beer and spirits, removing manual dip readings and letting winemakers, brewers, distillers and consulting oenologists follow tanks and barrels remotely against their own recipes and alert thresholds. On top of the continuous data the company describes a predictive data intelligence layer that anticipates stuck or drifting fermentations and ageing so the operator can intervene early. Its Alkios connected alcoholmeter, which reads spirit strength in about 30 seconds in the container without drawing a sample and feeds the Onafis platform for customs inventory, took a bronze medal at the SITEVI 2025 Innovation Awards and is aimed at cognac, rum and whisky producers. It trades in France as My Bacchus.

name: CLEMENS Technologies
ai_use_case: camera vision post detection on vineyard pre-pruners
short_description: CLEMENS Technologies is a German maker of viticulture and orchard machinery: undervine weeding tools, tool carriers and lift masts, soil cultivation and canopy management equipment, plus vineyard management software. Its C-Vision double sided pre-pruner uses what the company calls an AI based camera opening system that recognises trellis posts of any type and opens the pruning head automatically, and which can be trained on new trellis configurations. The system won a silver medal at the SITEVI 2025 Innovation Awards in Montpellier.

name: TecnoVict (Spezia srl)
ai_use_case: none, sensor driven variable rate vineyard spraying
short_description: TecnoVict, part of Spezia srl, designs, sells and services vineyard machinery in Italy, including trimmers, tying machines, leaf removers, pre-pruners and post drivers, and distributes DICKEY-john products in Italy. Its IN.NO.VA.R. retrofit kit, a SITEVI 2025 Innovation Awards nominee, converts a fixed dose airblast sprayer into a real time variable dose machine by combining ultrasonic and optical canopy sensors with pulse width modulation to control each nozzle individually at 0.1 second resolution. Checked, and TecnoVict makes no AI or machine learning claim: this is sensor and control engineering for precision viticulture.

name: Ma-Cuvee (Studio Budo)
ai_use_case: generative imagery for wine and spirits packshots
short_description: Ma-Cuvee, run by Studio Budo, turns a single photograph of a wine or spirits bottle into premium marketing visuals using generative AI, described on its own site as creating professional wine bottle photos via IA with automatic generation of unique royalty free visual content. It is aimed at estates and drinks brands that need year round packshot and beautyshot imagery without repeated studio shoots, and is a member of the French La WineTech association.

name: Baqio
ai_use_case: none, wine and spirits commercial management software
short_description: Baqio is a French web based commercial management system built specifically for wine and alcohol producers, covering invoicing and shipping, customer CRM, stock and materials accounting with French monthly and customs declarations, bank synchronisation and pre accounting, cellar door point of sale and an e-commerce tie in to its own storefront or WooCommerce. It is NF525 certified and trades in France as Vinosoft. There is no AI or machine learning claim anywhere on the site: it is a system of record for winery commercial operations.
